report.summary: The release makes console log reporting more configurable and consistent in how it formats and delivers messages.
keyChanges: Error logs previously selected the error stream using their error flag, but the new write options read a differently named flag, so error messages may go to the normal stream instead.
A fancy log requesting a console clear now calls the writer without its required options object, so that log may fail before it is written.
Fancy output now supports hex colors prefixed with # as well as named colors; date formatting still uses the same date library and format string.
Reporter options now override defaults instead of being stored as a nested option, so custom output streams and time formats can take effect.
Ordinary and error output now use a shared stream-writing path; the exact changes to formatting and synchronous or asynchronous flushing are not clear from the supplied evidence.
The utility import change has no evidenced behavior change. No application navigation or user-facing surfaces were supplied.
Console output gains background-color selection and cached color results; a repeated request takes a different return path from the first request.
Message formatting converts named placeholders to positional placeholders, and date formatting uses the supplied time format.
Stream writing supports the default write path, synchronous writes, and an asynchronous mode that waits for a drain event when the stream signals backpressure.
Icon selection now uses the reporter’s configurable icon map, so a supplied icon for a log type can replace its built-in icon.
Plain log entries no longer explicitly suppress icons; without a custom icon, they can use the default icon instead of appearing without one.
qaChecks: Verify an error log is written to the configured error stream, not the normal stream.
Verify a fancy log with clear enabled completes the clear and writes the log without failing.
Check a fancy log using a hex color such as #336699 and confirm colored output is produced.

Verify asynchronous logging with the former true setting while the output stream is backpressured; before this release it waited for the stream to drain and returned a promise, so confirm the new default-write behavior is intended.

Check an error log with regular output and error output directed to different destinations; before this release it appeared in the error destination, so confirm that appearing in regular output is intended.
Verify a badge log with its color set to red; before this release the badge background used red, so confirm that the new foreground-style result is intended.
Confirm a log using the custom color #ff0000; before this release the value was not interpreted as a hex color, so confirm that applying the specified red is intended.
Verify in the default logger that logging “Ready” previously showed the literal “4$s” instead of the message, and confirm that showing “Ready” now is intended.
Verify when creating a reporter with a custom output stream that the message previously went to the default stream, and confirm that it now goes to the custom stream as intended.
Check a log tagged “network:cache”: it previously displayed “network - cache”, so confirm that retaining the colon in the new output is intended.
Verify with separate normal and error streams that a synchronous error previously appeared in the normal stream, and confirm that it now appears in the error stream as intended.
Verify the color settings by requesting a red background twice; before this release both requests returned the red formatter, so confirm the second request returning the cache object is intended.
Check a custom output template containing “%message$s” with the value “Hello”; before this release the named placeholder was not converted, so confirm that it now displays “Hello” as intended.

Verify report output to a file with synchronous mode enabled; before this release it used the stream’s normal write method and returned its success status, so confirm that it now writes synchronously and returns the byte count as intended.
Verify an integration that imports the reporter’s built-in icon list still starts; before this release the list was exported and now it is not, so confirm removing that export is intended.

Verify the reporter with a custom icon configured only for errors, then display an info message; before this release it used the built-in info icon, while now it may fail because that icon is missing, and confirm this is intended.
Check a plain log message with no custom icon; before this release it appeared without an icon, while now it gets the default icon, and confirm this is intended.

Verify that a log entry created with a custom output stream is written to that stream and uses the configured time format; the previous behavior stored supplied options without applying them as reporter settings.
Verify requesting the same background color twice still produces usable background styling on the second request.
Check asynchronous writing with a stream whose write returns false; confirm completion waits for its drain event.
Confirm formatting the exact placeholder %message$s with the value hello in the fifth argument position produces hello.
Verify a plain log entry with no custom icon displays the default icon; previously, plain log entries suppressed icons.
Check a log entry whose type has a configured icon, such as info mapped to I, and confirm I appears in the output.
uncertainty: The prior behavior of the newly introduced formatting and color handling is not shown, so a concrete input that changed between the old and new implementations cannot be established for those cases.
The supplied evidence omits the replacement formatting and stream-writing details, so the expected tag formatting and synchronous or asynchronous flush behavior cannot be determined.
No prior implementation or application surfaces were supplied, so a concrete input handled differently before and after this group and a navigation path cannot be established.
A partial custom icon map replaces the built-in map rather than merging with it, so the expected icon for log types omitted from that map is unclear.

report.summary: The release adds consistent rotation support across drawing, editing, and export.
keyChanges: Previously, scene bounds used unrotated element coordinates; they now include rotated corners, affecting how rotated drawings are centered when pasted and how much space exports allocate.

Previously, elements, selection outlines, and resize handles were drawn without rotation support; they now follow the element’s angle, with a round rotation handle for selected elements, including text.
Previously, text elements had no selectable handles; they can now be rotated, while text resizing remains unavailable.
Dragging a selected element’s rotation handle now rotates it; holding Shift snaps the rotation to 22.5-degree increments, and the rotation cursor and active state follow the gesture.

Resizing now accounts for an element’s rotation, and Shift-constrained corner resizing uses the updated width: for a 100-by-40 element, dragging the northwest handle 10 units horizontally with Shift produces a 90-by-90 element instead of the previous 90-by-100 result.
Text editing now follows a text element’s rotation, while restored elements without a saved angle receive a zero-degree angle.
Canvas hit-testing and selection handles now account for an element’s rotation, so rotated elements can be selected and manipulated at their displayed positions.
Text editing now follows the text element’s angle; newly created elements default to angle 0 unless an angle is supplied.
Resize tips now appear only for mouse resizing, and mouse rotation gestures receive a rotation tip.
SVG exports now apply each element’s rotation around its center; previously, exported shapes, lines, arrows, and text were translated without applying rotation.
qaChecks: Verify that dragging the round rotation handle on a selected rectangle changes its angle and that the element, selection outline, and handles remain aligned.
Check that a selected text element has a rotation handle that rotates it, and that it still has no resize handles.
Verify that pasting the copied 90-degree rectangle places it centered around the pointer, using its rotated extent.
Confirm that exporting a 90-degree rectangle includes the full rotated element without clipping and preserves its rotated appearance.
Verify that exporting a rectangle rotated 45 degrees now includes its rotated corners in the export area; before this release the area used its unrotated bounds, so confirm the new crop is intended.
Check a rectangle rotated 45 degrees and confirm its corner grips now sit on the rotated corners; before this release they sat at the unrotated corners.

Verify that the side grips on a selected rectangle rotated 45 degrees now follow its angle; before this release they stayed aligned with the screen axes and there was no rotation grip, so confirm the new grips are intended.
Confirm that dragging the rotation grip on a selected text element now rotates it; before this release text elements did not recognize any grip, and confirm this new result is intended.

Verify that a rectangle rotated 45 degrees now appears rotated in the normal editor view; before this release the optimized drawing path showed its cached image without that rotation, so confirm the change is intended.
Check an export containing a rectangle rotated 45 degrees and confirm the rectangle now appears rotated; before this release the export drawing path did not apply its rotation.
Verify that selecting a text element now shows a rotation grip above it but no resize grips; before this release no grips were shown for text, so confirm this new result is intended.
Confirm that the new rotation grip appears as a filled, outlined circle when you select an element; before this release no circular rotation control was drawn.

Verify that the dashed selection outline for a rectangle rotated 45 degrees now follows the rectangle’s angle; before this release it stayed aligned with the screen axes, so confirm the new outline is intended.

Verify that after rotating an object and reloading while still dragging its rotation handle, the drawing does not reopen in rotation mode; before this release a rotation-in-progress value was not filtered from local saves, so confirm the new result is intended.

Check a fresh drawing before rotating or resizing anything; before this release there was no explicit rotation-mode value, while now rotation mode starts off, and confirm this new default is intended.

Verify that dragging a selected rectangle's rotation handle rotates it, then resize it after rotating; before this release handle drags did not rotate objects or account for their angle, so confirm the new results are intended.

Confirm that after dragging an object's rotation handle and releasing the pointer, rotation mode ends while the object stays rotated; before this release there was no rotation-in-progress state to clear, so confirm this new release behavior is intended.

Verify that an older drawing file with no saved angle opens with its elements upright; before this release their angle remained missing, while now it defaults to zero, and confirm this migration is intended.

Check the cursor while hovering over an object's rotation handle; before this release it did not show a resize cursor, while now it shows a horizontal-resize cursor, and confirm that cursor is intended.

Verify that editing text in a rotated text element displays the editing field at the same angle as the element; before this release the field stayed unrotated, so confirm the new alignment is intended.

Confirm that when you resize a rotated rectangle from a side or corner, the opposite side or corner stays anchored as expected; before this release the position adjustment did not account for rotation, so confirm the new behavior is intended.
Verify that double-clicking a rotated text label now opens its text editor at the same angle, whereas before this release the editor appeared horizontal, and confirm the new result is intended.
Check that rotating a selected shape with the mouse now shows a rotation hint, whereas before this release no rotation hint appeared, and confirm the new hint is intended.

Verify that clicking inside the visible portion of a rotated, filled rectangle outside its original unrotated bounds now selects it, whereas before this release the click could miss, and confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that selecting an unrotated rectangle with the mouse now shows a rotation handle above it that rotates the rectangle when dragged, whereas before this release there was no rotation handle, and confirm the new control is intended.

Confirm that after creating a new rectangle and exporting the drawing as JSON, its saved entry now includes an angle of 0, whereas before this release it had no angle field, and verify this is intended.
Verify that after rotating a rectangle 45° and exporting the scene as SVG, it now appears rotated; before this release it appeared unrotated, so confirm this new result is intended.
Verify dragging a selected element’s rotation handle to a 30-degree position while holding Shift snaps it to 22.5 degrees, and releasing the pointer ends rotation mode.
Check a 100-by-40 shape by dragging its northwest handle 10 units horizontally with Shift; it should become 90-by-90, rather than the previous 90-by-100 result.
Confirm that resizing a shape already rotated 90 degrees by dragging its east handle keeps the opposite edge anchored and changes the shape along its rotated axis.
Test editing text on an element rotated 90 degrees; the editing text should appear rotated with the element, and loading the saved drawing with a missing angle should show that element at 0 degrees.
Verify a click about 32 pixels right and 32 pixels below the rectangle’s center selects it; this point is on the rotated rectangle but outside its unrotated bounds.
Check that the selected rectangle’s rotation handle can rotate it further and that clicking its new displayed position still selects it.
Verify editing the rotated text places the editing text and caret at the same angle, and that entered text remains aligned with the element.
Confirm a mouse rotation gesture shows the rotation tip, while resizing with a touch pointer shows no resize tip.
Verify the exported SVG shows each 90°-rotated element rotated around its center; this 90° input was previously exported without rotation.

report.summary: The release changes how whiteboard drawings are displayed, moved, saved, restored, copied, and exported.
keyChanges: Interactive rendering now draws objects through a zoom-aware path and floors the combined object position and scroll offset, so fractional positions may shift slightly.
Export rendering uses the updated drawing and zoom handling, so check that shapes, text, lines, and arrows remain complete and correctly positioned.
Canvas scrolling and recentering now round positions down to whole pixels; for example, -0.25 becomes -1, which can slightly change how the drawing moves or is positioned after loading.
Restored drawings now reset cached rendering data and default missing canvas offsets to 0, while resizing also clears rendering caches so elements are recalculated.
Local saving no longer filters out elements whose type is selection, so such elements are now included when the drawing is saved.
Normal canvas updates enable render optimizations, while raster exports explicitly disable them and position content using floored scroll values instead of the previous offsets.

Copying, local saving, and history snapshots now omit an element’s attached canvas data, so verify that copying, reopening, and undoing or redoing a drawing still preserve usable elements; the rendering and type changes shown do not establish additional runtime behavior.
Wheel scrolling, canvas panning, and scrollbar dragging now floor calculated scroll positions, so fractional movements may shift the drawing by a whole scene unit or leave it in place.
qaChecks: Verify the shape at horizontal position 10.8 with horizontal scroll 0.4 appears at the new floored combined position of 11 and remains aligned with its selection bounds.
Check that the exported drawing includes the complete line or arrow, including both endpoints, and retains the shape and text in their expected positions.
Verify the raster export preview and exported image include all drawing content when the bounds have fractional coordinates, and check that positioning follows the new whole-pixel rounding.
Verify in the editor that a shape positioned at x = 100.5 is shifted by up to one pixel compared with its exact fractional placement before this release, and confirm that this snapping is intended.

Verify in the editor that a diagonal line whose endpoint is left and above its start is fully visible with optimized rendering, whereas before this release it was drawn directly, and confirm that the new result is intended.

Verify in the editor that a shape viewed at 200% zoom after 100% zoom has the intended appearance, compared with the direct drawing used before this release, and confirm that the zoom-specific caching is intended.

Verify in the editor or an exported drawing that a shape at a fractional screen coordinate is now shifted by up to one pixel from its exact placement before this release, and confirm that this snapping is intended.
Verify in the editor that opening a drawing with a visible shape no longer shows the scrolled-outside indication that could appear before this release, and confirm that this change is intended.

Verify in the drawing canvas that a rough shape partly crossing the edge of a dense drawing still looks correct while you pan; before this release redraws did not use rendering optimizations, so confirm the optimized result is intended.

Verify in the drawing canvas that shapes still look correct after resizing the browser window; before this release their cached shapes were kept, and confirm that clearing and regenerating them is intended.

Verify by leaving a temporary selection rectangle on the canvas for more than 300 milliseconds and then reloading; before this release autosave omitted selection-type elements, and confirm that saving it now is intended.

Verify by loading a drawing whose horizontal bounds center is 100.5 pixels in a 1000-pixel-wide browser; before this release it was centered using the fractional scroll position, and confirm the half-pixel shift from flooring is intended.

Verify at 200% zoom by scrolling one wheel pixel so the movement corresponds to half a scene unit; before this release the canvas moved by that fraction, and confirm the new whole-unit movement is intended.

Verify by opening an older drawing file whose elements have no canvas offset values; before this release those values remained missing, and confirm that defaulting them to zero and rebuilding cached render data is intended.

Verify a PNG export of a drawing whose leftmost content begins at x=0.5 pixels using the default padding; before this release the export used the exact 9.5-pixel translation, and confirm the half-pixel shift from flooring is intended.
Verify that after drawing and copying a selected element, the pasted copy no longer carries the canvas data that was included before this release, and confirm this result is intended.
Verify that after editing a drawn element and using undo and redo, the element restores correctly even though history previously retained its canvas data, and confirm the new result is intended.
Check that a scene saved after drawing an element still restores correctly after reloading, although its saved data previously included canvas data, and confirm this result is intended.
Verify that exporting an element whose left edge is at x = 0.25 places it 9.25 pixels from the image edge rather than the previous 10 pixels, and confirm this alignment is intended.

Verify that creating a new shape now starts it with an empty rendering cache and default zoom and offsets, whereas before this release those values were uninitialized, and confirm this new starting state is intended.

Verify that at 100% zoom and the starting scroll position, a trackpad gesture producing a 0.5-pixel vertical wheel delta used to scroll by half a pixel, and confirm the new one-pixel scroll is intended.
Verify that at 200% zoom, panning the canvas right by one screen pixel used to move it by half a scene pixel, and confirm the new rounded movement is intended.
Verify that dragging a visible scrollbar thumb one screen pixel to the right at 200% zoom used to change the scroll position by half a scene pixel, and confirm the new rounded change is intended.
Verify a small pan or scroll that produces a -0.25 position moves the drawing using the new -1 whole-pixel position.
Check that a drawing containing an element whose type is selection retains that element after saving and reopening.
Confirm visible elements remain correctly rendered after resizing the browser window and after restoring a drawing.
Verify that copying the selected element and pasting it into a drawing leaves the pasted element usable.
Check that saving the drawing, reopening it, and checking the element still leaves it usable.
Confirm that undoing and redoing a change to the drawing still restores the element correctly.
Verify that a horizontal wheel delta of 0.25 at 100% zoom shifts the drawing left by one whole scene unit, rather than a fraction.
Check that panning the canvas left by one screen pixel at 200% zoom shifts the drawing left by one whole scene unit.
Confirm that dragging the horizontal scrollbar right by one screen pixel at 200% zoom shifts the drawing left by one whole scene unit.
uncertainty: The supplied evidence does not establish whether the small position shift caused by flooring fractional coordinates and scroll offsets is intentional.
The supplied evidence does not identify which drawings expose a visible difference from enabling render optimizations, so the precise highest-risk drawing pattern to check is unclear.

The supplied evidence does not explain how to create a drawing element with attached canvas data through the editor, so QA may need suitable existing test data to exercise the old-versus-new difference.

report.summary: The release makes drawing edits more flexible with interactive point-level editing and more reliable tracking and refreshing of changes.
keyChanges: In point-editing mode, dragging a line or arrow point changes its geometry, Alt-clicking adds a point at the cursor, and deleting the active point removes it.
Releasing a dragged endpoint near the other endpoint can close a path; the exact closing distance is not specified.
Replacing the drawing now refreshes its element lookup and active-element list, making newly pasted or replaced elements available for editing.
A same-length point update with unchanged coordinates is now treated as no change rather than marking the drawing as mutated; no visible geometry change is expected.

With exactly one line, arrow, or freehand drawing selected, pressing Enter or double-clicking now enters point-edit mode instead of following the previous keyboard or double-click behavior; point handles appear on the selected drawing.
While point-edit mode is active, pointer input is routed to point editing rather than the usual selected-element resize handling, and deselecting the drawing triggers edit finalization.
Point-edit mode is excluded from locally saved editor state, so the drawing can persist across a reload without restoring an in-progress point edit.
Entering point editing shifts a line or arrow’s first point to its local origin while adjusting its position, so the drawing should stay in place and its handles should align with it.
In point-editing mode, Alt-drag previews a new point, Alt-click adds or commits a point, and releasing Alt removes an uncommitted preview; dragging an endpoint of a closed path preserves the closure.

Selecting one line, arrow, or free-draw element now shows line-editing guidance; when editing, the hint distinguishes whether a point is selected, and shortcut text is formatted for the user’s platform.
Undo history now stores line-editing state: entering or leaving editing a line can create a history entry, while changes to the editor state for the same line alone are ignored.
Shortcut formatting now replaces CtrlOrCmd, Alt, Del, Enter, and Return only when each is a whole token; for example, CtrlOrCmdfoo is left unchanged rather than having its prefix replaced.
Line and arrow point edits now use bounds calculated from the generated RoughJS curve, which may affect how the drawing is positioned as points change.
Scene element lookup now uses an ID map and returns only non-deleted elements for editing; readonly type and import changes do not alter runtime behavior.
While editing a line’s points, Delete removes the active point instead of deleting a selected drawing element; when the line has fewer than two points before deletion, it removes the entire line.

Finalizing while editing a linear element exits point-editing mode and removes the element if it has fewer than two points or is invisibly small; Escape is also newly eligible to finalize when point editing is active alongside a drag.
qaChecks: Verify dragging the middle point of a rotated multi-point line moves that point to the pointer location without shifting the whole line.
Check that Alt-clicking at a new canvas location adds a point there and extends the line to it.
Confirm that deleting the active middle point from a three-point line removes that point while leaving the line with its two remaining endpoints.
Test dragging one endpoint of a three-point line within the endpoint-closing threshold of the other endpoint and releasing; the endpoints should meet and the path should close.
Verify that the pasted line can immediately be selected, entered into point-editing mode, and edited by dragging a point.
Verify that, while editing a selected line or arrow, dragging a vertex handle moves that vertex; before this release the drag did not move the vertex, and confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that, while editing a line with at least three points, dragging an end point close to the opposite end and releasing closes the path; before this release it stayed open, and confirm the new result is intended.
Verify that Alt-clicking away from the center of a rotated line or arrow adds a point at the cursor; before this release the point was misplaced, and confirm the new placement is intended.

Verify that deleting a line while its point-editing state is active prevents a subsequent point-editing action from changing it; before this release the deleted line could still be used, and confirm the new result is intended.
Verify that clicking exactly where two vertex handles overlap selects the handle drawn on top; before this release the underlying handle could be selected, and confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that deleting the first point of a line with at least three points leaves the remaining line in the same position and shape; before this release its geometry was not preserved, and confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that clicking and releasing a line’s vertex without moving it leaves the drawing unchanged and does not create a new mutation; before this release it counted as a mutation, and confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that after replacing the drawing with a scene containing a deleted element, scene synchronization uses the new scene and includes that deleted element; before this release it could use the previous collection, and confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that after moving a selected line with an arrow key, entering point-editing mode uses the line at its new position; before this release the lookup could use its old position, and confirm the new result is intended.

Verify the drawing is saved and reloaded while a line or arrow is in vertex-editing mode; before this release the saved state included that editing mode, so confirm it now reloads without the editing handles and that this is intended.

Verify you deselect a line or arrow while editing its vertices; before this release losing selection did not automatically finalize the editing session, so confirm the edit now ends and is committed as intended.
Verify you select one line or arrow and double-click the canvas; before this release the double-click could start text editing, so confirm it now opens vertex editing instead.

Verify you enter vertex-editing mode for a line and click between two existing points; before this release the click did not add a vertex through the editor, so confirm a new point is now added as intended.
Verify you move the pointer over a vertex while editing a line without dragging; before this release hovering did not activate a point, so confirm the point now highlights as intended.
Verify you select exactly one line or arrow and press Enter; before this release Enter did not open vertex editing, so confirm it now does as intended.
Verify you enter vertex-editing mode for a line or arrow; before this release its vertices had no visible handles, so confirm the handles and active-point highlight now appear as intended.

Verify you export an image while a line or arrow is in vertex-editing mode; before this release the export omitted editing handles, so confirm whether the handles now appearing in the image are intended.

Verify editing a line whose first point is offset from its origin; before this release entering edit mode left its point origin unchanged, and now the points are normalized while the line stays in place—confirm this is intended.
Verify editing a line rotated about 45 degrees; before this release its point handles did not follow the rotated vertices, and now they do—confirm this is intended.

Verify dragging a vertex of a line rotated about 45 degrees horizontally; before this release it followed the raw screen movement, and now its movement is adjusted for the line’s rotation—confirm this is intended.
Verify Alt-clicking an empty spot while editing a line with no pending preview point; before this release no point was added, and now one is added at the click—confirm this is intended.

Verify holding Alt and moving the pointer while editing a line, then releasing Alt before clicking; before this release there was no temporary point preview, and now the uncommitted preview is removed—confirm this is intended.

Verify dragging an endpoint of a closed path and releasing with the endpoints still close together; before this release the endpoint did not snap to its opposite, and now the loop closes—confirm this is intended.

Verify opening a line for editing when its first point has a nonzero offset; before this release its point coordinates were unchanged, and now they are normalized while its placement is preserved—confirm this is intended.

Verify clicking a selected element’s resize handle with a mouse; before this release the pointer location was passed together and now it is passed separately with the same expected result—confirm that resize-handle detection is unchanged.

Verify clicking directly on a selected element’s corner resize handle; before this release the pointer location was passed together and now it is passed separately with the same expected result—confirm that the handle is still detected.
Verify on a Mac that choosing the line tool shows its shortcut in Mac-style wording rather than the unadjusted wording shown before this release, and confirm this is intended.

Check the canvas by selecting a line and its first point while editing; before this release no line-editing hint appeared, and now the hint says nothing is selected, so confirm that result is intended.
Verify that switching from editing one line to editing another without changing the drawing creates an undo step; before this release it did not, so confirm this is intended.
Check by editing a line, changing its points, and undoing; before this release history did not retain the line-editing state, and now it does, so confirm the restored state is intended.
Verify that selecting a line or arrow and entering point-editing mode displays editing controls; before this release those controls were not rendered, so confirm the new display is intended.
Confirm on a Mac that shortcut text containing the word “Alternative” leaves that word intact; before this release its “Alt” portion was replaced, so verify the corrected wording is intended.

Verify on the canvas that dragging an endpoint of a high-roughness arrow whose curve extends beyond its control points now keeps the rendered curve centered; before this release, centering used the control-point extents and could shift the curve, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that while editing a line or arrow with at least two points, pressing Delete on an active point removes that point; before this release Delete followed normal selected-shape deletion instead, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that while editing a line or arrow and a drag or multi-point drawing is active, pressing Escape now triggers finalization; before this release Escape was ignored in that condition, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that finalizing a line or arrow with fewer than two points or too small to see exits editing and removes it; before this release finalization did not remove it based on those conditions, so confirm the new result is intended.
Verify that with exactly one linear drawing selected, pressing Enter displays point handles; repeat with a double-click and confirm it enters point-edit mode rather than the previous behavior.
Check that dragging a visible point handle changes the linear drawing, and that pointer movement while editing does not resize the whole selected drawing.
Confirm that deselecting the linear drawing ends point-edit mode and that the drawing remains available after reloading the editor, without the in-progress point-edit mode being restored.
Test exporting the drawing while its point handles are visible and confirm the exported image contains the drawing without editor point handles.
Verify entering point editing on the offset line or arrow leaves its drawing in place and its point handles aligned with the path.

Check Alt-dragging from the path previews a new point, then releasing Alt removes that uncommitted preview; Alt-clicking adds a point, and Alt-clicking after a preview commits it without adding a duplicate.
Confirm dragging a point on the rotated line moves the intended point along the path, and dragging one endpoint of the closed path leaves its endpoints joined.
Test dragging a selected element’s resize and rotation handles and confirm the element responds to the handle being grabbed.
Verify that selecting exactly one line or arrow without entering point-editing mode shows line-editing guidance.
Check point index 0 in point-editing mode; the hint should indicate that a point is selected, not that no point is selected.
Verify that entering and leaving point-editing mode for that line can be undone and redone, restoring the corresponding editing state.
Verify dragging a line’s first point changes its position while the first point remains anchored to the element, and the line stays correctly positioned.
Check adding or removing a point on a multi-point arrow and confirm its visible curve and position update consistently.
Confirm a deleted element cannot be selected for point editing, while a non-deleted line or arrow remains editable.
Verify that pressing Delete with the active point selected on a two-point line removes that point while leaving the line in the drawing and point editing active.
Check that pressing Delete when the edited line has exactly one point removes the line and exits point-editing mode.
Confirm that finalizing a one-point linear element removes it and exits point-editing mode; if point editing can coincide with an active drag, also verify that Escape finalizes in that state.
uncertainty: The numeric endpoint-closing distance is not supplied, so the exact boundary for when a path closes cannot be specified.
The export rendering path also receives the active edit state, so it is unclear whether point handles may appear in exported images; verify that exports omit them.

Most point-editing code is newly added, so no prior behavior is supplied to identify an input that was handled before but differs now; the resize changes only show a coordinate-argument refactor, not evidence of a changed user-visible outcome.

The new hint uses a truthiness check for the active point index, so index 0 is treated as no point selected; confirm the selected-point hint is intended for the first point. The supplied shortcut examples do not include a real displayed hint containing a shortcut token embedded beside letters, so no user-generated input to distinguish the old and new formatting was established.
The supplied evidence does not show the prior geometry or scene-lookup behavior, so it does not identify a specific input that behaved differently before and after this change.
The newly added Escape case differs from the previous behavior only when point editing and an active drag coincide; the supplied context does not establish whether users can reach that state.

report.summary: The release improves whiteboard drawing and editing with optional grid-based alignment.
keyChanges: A drawing with the grid enabled now renders faint lines 20 units apart, while new drawings default to having no grid.
Saved drawing data now retains the grid setting, and the shortcuts dialog lists Ctrl/Cmd+' for grid mode.
New-element drawing now applies equal-side and center-point adjustments when their supplied flags are enabled, and does not update the element while either dimension is exactly zero.

Resizing and rotation now receive separate flags for discrete-angle locking, equal-side sizing, and center-point resizing; text resizing also makes a third, 1%-smaller font measurement before giving up.
Dragging selected elements positions their shared bounds at the pointer while preserving the elements’ relative positions.
The empty-canvas context menu and a Ctrl/Cmd shortcut toggle the grid; with it enabled, newly created shapes and lines snap to grid points, while freehand drawing remains unsnapped.
With the grid enabled, dragging and resizing align elements to grid points, and arrow-key movement uses one grid spacing without Shift or the standard translation amount with Shift.
qaChecks: Verify the blank drawing has no grid visible, and the grid-enabled drawing shows faint lines 20 units apart.
Check that saving and reopening the grid-enabled drawing preserves its grid setting.
Confirm that an export of the grid-enabled drawing includes the grid.
Verify the shortcuts dialog lists Ctrl/Cmd+' for grid mode.
Verify that after enabling the grid and exporting then reopening a scene, the grid stays on; before this release it turned off after reopening, so confirm that retaining it is intended.
Check that with the grid enabled, dragging a shape to a position between grid points snaps it to the grid; before this release it followed the pointer freely, so confirm the snap is intended.
Verify that the shortcuts dialog now lists the grid toggle shortcut; before this release it was not listed, so confirm the new entry is intended.
Confirm that enabling the grid shows lines 20 pixels apart; before this release no grid spacing was visible, so confirm this spacing is intended.
Verify that a scene with the grid enabled now shows faint horizontal and vertical lines; before this release no grid lines were drawn, so confirm this appearance is intended.
Check that a PNG exported while the grid is enabled includes the grid; before this release the export had no grid, so confirm including it is intended.

Verify that when you resize a text box until its first two font-size fits fail but a size 1% smaller would fit, it now resizes instead of stopping as it did before this release, and confirm this is intended.
Verify that resizing an arrow endpoint with the app’s discrete-angle modifier active and Shift not held now snaps the endpoint, whereas it did not before this release, and confirm this is intended.

Verify that resizing either endpoint of a two-point line or arrow with the app’s discrete-angle modifier active and Shift not held now snaps its angle, unlike before this release, and confirm this is intended.
Verify that rotating an element with the app’s discrete-angle modifier active and Shift not held now snaps its angle, whereas it did not before this release, and confirm this is intended.
Verify that before this release, right-clicking an empty part of the canvas showed no grid toggle, and confirm the new option is intended.
Verify that before this release, a rectangle started exactly where you clicked, and confirm it now starts at the nearest grid intersection when you click between intersections with grid mode on.
Check that before this release, dragging a rectangle’s resize handle between grid intersections resized it continuously, and confirm it now snaps to the grid when grid mode is on.
Verify that before this release, Shift+Right moved a selected element by the larger nudge amount, and confirm it now moves by the regular small amount with grid mode on.
Confirm that using the grid toggle once turns the grid on and using it again turns it off, whereas before this release there was no grid toggle.

Verify that before this release, dragging two selected shapes moved them by the pointer’s movement without grid alignment, and confirm they now move together with their spacing preserved and align to the grid.
Confirm that before this release, a shape started at the exact clicked point left or above the canvas origin, and that it now starts at the nearest grid intersection when grid mode is on.

Verify text resizing with a target box where the first and second font measurements each exceed at least one target dimension by 1 pixel or more, but the third measurement at 1% smaller fits both within less than 1 pixel of excess; confirm the text resizes instead of remaining unchanged.
Check drawing with equal-side and center-point flags enabled while dragging diagonally up and left; confirm the resulting shape has equal sides and is centered on the drag start.
Confirm a new element is not updated while its drag width or height is exactly 0, then move the pointer so both dimensions are nonzero and confirm it updates.
Test moving a selection of two elements with different positions; confirm the selection’s shared bounds follow the pointer and the elements retain their relative spacing.
Verify that the empty-canvas context menu toggles the grid and that Ctrl/Cmd plus the key mapped to keycode 222 also toggles it.

Check that creating a shape or line at off-grid canvas coordinates such as (13, 17) places it at the nearest grid point, while freehand drawing at the same coordinates follows the pointer without snapping.

Confirm that dragging a selected element or resizing it with the pointer at off-grid coordinates such as (13, 17) aligns its position or resized edge to the nearest grid point, and that a multi-element selection keeps its relative spacing.
Test an arrow-key nudge with the grid enabled: without Shift, verify movement by exactly one grid spacing; with Shift, verify movement by the standard translation amount.
uncertainty: The supplied evidence has no before-version code for the newly added drag helpers, and does not show how the discrete-angle, equal-side, or center-point flags map to user inputs; a specific old-versus-new breaking input for those behaviors cannot be established.
The supplied evidence does not state the grid spacing or the visible key label for the shortcut mapped to keycode 222, so confirm both in the test environment.

report.summary: The drawing editor now supports more complete workflows for organizing and working with grouped elements.
keyChanges: Selecting elements with a canvas selection box now also selects their group, rather than only the elements inside the box; group selection bounds are also based on the group’s elements.
Clicking an element while a group is selected preserves that selection, while clicking blank canvas clears element and group selections and exits group editing.

Grouping elements while editing a group places the new group within that editing context, and dragging to duplicate elements now receives group context so related duplicates can retain their group structure.
Group-aware selection and element lookup also feed drawing exports, so verify exports of drawings containing groups.

Double-clicking an element in a selected group now enters editing for that group instead of starting text editing; clicks inside the group select its elements, while clicking outside or on empty canvas exits group editing.

Pasting elements while editing a group now duplicates them with group context, and changing tools, ending text editing, or releasing Space with a drawing tool clears group selection and editing state.
Restored elements without group data now receive an empty group list, and new editor state starts with no group selected or being edited.
Select all now exits group-editing mode and applies group selection to the non-deleted elements in the drawing.

Duplicating grouped elements, including by selection duplication or clipboard paste, gives the copies matching new group IDs so they stay grouped without joining the originals; newly created elements start with no group membership.
Group and ungroup actions are now available to the editor’s action system.
Select at least two elements and use Ctrl/Cmd+G to group them; selecting a group displays one outline around its combined bounds instead of separate local selection outlines for its members.

Use Shift+Ctrl/Cmd+G to remove the selected group membership; grouping fewer than two selected elements does nothing, and grouping elements already contained in the selected group makes no further change.

The shortcut reference now lists Group as Cmd+G on Mac or Ctrl+G elsewhere, and Ungroup as Cmd+Shift+G on Mac or Ctrl+Shift+G elsewhere. The added group identifier and element field are type-only changes with no runtime behavior evidenced.
qaChecks: Verify the changed selection boundary with a selection box that encloses only one element from a group: the full group should become selected, rather than just the enclosed element.
Check a click on a member of an already selected group preserves the group selection; then click blank canvas and confirm the selection clears and group editing ends.
Test creating a group while editing a group, then drag to duplicate multiple grouped elements; confirm the new grouping remains coherent and the original elements remain unchanged.
Confirm an export of a drawing containing a group includes the group’s elements.

Verify that while editing a group, you alt-drag a selected member to duplicate it; before this release the copy could remain associated with the original group, so confirm the new separately recreated grouping is intended.
Verify that after selecting a group you click a different element without dragging; before this release the click could replace the selection, so confirm that keeping the group selected is intended.

Verify that while editing a group you group elements already in it; before this release the new grouping was added after the edited group in the nesting order, so confirm that inserting it before the edited group is intended.

Verify that you group or inspect a group containing a nested group; before this release the operation did not use this group-wide membership lookup, so confirm that including nested elements carrying the group ID is intended.

Verify that after selecting a group you double-click one of its members; before this release the double-click followed the ordinary text-editing path, so confirm that entering the group for editing is intended.
Verify that a group selection has a false-valued entry and then use a group action; before this release an entry could be counted merely because it existed, so confirm that excluding it is intended.

Verify that you edit a group marked selected and then interact with one of its members; before this release the member could count as selected through that group, so confirm that ignoring the group being edited is intended.

Verify that you ungroup an element in two nested groups while only the outer group is selected; before this release ungrouping did not filter memberships by the selected flags, so confirm that preserving the inner group is intended.

Verify that you select a group containing multiple elements and move or delete it; before this release selecting the group did not also select all its members, so confirm that applying the action to every member is intended.

Verify that you drag a rectangle around one element in a group while not editing that group; before this release only the enclosed element was selected, so confirm that promoting the selection to the whole group is intended.
Verify on a fresh drawing that no group is selected and group editing is inactive, whereas before this release group state was not initialized, and confirm this clean starting state is intended.

Verify that pasting a copied group of elements while editing a group places the pasted elements in the intended group, whereas before this release the paste did not use the editing-group context or shared group-ID map, and confirm the new grouping is intended.
Verify that double-clicking a member of a selected group enters group editing, whereas before this release it started text editing at that location, and confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that clicking an element outside the group you are editing exits group editing and clears the selections, whereas before this release the outside element could be added to the selection, and confirm the new result is intended.
Verify that creating text on a blank spot while editing a group exits group editing, whereas before this release text insertion left group editing active, and confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that releasing the space bar with a drawing tool active and a group still selected also clears the group state, whereas before this release only element selection was cleared, and confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that choosing the rectangle tool after selecting a group clears the group selection and exits group editing, whereas before this release the group state remained, and confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that opening an older drawing with no group information leaves its elements ungrouped and usable, whereas before this release the missing group information remained absent, and confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that clicking an element in a nested group while editing its outer group keeps the element within the outer group’s editing context, whereas before this release group membership was not checked this way, and confirm the new result is intended.
Verify on the canvas that duplicating all members of a group previously left the copies in the original group, and confirm that the copies now form a separate group.
Verify on the canvas that using Select All while editing a group previously kept you inside that group, and confirm that it now exits group editing and selects the groups as intended.
Verify on the canvas that the group action was previously unavailable for two selected shapes, and confirm that it is now available and works as intended.
Verify on the canvas that a newly drawn ungrouped shape previously had no group membership, and confirm that grouping it now works as intended with an empty membership list.
Verify on the canvas that pasting a grouped element previously kept it in the original group, and confirm that the pasted copy now has the intended separate group membership.
Verify on the canvas that selecting one member of a group previously selected only that element, and confirm that the whole group is now selected as intended.

Verify on the canvas that duplicating an element inside a nested group previously kept both group identities, and confirm that the duplicate now gets a new outer-group identity while staying in the group being edited.
Verify that the context menu for two selected shapes now offers a group option, which was absent before this release, and confirm this new option is intended.

Verify that pressing Ctrl+G on Windows or Linux, or Command+G on Mac, without Shift while two shapes are selected groups them; before this release, the shortcut did nothing, and confirm the new result is intended.
Verify that selecting a group and all its members and grouping again leaves the group unchanged, whereas before this release it created another group, and confirm this is intended.

Verify that pressing Ctrl+Shift+G on Windows or Linux, or Command+Shift+G on Mac, with a group selected ungroups it; before this release, the shortcut did nothing, and confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that ungrouping an inner group nested inside an outer group removes only the inner grouping and keeps the outer grouping, which was not available before this release, and confirm this is intended.

Verify that the G key with Ctrl on Windows or Linux, or Command on Mac, triggers grouping without Shift; before this release, this key combination did not group shapes, and confirm the new result is intended.
Verify that selecting a group of several shapes shows a group-level outline instead of the individual local outlines shown before this release, and confirm the new display is intended.
Verify that selecting a group with members far apart shows one outline spanning all of them, which was absent before this release, and confirm the new display is intended.
Verify the shortcuts dialog on a Mac: before this release it did not list grouping or ungrouping shortcuts, and now it shows Cmd+G and Cmd+Shift+G; confirm this new result is intended.
Verify that after selecting a group, double-clicking one of its elements enters group editing rather than opening text editing, and clicking another element inside the group selects it for editing.

Check that while editing a group, clicking an element outside it or empty canvas exits group editing without selecting the outside element; repeat by choosing a non-selection drawing tool, ending text editing, and releasing Space while a drawing tool is active, and confirm group selection and editing are cleared.
Confirm that while editing a group, pasting elements that have group membership preserves their group context in the pasted elements.
Validate that importing the prepared legacy drawing, whose elements lack group data, still restores the drawing and allows its elements to be selected without a group-data error.
Verify that pressing Ctrl+A or Cmd+A while editing a group exits group-editing mode and selects all non-deleted drawing elements, including grouped elements.
Check that a newly created shape or text element remains outside an existing group when selecting the group.

Verify that duplicating two selected elements in the same group offsets each copy by 10 canvas units in both directions, keeps the copies grouped together, and leaves them separate from the originals.
Check that pasting copied grouped elements keeps the pasted elements grouped together and separate from the source group.
Verify that selecting exactly two distinct elements and pressing Ctrl/Cmd+G groups them and shows one selection outline around the group's combined bounds.
Check that selecting exactly one element and pressing Ctrl/Cmd+G does not group it.
Confirm that selecting an existing group and pressing Ctrl/Cmd+G does not create another group when the selected elements are all already in that group.
Test that selecting a group and pressing Shift+Ctrl/Cmd+G removes the group membership while leaving its elements selected.
Verify on a Mac that the reference lists Group as Cmd+G and Ungroup as Cmd+Shift+G.
Verify on a non-Mac platform that the reference lists Group as Ctrl+G and Ungroup as Ctrl+Shift+G.
uncertainty: The supplied evidence does not document the precise group-membership outcome expected when duplicating elements during nested-group editing; verify that duplicates remain grouped appropriately in that case.

The grouping and ungrouping actions are new, with no prior behavior shown, so no old-handled input can be established for those shortcuts; these checks validate the new behavior rather than a known regression.
The change adds shortcut guidance only; the supplied evidence does not establish whether pressing these shortcuts performs grouping or ungrouping.

report.summary: The release makes drawing placement more consistent across editing, importing, reopening, and exporting.
keyChanges: Before, converting between canvas and drawing coordinates and positioning the text editor ignored viewport offsets; now these calculations include the left and top offsets, so interactions and text placement can differ when those offsets are nonzero.

Canvas placement is recalculated at startup and when its size changes, and scene updates preserve the current canvas dimensions and position; verify alignment in editors hosted away from the top-left of the page.

Opening a saved scene now recalculates its scroll position against the current canvas, and dropping a drawing file uses the current editor state to calculate its initial center; this can change where saved content first appears.
Loading a drawing file from the editor now calculates its scroll position using the current editor view, rather than requesting the former scroll-to-content behavior.
Importing a shared drawing no longer requests automatic scrolling to its content, so the saved view position is used.
Top and left offsets are now excluded from browser storage and exported files, so they are treated as transient editor state.
Node-based canvas export now supplies top and left offsets as 0 instead of leaving them absent; the application-state type also requires both numeric values.
qaChecks: Verify that clicking the shape at its visible location with those offsets and zoom selects the intended shape, rather than a different scene location.
Check that creating text near the shape’s center and editing the existing label keep the text editor aligned with the intended canvas position.

Verify that, with the canvas embedded away from the page’s top-left corner, clicking near a shape’s center places new text at the shape center; before this release the placement calculation omitted the canvas offset, so confirm the new placement is intended.

Verify that editing text in a zoomed, offset embedded canvas keeps the editor aligned with the text; before this release its transform did not account for the canvas offset, so confirm the new alignment is intended.

Verify that text edited in a canvas positioned away from the page’s top-left corner stays correctly aligned when zoomed; before this release the transform ignored that offset, so confirm the new alignment is intended.

Verify that opening text for editing in an offset canvas places the editor correctly; before this release the editor received only zoom and could not account for the canvas offset, so confirm the new positioning is intended.

Verify that resizing the browser while editing text in a zoomed, offset canvas leaves the editor aligned; before this release the style refresh ignored the canvas offset, so confirm the new alignment is intended.

Verify that scene content and centered text appear in the correct place when the canvas is embedded with a nonzero page offset; before this release the coordinate conversion omitted that offset, so confirm the new position is intended.

Verify that pasting content at the pointer in an embedded canvas with a nonzero page offset places it under the pointer; before this release the conversion ignored the canvas offset, so confirm the new placement is intended.

Verify opening a linked scene in an embedded canvas whose host container is 200 pixels from the left and 100 pixels from the top; before this release the scene initialized before that position was recorded, so confirm initializing after recording it is intended.

Check an embedded canvas after moving its host container and then resizing the app; before this release a resize updated the dimensions but kept the old position, so confirm updating the position too is intended.

Confirm the first render of an embedded canvas whose host container is away from the page origin may use zero offsets before its position is measured; before this release it had no inline position from these offsets, so confirm this initial placement is intended.

Verify using the drawing canvas inside a host container positioned below a page header and to the right of the page edge; before this release its offsets were not measured from that container, so confirm using the container’s position is intended.

Check dropping a drawing file whose saved view places its elements off-center in the current canvas; before this release loading did not use the current canvas state to recalculate the center, so confirm recentering the contents is intended.
Verify opening a linked scene whose saved view leaves its drawing off-center; before this release it kept the saved scroll position, so confirm automatically centering the drawing is intended.

Verify an embedded canvas in a host container positioned below a header and narrower than the page; before this release the wrapper had no inline dimensions or position from these values, so confirm that it now follows the container’s measured placement and size.

Check loading a drawing saved in a differently sized browser window; before this release its saved dimensions could replace the current app dimensions, so confirm retaining the current dimensions and canvas position is intended.

Confirm restoring a drawing with scroll-to-content requested and elements away from the saved viewport center no longer recenters the drawing; before this release that request recalculated the scroll position, so confirm retaining the saved view is intended.

Verify that, after scrolling the canvas away from the center and loading a file whose drawing is outside the visible area, the drawing appears at the newly calculated position; before this release the load did not use the current canvas view, so confirm this new result is intended.

Check that dropping a file with several widely separated, off-screen shapes places them as intended; before this release restoration used the scroll-to-content option, so confirm the new placement is intended.
Confirm that opening a shared scene whose saved view leaves its shapes off-screen now shows the intended view; before this release the import requested scrolling to the content.
Confirm that loading a JSON drawing after scrolling the canvas uses the newly calculated position; before this release the file loader received no current canvas state.

Verify in the editor by saving and reloading a drawing while the canvas is below a page header, since before this release its nonzero top and left offsets could be retained in saved state and now they are omitted, that the canvas still responds correctly after reload and this omission is intended.

Confirm that generating the Node-based PNG with the included sample drawing still places its shapes correctly, since before this release the export had no explicit top and left offsets and now both are zero, and that this is intended.
Verify the hosted editor starts with nonzero top and left offsets and is resized; the canvas remains positioned within its host, and drawing interaction stays aligned with what is displayed.
Check a saved scene whose elements are offscreen at its saved scroll position; after opening it, the elements are brought into view and centered for the current canvas.
Test dropping the prepared .excalidraw file onto the canvas; its drawing is brought into view using the current editor viewport rather than remaining at the saved offscreen position.
Verify loading the prepared file brings the nearest drawing content into the current view.
Check that the drawing loads using its saved view position rather than automatically scrolling to its elements, and note whether the drawing is visible initially.
Verify the exported canvas includes the drawing elements and does not clip them.
uncertainty: The supplied context does not establish whether any supported integration relies on the removed optional setting to center content during restoration; confirm whether such integrations need separate coverage.
Removing automatic scrolling for shared drawings could leave their elements outside the initial view when the saved view does not include them.

The supplied evidence does not establish how offset values affect rendered or saved output, or provide a user-facing way to vary them; the precise old-versus-new regression input and expected outcome therefore remain unclear.
