report.summary: The release reorganizes how the editor starts, shares, and saves drawings, expands support for embedded use, and refines live collaboration.
keyChanges: Collaboration messages and saved room drawings now use AES-GCM encryption with a fresh 12-byte random IV; decryption failures show an alert and the invalid message is ignored.

The previous collaboration flow explicitly sent a full scene when a new participant joined and protected locally edited, resized, or dragged elements during remote reconciliation; those implementations were removed, so verify the replacement preserves those outcomes.

The room dialog’s prior implementation, including starting or stopping a session, copying its link, editing a participant name, and returning focus to its opener when closed, was removed from this component; verify these controls remain available in the application.
Drawing restoration now accepts null data and restores an empty scene instead of accessing properties on missing data.
The editor now defaults omitted embed width and height to the browser viewport, and its embed API adds readiness, history clearing, scroll-to-center, and access to non-deleted drawing elements.
Scene loading and URL-based shared-scene handling move into the showcase app wrapper; verify local drawing restoration, shared-link loading, and collaboration still initialize correctly.
Pointer updates now flow through the collaboration callback, including when two pointers are active, while scene-change broadcasting is delegated through the app wrapper.
Embed scene updates can omit drawing elements and can update collaborators or resume history recording; verify partial updates do not replace drawing content.

External drawing and collaboration links now use the app’s scene-loading flow: a drawing loads without confirmation when the local scene is empty, and the same collaboration room is force-loaded without confirmation when reopened within 15 seconds of leaving.
When a local drawing exists, opening an external drawing link asks for confirmation; accepting loads the linked drawing, while declining keeps the current drawing.
Joining live collaboration loads the room’s saved scene when available, otherwise uses the live session’s scene; drawing changes are saved locally and broadcast to collaborators.
The previous callback that saved a changed collaboration username locally was removed, so retaining a changed name after reload is uncertain.

The collaboration dialog control is replaced in desktop and mobile menus by a collaboration button; the button appears when its handler is supplied, shows a count only above zero, and reflects whether collaboration is active.
Remote pointer updates no longer include the sender’s selected drawing items, so whether this changes what collaborators see about selections needs confirmation.
Several session and editor helpers are removed from their previous location, but the supplied evidence does not show their replacement behavior.

Collaboration setup, remote drawing updates, session cleanup, and exit-time saving are removed from the main editor path; verify the collaboration link workflow still synchronizes drawings and preserves pending edits.
The embeddable editor now supports optional dimensions, asynchronous or null initial data, and a readiness-aware API ref with additional scene and history controls.
Flushing a deferred action before it has been scheduled now does nothing instead of calling its callback without arguments.

Scene updates now receive the syncable drawing elements from the collaboration callers, while full-scene broadcasts also update the version used to track synchronization; verify that new participants receive the current drawing and later edits continue to sync.

Remote drawing updates now check the wrapper’s stored editor interaction state when reconciling conflicts; verify that a local element being edited, resized, or dragged is preserved while remote changes are applied.

Live-collaboration pointer updates now take selected elements from the editor state and send an empty selection when that state is unavailable, which may affect what other participants see during setup.

Creating a collaboration session generates a link with a 20-character hexadecimal room ID and a 128-bit AES-GCM encryption key; the embeddable editor also now forwards its editor ref and collaboration and pointer properties to the editor.
Creating a room clears drawing history before committing the current drawing; ending a session saves the room, removes the room link from the address, and disconnects participants.

Incoming drawing updates are reconciled without being rebroadcast, initial drawings are centered, and received updates clear undo history; outgoing drawing updates are sent only when the scene version is higher than the last sent or received version.
Participant pointer updates are sent only when fewer than two pointers are active; participant presence is updated from received messages, and edited usernames are saved locally.
The collaboration dialog supports copying and selecting the room link, reports copy failures, and returns focus to the collaboration control when closed.
qaChecks: Verify that when a second participant joins a room containing existing elements, those elements appear in their drawing and subsequent edits synchronize between sessions.
Check that while one participant is editing, resizing, or dragging an element, a remote update to that same element does not discard the local in-progress change.
Confirm the room dialog still lets a participant start or stop a session, copy the collaboration link, and edit their name; closing the dialog should return keyboard focus to its opener.
Verify that with no initial scene data (null), the editor opens an empty drawing rather than failing to load.

Verify that when a second person joins an already-open collaboration room, the existing scene is still shared as intended; before this release, their arrival triggered an initial full-scene broadcast.
Check that after opening the room dialog with the keyboard and closing it, focus goes where intended; before this release, focus returned to the button that opened the dialog.
Verify that loading a scene with no imported data results in an empty scene; before this release, restoring null data failed, and confirm the new result is intended.
Confirm that opening a backend scene link with its private key loads the decrypted drawing; before this release, the legacy import path expected JSON rather than decrypting the response.

Verify that opening a backend scene while your local appearance setting differs keeps the local setting; before this release, the backend restore could omit that local setting, and confirm the new result is intended.
Verify a fresh launch with no saved scene or user name; before this release the default state supplied an empty user name and a false collaboration flag, so confirm their absence now is intended.
Verify an embedded drawing when you change its URL hash to a scene link; before this release the app reacted to that hash change, so confirm that it no longer loading a scene is intended.

Verify an embedded drawing after its parent changes the supplied width from 600 pixels to no width; before this release the app used the missing value, so confirm that it now filling the viewport is intended.

Verify an integration that uses the drawing’s imperative reference to clear history and read elements; before this release history clearing was a direct method and reading non-deleted elements was unavailable, so confirm the new reference API is intended.

Verify scene positioning in a page where the drawing sits inside an extra layout wrapper; before this release offsets came from the drawing element’s parent, so confirm the new parent-based positioning is intended.

Verify an integration that reads the drawing through its imperative reference after deleting an element; before this release there was no method for reading only non-deleted elements, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify an embedded drawing opened at a URL with a legacy scene identifier or encoded scene hash; before this release the component loaded that external scene, so confirm that it now ignoring the URL scene is intended.
Verify closing or refreshing a tab while it is connected to a collaboration room; before this release unloading explicitly destroyed the connection, so confirm that omitting that cleanup is intended.

Verify resetting a scene while its loading indicator is active without asking to clear that indicator; before this release reset always ended loading, so confirm that the indicator now remaining active is intended.
Verify a two-finger gesture while pointer updates are enabled; before this release pointer updates were suppressed when two pointers were active, so confirm that updates now being sent is intended.

Verify loading scene state with collaboration values that differ from the active room; before this release the active collaboration flag and collaborator list were retained, so confirm that scene state can now replace them.

Verify an integration that updates only the background color and leaves out the elements list; before this release an elements list was required, so confirm that the background now changing without replacing the scene is intended.

Verify starting a collaboration session from the main app; before this release the drawing was rendered without the new collaboration-wrapper integration, so confirm that the collaboration controls and session behavior now provided are intended.

Verify starting the app with a saved scene that takes time to initialize; before this release the drawing received data through the prior startup flow, so confirm that the new promise-based loading and collaboration handoff are intended.

Verify startup with scene data that resolves asynchronously; before this release there was no caller-resolvable promise helper here, so confirm that the drawing now waiting for initialization to resolve is intended.
Verify panning with repeated native pointer-move events; before this release this helper did not group the resulting state updates, so confirm that they now being batched is intended.
Verify that opening a collaboration-room link with a saved scene previously loaded that scene, and confirm whether it is intended for loading to fail now.
Verify that editing an element in a collaboration room previously did not send the edit to other participants, and confirm that broadcasting it now is intended.
Verify that changing the URL hash to a valid shared-scene link while the app is open previously left the canvas unchanged, and confirm that loading the linked scene now is intended.

Verify that opening an external scene link in a background tab with existing local content previously handled the link without waiting for focus, and confirm that deferring it until focus is intended.
Verify that changing the collaboration username previously persisted it after a reload, and confirm that no longer persisting the change is intended.
Verify that opening an external scene link on an empty canvas previously prompted before loading, and confirm that skipping the prompt now is intended.

Verify in a shared drawing that after rapid edits and waiting through the full-scene sync interval, a full scene update no longer occurs, whereas before this release it was broadcast, and confirm this is intended.

Verify that after navigating away from a drawing, changing the URL hash or closing the tab no longer triggers its old browser-event handling, whereas before this release its listeners were removed on unmount, and confirm the new behavior is intended.

Verify in an embedded drawing with no collaboration-button callback that the collaboration button is absent, whereas before this release the room controls were available, and confirm this is intended.
Verify that edits in a shared room no longer cause this room-save path to save data to Firebase, whereas before this release it saved the syncable elements, and confirm this is intended.
Verify in a shared room that another person joining or leaving no longer updates the collaborator list through this path, whereas before this release it did, and confirm this is intended.

Verify that reopening the same collaboration room within 15 seconds while a nonempty drawing is open no longer force-loads the room without prompting, whereas before this release it did, and confirm this is intended.

Verify that pasting a drawing containing several elements still produces the intended complete result without visible intermediate updates, whereas before this release the handler updates were batched, and confirm the new update behavior is intended.

Verify that clicking the collaboration button invokes the supplied callback and opens the intended collaboration experience, whereas before this release the room control managed its dialog, and confirm this is intended.

Verify in the desktop canvas menu with no collaboration-button callback that the collaboration button is absent, whereas before this release the room dialog control was present, and confirm this is intended.

Verify in the mobile canvas menu with no collaboration-button callback that the collaboration button is absent, whereas before this release the room dialog control was present, and confirm this is intended.

Verify in an embedded drawing that joins a collaboration room without setting the separate collaboration-active prop whether the collaboration control appearing inactive, whereas before this release it reflected the active app state, is intended.

Verify in a shared drawing that another person no longer sees your selected elements conveyed with your moving pointer, whereas before this release that selection was included in the pointer broadcast, and confirm this is intended.

Verify in a drawing with a custom user name that clearing the canvas no longer retains that name as part of the reset state; before this release, clearing retained it, so confirm the new result is intended.

Check browser save and reload after setting a name or joining a shared drawing; before this release, the configured saved state included the name and collaboration status, so confirm that they are no longer included as intended.

Verify in a development or test page that loading the application a second time preserves the existing debug object and refreshes its exposed values; before this release, the object was replaced, so confirm the new repeated-load result is intended.

Verify in a shared room that closing or reloading the tab with an unsaved edit no longer triggers the previous save attempt and browser leave warning; before this release, both were triggered, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that disconnecting from a shared room with another collaborator visible no longer performs the previous socket close and collaborator-list reset; before this release, it did, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify in a shared room when another participant adds an element that the canvas no longer applies the incoming scene through the previous update routine; before this release, it showed the change and cleared local undo history, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that opening a shared-room link with no initial scene update before the timeout no longer ends loading through the previous fallback; before this release, the fallback ended loading, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify by opening a collaboration link and receiving a scene or pointer update that the app no longer performs the previous connection and message handling; before this release, it joined the room and processed those updates, so confirm the new result is intended.

Check the drawing page by changing its URL hash to a different scene; before this release, a nonempty hash change reinitialized the scene, so confirm that the scene no longer reinitializing is intended.

Verify that starting a shared session from a drawing with a deleted element no longer follows the previous room-creation and deleted-element cleanup flow; before this release, it created a room link and removed the deleted element from history, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify by flushing a newly created debounced action before using it that nothing happens; before this release, the flush attempted to invoke the action without arguments, so confirm the new no-op result is intended.

Verify in a shared drawing that when an older update arrives after you finish editing the same shape as another person, your newer shape is kept as it was before this release and confirm that the new result, in which it may disappear, is intended.

Verify in a collaboration session that selecting an element and moving the pointer now shares that selection with collaborators; before this release the pointer update did not include the selected-element IDs, and confirm the new result is intended.

Verify in an embedded drawing that changing the collaboration username no longer calls the supplied username-change callback; before this release the callback was passed through, and confirm this change is intended.
Verify in a collaboration room that an unchanged drawing rendered a scene update again before this release, and confirm that it is no longer sent when you make no changes.
Verify that stopping a session after adding a drawing closed the room without saving it first before this release, and confirm the drawing is now saved before the session ends.
Verify that closing the room dialog left keyboard focus elsewhere before this release, and confirm focus now returns to the collaboration button.
Verify that loading a room snapshot positioned away from the current viewport did not center it before this release, and confirm the view now centers on the snapshot.
Verify that receiving the initial scene before the timeout still allowed the timeout fallback to run before this release, and confirm the fallback no longer runs after initialization.
Verify that a collaborator using a legacy cursor message showed no correctly identified cursor before this release, and confirm the cursor now appears under the right collaborator.
Verify that clicking the collaboration button did not open the room dialog before this release, and confirm it now opens.
Verify that a two-finger gesture sent collaborator pointer updates before this release, and confirm those updates are now suppressed.
Verify that a changed username was lost after reloading before this release, and confirm it is now retained.

report.summary: The release improves how text attached to shapes is laid out, edited, selected, and preserved across drawing actions and exports.
keyChanges: Text attached to a shape now wraps within the shape, can grow or shrink the shape as content changes, and retains its original text when edits are saved.
When starting text editing inside a shape with attached text, hit testing skips text elements to locate the shape and its existing attached text.
Text measurement now supports a width limit and accounts for empty lines, affecting text sizing and rendering.

Ordinary pointer hit-testing now leaves attached text out, while text editing still includes it; double-clicking the center of a shape can open its attached text or create new text attached to that shape.
Text editing now positions the editor using viewport coordinates and, when submitted by keyboard, selects the containing shape rather than its attached text.
Marquee selection no longer selects attached text separately, and duplicating a shape with attached text preserves the text-to-shape connection.

Resizing a shape with attached text now reflows that text to the available width and adjusts its position and height; a shape cannot be resized below the attached text’s minimum line width or into negative dimensions.
Rotating or flipping a shape now also updates its attached text, while text sizing measurements account for its container width.
When text is added to a container, the container is raised to minimum dimensions based on the text’s font metrics. Navigation was not found in code.
Copying a selected shape now includes its attached text, so verify copied drawings retain the complete shape-and-text combination.
Editing text attached to a container now measures it within the text width and can enlarge the container to leave 30 pixels of padding; dimension updates are now conditional.

Transparent fills are now recognized by their transparency value: an unbound transparent shape is no longer draggable from its interior, while a transparent shape with attached text remains draggable from inside.
Arrow binding now excludes text already attached to a shape, while standalone text remains eligible; selecting a rectangle, diamond, ellipse, or image also adds a context-sensitive text-binding hint.
Text wrapping and sizing now use canvas-based width measurements with per-character caching, so text layout is an important area to check.
Canvas text entry now accounts for shapes with attached text, and the keyboard text-entry path for a selected shape explicitly requests attachment to that shape.
Pasting or inserting library items and dragging to duplicate selected shapes now preserve attached text; moving an ungrouped shape also moves its attached text.
Image exports and Library items made from a selection now include text attached to selected shapes.
Restored text without attachment metadata now receives an unattached default and an empty original-text value.

For text attached to a shape or connector, line spacing now follows an approximate font line height instead of dividing the text area height evenly across its lines; verify multiline text does not stretch to fill a tall text area.
Selecting a shape now includes its bound text when grouping it, adding it to the Library, or copying the selection as PNG or SVG.
Deleting a selected shape now also deletes text bound to that shape; duplicating it now creates a matching text copy that remains bound to the duplicate.
Select All no longer directly selects container-bound text as a separate element.
qaChecks: Verify attached text containing one unbroken word longer than the shape’s inner width wraps within the shape and the shape grows as needed; save and reopen the text to confirm the content remains.
Check the overlap where attached text sits inside its shape by double-clicking the text; confirm the existing attached text opens for editing and is not treated as a separate enclosing shape.
Confirm that shortening attached text lets the shape shrink toward its original height, and that increasing the text size enough to exceed the shape’s inner height does not clip the text.
Verify that an unbound text item containing “A\n\nB” preserves the blank line’s visible spacing.

Verify that after editing and committing a long sentence in a rectangle, then widening it, the original line flow returns; before this release the saved wrapped lines could not restore it, so confirm the new result is intended.
Check that creating text inside a rectangle now makes it belong to that rectangle; before this release the new text was independent, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that several lines of text inside a tall rectangle now use consistent single-line spacing; before this release spacing was not based on a single-line measurement, so confirm the new result is intended.
Confirm that text with an empty first line now leaves space for that line; before this release the empty line could be dropped from the dimensions, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that changing the font size of a long sentence in a narrow rectangle keeps its recalculated text within the rectangle; before this release its dimensions could expand beyond the width limit, so confirm the new result is intended.

Check that typing a long sentence inside a narrow rectangle now wraps in the editor and keeps the new lines visible; before this release the editor stayed on one line, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that committing a long unbroken sentence inside a narrow rectangle now saves it wrapped to the shape's width; before this release it remained one unbroken line, so confirm the new result is intended.

Confirm that increasing the font size while editing bound text now triggers the expected layout adjustment; before this release the font change was not detected for that adjustment, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that a short rectangle now grows when added lines exceed its height and shrinks again when those lines are removed; before this release its height stayed fixed, so confirm the new result is intended.

Check that clicking overlapping text and a rectangle now identifies the rectangle beneath the text; before this release the text itself could be identified as the hit element, so confirm the new result is intended.
Verify on the canvas that right-clicking a shape’s bound text label targeted the label before this release and now targets the containing shape, and confirm this change is intended.
Check on the canvas that clicking a bound text label selected the label before this release and now hits the containing shape, and confirm this change is intended.

Verify on the canvas that double-clicking near the edge of a selected shape with a bound label could start new text before this release and now opens the bound label, and confirm this change is intended.
Confirm that pressing Enter after changing a shape’s bound text selected the text before this release and now selects the containing shape, and verify this is intended.
Verify that clicking the center of a shape with the text tool created unbound text before this release and now creates bound text, and confirm this change is intended.
Check that copying and pasting a shape with bound text left the pasted label unbound before this release and now keeps it attached, and confirm this change is intended.
Verify that dragging a transparent shape with bound text from its empty interior did not move it before this release and now moves it, and confirm this change is intended.
Confirm that a selection box enclosing a shape and its bound text could select the label separately before this release and now excludes it, and verify this change is intended.
Verify that marquee-selecting a shape and its bound text included both elements before this release and now omits the bound text, and confirm this change is intended.
Check that duplicating a selected shape with bound text copied the shape without its attached label before this release and now copies the label with it, and confirm this change is intended.

Verify that resizing bound text which wraps onto multiple lines now keeps its baseline aligned; before this release the baseline was measured without a width limit, so confirm the new alignment is intended.

Verify that dragging a bound container’s side handle narrower than the minimum width needed for its text now stops at that minimum; before this release the container could become narrower, so confirm the new limit is intended.

Confirm that resizing a selection containing a container with bound text now adjusts the text to fit; before this release the selection resize did not adjust the bound text, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that adding text to a very short container now increases its height enough for a minimum line; before this release the container was not raised to this minimum, so confirm the new sizing is intended.

Verify that adding text to a very narrow container now increases its width enough for a minimum line; before this release the container was not widened to this minimum, so confirm the new sizing is intended.

report.summary: The release makes diagram editing more reliable by improving how objects are selected and connections are maintained.
keyChanges: Canvas pointer targeting and arrow-to-shape binding now use shared geometric hit testing, affecting selection, text editing, and which shape an arrow can connect to.

Binding distinguishes arrows from other lines and strokes: arrows can connect to rectangles, diamonds, ellipses, and text; moving or resizing a connected shape updates its arrow endpoints, and removing one connection should preserve another connection to the same shape.
Canvas hit detection now uses shape-distance checks for shapes, text, lines, arrows, and freehand drawings, affecting which elements pointer actions can select or connect to.
Arrow-binding proximity is sized from the smaller shape dimension, with a 15–80 pixel limit and a diamond adjustment; suggested connections now receive a canvas highlight.
Linear-element editing points and resize or rotation handles are rendered as filled circles or filled handles instead of the previous outlined point squares or rotation circle.
The new geometry calculations feed pointer hit-testing and arrow connection placement and updates, so selection and connected diagrams are the main areas to exercise.
Arrows can now suggest and attach to eligible shapes while drawing or editing, and holding Ctrl or Cmd temporarily disables binding; changing away from an arrow tool clears binding suggestions.

Pasting or inserting a connected shape-and-arrow set now repairs its connections to the duplicated elements, and submitting blank or whitespace-only text removes its connections when that text element is deleted.
Changing tools during an in-progress arrow can bind its last point to a shape when binding is enabled.
Arrow endpoints can connect to eligible shapes, and connections are recalculated when a connected shape moves or resizes; no other supplied change establishes a user-visible behavior difference.
Drawing or moving an arrow endpoint over a shape now suggests and applies a connection when the pointer is released; moving or resizing connected shapes also updates their attached elements.
Deleting a connected shape now clears connections that refer to it, and deleting a line or arrow endpoint clears its pending endpoint connection.

Copying, duplicating, or Alt-dragging connected elements now updates their connections to preserve links within the copied set; releasing Alt after creating an uncommitted line point now clears that temporary-point state.
Finishing a line or arrow can now bind its endpoints to shapes, with binding enabled by default.
Duplicating connected shapes and connectors now remaps their relationships to the duplicated elements instead of leaving copies tied to the originals.
Restoring saved drawings now retains connector bindings, and undo or redo repairs bindings when elements are deleted or restored.

The geometry behind canvas hit-testing and arrow-to-shape binding now uses new calculations for ellipses, rectangles, diamonds, and text; check that pointer selection and connections still behave as expected.
qaChecks: Verify that an arrow drawn with an endpoint on each of a rectangle, diamond, ellipse, and text item connects at the target boundary, and that its connection suggestion appears when hovering over an eligible target.
Check a two-ended arrow connected to the same shape at both ends: move and resize the shape, then disconnect one endpoint; confirm the remaining endpoint stays connected and follows the shape.

Confirm a line or freehand stroke does not behave as an arrow connection, while an arrow endpoint placed on a rotated shape connects to that shape; clicking within the rotated shape targets it, while clicking outside does not target it.

Verify that when you double-click or right-click the overlap of two grouped shapes, the element hit at the pointer is targeted; before this release the action could target a different element, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that when the free end of a simple arrow is hovered over the same shape already bound to its opposite end, no suggestion appears; before this release that shape could be suggested, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that after both ends of an arrow are bound to one rectangle, unbinding just one end leaves the other end attached; before this release the rectangle could lose the arrow association, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that an arrow endpoint over a rectangle covered by a non-bindable line can still target the rectangle; before this release the line could block the target, so confirm the new result is intended.
Verify that with arrow binding turned off, moving an endpoint over a rectangle leaves it unattached; before this release it could still bind, so confirm the new result is intended.
Verify that moving a rectangle into the binding area of an unbound arrow endpoint attaches the endpoint; before this release it stayed unattached, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that drawing an arrow from inside one rectangle to another attaches each end to the rectangle at that end; before this release the arrow could finish unattached, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that when you move and resize a rectangle together with its attached arrow, the endpoint stays on the border without an extra shift; before this release it could shift again, so confirm the new result is intended.
Confirm that element positions and bounds behave the same as before; this release changes only the declared type, so there should be no user-visible difference.

Verify that a point at the center of an odd-sized rectangle is treated as its center for hit testing and binding; before this release the center calculation could differ, so confirm the new result is intended.
Verify that clicking just outside a 45-degree rotated rectangle does not count as hitting its edge; before this release the unrotated bounds could count it, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that an arrow attached to a 90-degree rotated ellipse remains positioned against the correct side as its other endpoint moves; before this release the focus could use the unrotated orientation, so confirm the new result is intended.
Verify that an arrow endpoint placed on a text element’s border can bind to it; before this release text was not treated as a binding target, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that a line does not acquire arrow-style endpoint bindings when its endpoint is placed over a rectangle; before this release it could be treated as eligible, so confirm the new result is intended.
Verify that a line drawn onto a rectangle remains unbound while an arrow can attach; before this release the line type could pass the binding check, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that a point at x=120, y=40 hits the expected location on a shape rather than its transposed location; before this release the coordinates could be reversed, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that an arrow attached to a shape stays at the correct scene position as its other endpoint moves; before this release the inverse calculation could shift the focus the wrong way, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that clicking just outside a sloping edge of a very wide or tall diamond is treated consistently as outside; before this release the distance could vary with equation scale, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that clicking just outside a diamond’s diagonal edge is consistently treated as outside; before this release the edge calculation could vary with point ordering or scale, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that points at the same small distance outside a rectangle border or diamond edge are classified consistently; before this release the distance calculation could differ, so confirm the new result is intended.
Verify that a binding point at x=120, y=40 appears at that position rather than at x=40, y=120; before this release the axes could be reversed, so confirm the new result is intended.
Verify that an arrow endpoint attached at x=120, y=40 remains reported at x=120, y=40; before this release the returned coordinates could be reversed, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that a point on the edge of a rectangle rotated 90 degrees counts as a hit, while a point just outside does not; before this release the transformed point could produce a different hit result, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that a rectangle rotated 90 degrees is hit at its displayed edges and not at the old unrotated edges; before this release the collision transform could use a different pivot or direction, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that after moving a shape 120 pixels right and 40 pixels down, hit testing follows it at that new position; before this release the transformed position could be offset in the wrong direction, so confirm the new result is intended.
Verify on a canvas with a large rectangle that a connector endpoint just outside its edge did not bind before this release but may bind now, and confirm the larger binding area is intended.
Check a connector approaching a wide, shallow ellipse diagonally; its attachment focus used the previous calculation before this release, so confirm the newly shifted attachment point is intended.

Verify that hovering a connector endpoint near a bindable shape’s edge used the previous hit test before this release and now follows the shape-specific boundary, and confirm the changed binding response is intended.

Confirm that a connector endpoint just outside a diamond’s sloping edge was judged by the previous edge test before this release and is judged by the new distance calculation now, and verify the binding result is intended.

Verify that a connector endpoint near the curved edge of a very wide, thin ellipse was checked by the previous ellipse hit test before this release and now uses the closest-point calculation, and confirm the result is intended.
Check a connector endpoint just outside a rectangle near a corner; the previous edge test decided binding before this release, so confirm the new near-side distance gives the intended result.

Verify a pointer or connector endpoint near the edge of a highly elongated ellipse; the previous calculation found the edge point before this release, so confirm the new estimated point produces the intended hit or binding result.

Verify that clicking just outside a shape’s edge at a non-default zoom used the previous edge test before this release and now uses the shared zoom-aware test, and confirm the changed selection behavior is intended.

Check clicking just beyond a line or arrow’s endpoint, outside its bounding box; the previous linear hit test handled this before this release, so confirm the new early bounds rejection gives the intended result.

Verify that clicking inside a filled loop-shaped line or drawing was handled by the previous direct hit test before this release and now follows the shared linear test, and confirm the selection result is intended.

Confirm that clicking well inside a filled rectangle was handled by the previous filled-shape test before this release and now passes the signed-distance check, and verify that interior selection is intended.

Verify that moving a connector endpoint inside a bindable rectangle was handled by the previous binding hit test before this release and is now rejected by the outside-only check, and confirm that behavior is intended.

Check binding a connector to a very large rectangle from more than 15 pixels away but within one quarter of its smaller dimension; the previous gap limit applied before this release, so confirm the larger gap is intended.

Verify a point just inside an ellipse’s edge for binding or selection; the previous sign calculation determined its inside or outside result before this release, so confirm the result from the new sign calculation is intended.

Confirm that testing a point near a rectangle’s corner used the previous side-selection calculation before this release and now uses the normalized vector, and verify the resulting hit or binding decision is intended.
Verify a selected line’s point handles or rotation handle; they were outlines only before this release, so confirm that the newly filled circles are intended.
Check a binding suggestion after panning the canvas; no highlight was rendered here before this release, so confirm the newly visible, correctly positioned highlight is intended.
Verify hovering a connector near a large diamond; it had no padded binding outline before this release, so confirm the new shape-adjusted outline is intended.
Confirm that hovering a connector’s start point near a bindable target showed no filled endpoint highlight before this release and now shows one, and verify the new highlight is intended.
Verify the rotation handle on a selected element; it was an outline before this release, so confirm the newly filled handle is intended.
Check the point handles while editing a line or arrow; they were outlined before this release, so confirm the new filled appearance and active-point color are intended.
Verify the canvas while a connector has a suggested binding and binding is enabled; no suggestion highlight appeared before this release, so confirm that it now appears as intended.
Confirm that a rotated diamond showed no binding-highlight outline before this release and now shows a padded outline when a binding is suggested, and verify the rotation and padding are intended.
Verify the binding highlight for a rotated ellipse; no outline was drawn here before this release, so confirm the new rotated padded outline is intended.
Verify in the geometry calculator that adding 3 to [1,2,0,0,0,0,0,0] previously gave an invalid result and now gives [4,2,0,0,0,0,0,0], and confirm this change is intended.
Check in the geometry calculator that conjugating [1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8] previously produced a different sign pattern and now gives [1,-2,-3,-4,-5,-6,-7,8], and confirm this change is intended.
Confirm that creating a direction with x=0 and y=0 previously gave a zero direction and now gives undefined numeric values, and verify that this is intended.
Verify in the geometry calculator that taking the dual of [1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8] previously gave a different result and now gives [8,7,6,5,4,3,2,1], and confirm this change is intended.
Check that measuring the inorm of [0,0,0,0,2,0,0,0] previously returned NaN and now returns 2, and confirm this change is intended.
Confirm that normalizing the zero vector previously attempted a division by zero and now returns the zero vector unchanged, and verify that this is intended.
Check that using 0 as the second input to a scalar operation previously followed the non-scalar path and now follows the scalar path, and confirm this change is intended.
Verify in the geometry calculator that joining [0,1,0,0,0,0,0,0] with [0,0,0,0,0,0,0,1] previously gave a different result and now gives [0,1,0,0,0,0,0,0], and confirm this change is intended.
Check that the scalar part of joining [1,0,0,0,0,0,0,0] and [0,0,0,0,0,0,0,1] previously differed from 1 and now equals 1, and confirm this change is intended.
Verify in the geometry calculator that meeting [1,0,0,0,0,0,0,0] with [0,1,0,0,0,0,0,0] previously gave a different result and now gives [0,1,0,0,0,0,0,0], and confirm this change is intended.
Confirm that multiplying [1,2,0,0,0,0,0,0] by 0 previously did not return the zero vector and now does, and verify that this change is intended.
Check that the scalar part of multiplying [0,0,1,0,0,0,0,0] by itself previously differed from 1 and now equals 1, and confirm this change is intended.
Verify that measuring the norm of [0,0,2,0,0,0,0,0] previously returned NaN and now returns 2, and confirm this change is intended.
Check that normalizing [0,0,0,0,0,0,-2,0] previously retained a negative seventh component and now gives that component as 1, and confirm this change is intended.
Confirm that creating a vector with index 8 previously did not throw an index-range error and now does, and verify that this change is intended.
Verify that an offset with x=2 and y=3 previously placed its coordinates differently and now gives [0,0,0,0,3,2,0,0], and confirm this change is intended.
Check in the geometry calculator that subtracting 3 from [5,2,0,0,0,0,0,0] previously gave an invalid result and now gives [2,2,0,0,0,0,0,0], and confirm this change is intended.
Confirm that displaying a vector with a component of exactly 0.000001 previously included that component and now omits it, and verify that this change is intended.
Check that converting a point with nonzero scalar and homogeneous components previously retained those components and now drops them, and confirm this change is intended.
Verify that taking the perpendicular of a direction with coordinates x=3 and y=0 previously retained magnitude 3 and now has unit magnitude, and confirm this change is intended.
Check that finding a perpendicular direction for a horizontal line previously gave a different result and now points along its perpendicular, and confirm this change is intended.
Verify that measuring between the parallel lines y=0 and y=5 previously gave a different distance and now gives their separation, and confirm this change is intended.
Check that moving the horizontal line y=0 by a distance of 5 previously did not shift it by changing its first coordinate and now does, and confirm this change is intended.

Verify that taking the absolute value of a point at x=-2 and y=-3 previously retained a negative coordinate or homogeneous component and now gives x=2, y=3, and homogeneous component 1, and confirm this change is intended.
Check that composing a 90-degree rotation followed by a rightward translation previously applied the rotation first and now applies the translation first, and confirm this change is intended.
Verify that translating by 4 along a horizontal line previously did not translate by 2 along its perpendicular and now does, and confirm this change is intended.

Verify that copying a rectangle with an attached arrow and pasting both used to leave the arrow connected to the original rectangle, and confirm that it now connects to the pasted rectangle as intended.
Verify that drawing an arrow endpoint on a rectangle and switching tools used to leave it unconnected, and confirm that it now connects to the rectangle as intended.

Verify that hovering an arrow tool or unfinished arrow endpoint over a rectangle border used to show no binding suggestion, and confirm that the rectangle is now suggested and the suggestion clears when you move away.
Verify that submitting empty or spaces-only text on a shape connected to an arrow used to leave its connection unrepaired, and confirm that the connection is now fixed as intended.
Verify that moving over a rectangle border and then empty canvas used to provide no updated binding suggestion, and confirm that the rectangle is now suggested only while you hover over it.
Verify that switching windows while holding Control or Command used to leave binding disabled after returning, and confirm that binding is now re-enabled as intended.
Verify that drawing an arrow near a rectangle while holding Control or Command used to allow binding, and confirm that binding is now suppressed while the modifier is held.
Verify that releasing Control or Command used to leave binding disabled until another event changed it, and confirm that releasing the key now re-enables binding as intended.
Verify that switching from an arrow tool to the rectangle or selection tool used to leave the prior binding suggestion in place, and confirm that it now clears as intended.

Verify that editing an arrow attached to a rectangle and dragging only a middle point used to have no explicit preservation of its endpoint connections, and confirm that the endpoints now remain attached as intended.

Verify that with a two-point line already attached at its start to a rectangle, attaching its end to that same rectangle used to connect both ends; confirm that the second connection is now refused as intended.
Verify that disconnecting one end of a line while keeping its other end attached used to risk changing the kept connection; confirm that the kept end now stays attached as intended.
Verify that selecting a line with an endpoint touching a shape used to leave it unconnected; confirm that the endpoint now connects when the elements are selected as intended.
Verify that creating a connection with an endpoint exactly on a shape’s border used to leave no gap; confirm that the endpoint now has at least a one-pixel gap as intended.
Verify that moving a shape with a stale attached-line list used to move a listed line even when neither endpoint was connected to it; confirm that the unrelated line now stays put as intended.
Verify that selecting both a line and the shape it touches used to show that shape as a connection suggestion; confirm that the selected shape is now omitted as intended.
Verify that selecting a line with an endpoint on a shape’s border used to leave the shape out of endpoint-based connection suggestions; confirm that it is now eligible as intended.

Verify that during line creation a shape already attached to the other end used to be suggested again when the cursor hovered over it; confirm that it is no longer suggested for a two-point line as intended.
Verify that moving a rectangle over a free line start used to produce no endpoint-specific connection suggestion; confirm that the line is now suggested with its start as the eligible end.
Verify that with a line touching two different shapes at its two ends, the old suggestion behavior did not gather both endpoint candidates; confirm that both shapes are now offered as intended.
Verify that for a three-point line whose last point touches a shape, the old end check did not use that final point; confirm that the actual line end is now used as intended.
Verify that moving a shape and its connected line together used to reposition the line separately and could distort the connection; confirm that the line now moves with the selection as intended.
Verify that a line endpoint already connected to one shape used to be suggested for another shape when it overlapped it; confirm that it is now excluded from new-connection suggestions as intended.
Verify that attaching both ends of a two-point line to the same shape used to be allowed; confirm that the simple-line check now identifies and prevents that duplicate as intended.

Verify that hovering over the shape attached to the opposite end of a two-point line used to leave that existing connection unchecked; confirm that the shape is now recognized as already connected as intended.
Verify that shrinking a connected shape used to leave its line gap unchanged; confirm that the gap now scales down but never below one pixel as intended.
Verify that disconnecting only the start of a line used to leave that start attached; confirm that the start is now disconnected while the end remains connected as intended.
Verify that selecting two connected lines and using the unbind action used to leave their connections in place; confirm that both lines are now disconnected as intended.
Verify that moving a shape attached to the start of a three-point line used to leave that start behind; confirm that the start now follows the shape while the other end stays in place as intended.

Verify that requesting a line, a deleted shape, a missing item, and a live shape used to have no filtered multi-item lookup; confirm that only the two live elements now remain in their original order as intended.

Verify on the canvas that, before this release, deleting a rectangle attached to an arrow could leave the arrow bound to the deleted rectangle, and confirm that deleting it now clears that binding without disturbing the arrow’s other endpoint as intended.
Verify on the canvas that, before this release, starting an arrow inside a rectangle did not bind its starting endpoint to that rectangle, and confirm that the new arrow now binds there as intended.

Verify on the canvas that, before this release, dragging two selected arrows near a rectangle showed no binding suggestion for the selection, and confirm that eligible targets are now suggested as intended.

Verify on the canvas that, before this release, Alt-dragging a bound arrow and its rectangle could leave the duplicate arrow attached to the original rectangle, and confirm that the duplicate now binds to the duplicated rectangle as intended.
Verify on the canvas that, before this release, an arrow released over a rectangle did not bind its endpoint there, and confirm that it now binds on release as intended.
Verify on the canvas that, before this release, deleting a rectangle could leave its surviving arrow bound to it, and confirm that the arrow’s binding is now cleared as intended.

Verify on the canvas that, before this release, pasting a rectangle and its attached arrow could leave the pasted arrow bound to the original, and confirm that it now binds to the pasted rectangle as intended.
Verify on the canvas that, before this release, deleting an arrow’s target shape could leave the endpoint bound to it, and confirm that the endpoint is now unbound as intended.

Verify on the canvas that, before this release, copying a rectangle and its bound arrow could leave the copied arrow attached to the original rectangle, and confirm that it now attaches to the copy as intended.
Verify on the canvas that, before this release, dragging a rectangle by itself could leave its bound arrow endpoint behind, and confirm that the endpoint now follows the rectangle as intended.
Verify on the canvas that, before this release, releasing a rotated arrow endpoint over a rectangle could miss the binding target, and confirm that it now binds at the rotated endpoint as intended.
Verify on the canvas that, before this release, moving an arrow endpoint over a rectangle showed no binding suggestion, and confirm that the rectangle is now suggested during the drag as intended.

Verify on the canvas that, before this release, Alt-clicking to add an arrow endpoint on a rectangle did not record it as a binding candidate, and confirm that the endpoint now binds to the rectangle as intended.

Verify on the canvas that, before this release, releasing Alt during point creation could leave the next Alt-click unable to add a fresh point, and confirm that the next point now adds correctly as intended.
Verify on the canvas that, before this release, releasing an arrow endpoint on a rectangle did not record it for binding, and confirm that the endpoint now binds there as intended.

Verify on the canvas that, before this release, moving an arrow endpoint could not update its binding together with the point change, and confirm that endpoint movement now preserves the intended binding.
Verify on the canvas that, before this release, there was no offset-based endpoint move, and confirm that moving a rotated line endpoint by a small offset now places it correctly as intended.

Verify on the canvas that, before this release, converting a point on a rotated line did not use this rotation-aware conversion, and confirm that the endpoint now lands at the intended canvas position.
Verify on the canvas that, before this release, rotating a rectangle could leave its bound arrow endpoint in place, and confirm that the endpoint now follows the rotation as intended.

Verify on the canvas that, before this release, resizing a selection containing a rectangle and its attached arrow could leave the endpoint misplaced, and confirm that it now remains attached as intended.
Verify on the canvas that, before this release, resizing a rectangle could leave its attached arrow endpoint out of place, and confirm that the endpoint now stays attached as intended.

Verify on the canvas that duplicating a selected rectangle together with its connected arrow used to leave the new arrow connected to the original rectangle, and confirm the new arrow connects to the duplicate as intended.
Verify on the canvas that finishing an arrow with its endpoint on a rectangle’s center used to leave it unconnected, and confirm the new connection is intended.
Verify on the canvas that redoing the deletion of a rectangle connected to an arrow used to leave the arrow connected to the removed shape, and confirm the arrow now disconnects as intended.
Verify on a drawing that turning off automatic arrow connections and reloading used to have no setting to reset, and confirm the setting now returns to enabled as intended.
Verify on a new blank drawing that an arrow ending on a rectangle used to remain unconnected by default, and confirm it now connects as intended.
Verify that opening a saved drawing containing a rectangle used to omit the rectangle, and confirm it now appears as intended.
Verify that opening a saved drawing with a rectangle connected to an arrow used to discard that connection information, and confirm deleting the rectangle now disconnects the arrow as intended.
Verify on the canvas that drawing an arrow to a newly created rectangle used to leave the arrow behind when the rectangle moved, and confirm the arrow now follows it as intended.

report.summary: The release adds end-to-end hyperlink support for drawings in the editor, from adding and editing links to viewing and opening them.
keyChanges: A link action is now included when exactly one element is selected, and the help shortcuts list documents Ctrl/Cmd+K for the link action.
Tooltips now reposition when centered placement would extend beyond the left edge, using a 5-pixel margin; link tooltips prefer above the link icon and move below it when there is not enough room.
Unselected drawing elements with links now show a 14-pixel external-link indicator on the canvas; selecting the element hides it, and exports do not render the indicator.

Hyperlink popup state now starts hidden and is cleared when the context menu opens or the editor changes from selection to another tool; the context menu also includes the link action when its availability condition is met.
Link data is now retained when an element is restored; older elements without a link receive a null link value, while existing link values are kept.
The link action is assigned Ctrl+K on non-Mac platforms and Cmd+K on Mac, so verify the shortcut is shown and recognized for that action.
The rounded-diamond path change removes only extra whitespace and has no expected visible effect.
A link action is added for a single selected element; Ctrl/Cmd+K opens the link editor, and the context-menu action distinguishes creating a link from editing an existing one.
New drawing elements now retain a supplied link value and default to no link when none is supplied; pointer hit-testing behavior is unchanged by its export-only change.
Hyperlink entries are trimmed; a value without “://” that does not start with “/” or “[” receives an “https://” prefix, while blank input stays blank.
Submitting with Enter or Escape saves the entered link; editing and removing a link update the drawing, and removing it closes the popup.
Linked addresses starting with “/” or containing the current site’s origin open in the same tab; other addresses open in a new tab, with link activation based on a zoom-adjusted icon hit area.

The information popup is designed to remain visible when the pointer is over the linked element, the gap below it, or the popup, and to close after the pointer leaves those areas. Its position is anchored above the element.

Hovering a linked element’s link icon now shows a pointer cursor and link tooltip; clicking or tapping the icon navigates only when both press and release are on the icon, opening local links in the same tab and external links in a new tab.

Selecting one linked element, including through a drag selection that selects exactly one, now displays its hyperlink popup; pressing the link icon is treated as a link interaction rather than ordinary element selection.
Drawing elements now include a link field that accepts a string or null; no user-visible behavior change is evidenced.
qaChecks: Verify the link action is available with exactly one selected element and is not shown when multiple elements are selected.
Check that the help shortcuts list shows Ctrl/Cmd+K for the link action.
Confirm a linked, unselected element shows its link icon and that hovering over the icon displays the element’s link; move the pointer away and confirm the tooltip hides.
Test a linked, rotated element at a changed zoom level and confirm its visible link icon and hover target remain aligned.
Verify that the tooltip for a control near the left edge remains visible within the viewport with at least a 5-pixel left margin, rather than being clipped.
Verify the selected-shape panel with exactly one shape selected; before this release it did not show a link action, so confirm the new link action is intended.
Verify the shortcuts section in the help dialog; before this release it did not list a shortcut for links, so confirm the new Ctrl+K or Cmd+K listing is intended.
Check a control near the left edge of the browser window whose tooltip would extend past that edge; before this release the tooltip could be clipped, so confirm it is now shifted inward.

Verify a linked shape with its link icon close to the top edge of the browser window; before this release hovering the icon showed no destination tooltip, so confirm it now appears below the icon when it cannot fit above.

Verify a linked shape rotated away from zero degrees and try its link icon; before this release the shape had no link-icon hit area, so confirm the icon is now positioned and clickable at the rotated corner.

Check moving the pointer onto a linked shape and off it again before the tooltip delay expires; before this release no delayed destination tooltip was shown, so confirm it now stays hidden after you leave.
Verify hovering the link icon for a shape linked to https://example.com; before this release the destination was not shown on hover, so confirm it now appears in a tooltip near the icon.

Check moving the pointer from one linked shape to another before the tooltip delay expires; before this release no delayed destination tooltip was shown, so confirm only the second shape’s destination appears after the delay.
Verify that a new drawing starts with no hyperlink popup visible; before this release there was no popup setting, and confirm the new hidden-by-default result is intended.

Check that the link editor now shows the pencil-style edit icon where the edit control appears, whereas that icon was unavailable before this release, and confirm this is intended.

report.summary: Text attached to shapes now supports vertical alignment and adjusts its layout accordingly.
keyChanges: Editing or resizing a shape with attached text now places top-aligned text at a 5 px inset, bottom-aligned text at a 5 px inset from the bottom, and middle-aligned text in the center; resizing previously centered text regardless of alignment.
No navigation or user-facing control for choosing vertical alignment was supplied, so verify the changed positioning using drawings already set up with each alignment.
Selection properties now include vertical-alignment controls when every selected item is either a shape with attached text or text attached to a container.

Reopening existing attached text no longer resets its vertical alignment when it has no center snap position or its horizontal alignment is left or right; bottom-aligned text now renders using the container’s bottom padding in the editor and image exports.

Bound text that was previously centered can now be positioned at the top, middle, or bottom of its shape; top and bottom positioning use padding and no longer enlarge the shape when the text is too tall, while middle positioning retains the previous resize behavior.
The vertical-position controls now show the alignment of a selected shape’s attached text, and changing text font, size, or alignment recalculates its position using the chosen vertical alignment.
The horizontal-alignment control now reads the alignment from text attached to a selected shape.

Check that editing top-aligned text keeps it at the top inset, while editing bottom-aligned text places it 5 px above the container’s bottom edge.
Confirm that resizing attached text with middle alignment keeps it vertically centered.

Verify that a shape with bottom-aligned bound text places the text 5 pixels from the bottom after you resize the shape; before this release the text was vertically centered, so confirm the new placement is intended.

Verify that editing top-aligned text inside a shape keeps the editor at the top rather than centering it; before this release the editor was vertically centered, so confirm the new placement is intended.
Verify the selected-shape controls for a container with attached text; before this release the vertical-alignment control was absent, and confirm its appearance now is intended.
Verify editing left-aligned, bottom-aligned text attached to a container; before this release it reset to the default vertical alignment, and confirm it now stays bottom-aligned as intended.
Check a container with attached text set to bottom alignment; before this release its position used the height-and-baseline offset, and confirm the new bottom-padding position is intended.
Verify the text properties for text inside a shape, where no vertical-alignment control appeared before this release, now offer top, middle, and bottom alignment, and confirm this is intended.

Check the properties for text inside a shape that is bottom-aligned; before this release there were no vertical-alignment choices, and now bottom should be selected among the three choices—confirm this is intended.
Verify that choosing bottom alignment for text inside a shape, an option unavailable before this release, moves the text to the bottom and can be undone, and confirm this is intended.
Confirm that selecting top alignment for text inside a shape, which had no available vertical-alignment action before this release, now applies top alignment as intended.

Verify that selecting the attached text and its container shows a vertical-alignment control, while selecting only the unattached text does not.

report.summary: The release improves how users shape and edit lines and arrows.
keyChanges: Line and arrow editing now calculates midpoint handles per segment, places handles on round multi-point curves using the curve itself, and omits handles for segments that are too short at the current zoom.
Clicking a segment midpoint adds a point at that segment’s position rather than always inserting at the former general midpoint location.
During live collaboration, editing handles are rendered using the corresponding visible drawing element, which is intended to avoid mismatches with the editor’s stored element.

Rounded lines and arrows with multiple points now use sampled curve geometry and curve length to position segment midpoint handles at the halfway point along the curve, affecting their display and pointer targeting during editing.

Midpoint hover and hit detection now use segment midpoint coordinates instead of a single midpoint between the line’s endpoints; this makes segment-level editing available, including for lines with three or more points.
qaChecks: Verify that clicking the midpoint of the segment between the second and third vertices adds a point on that segment, rather than inserting it at the former general midpoint location.
Check that a round multi-point line shows its segment midpoint on the visible curve and that clicking there adds a point on the curve.
Confirm that a segment short enough to fall below the new four-point-handle-size screen-distance cutoff has no midpoint handle to hover over or select.

Test editing a multi-point line while the other participant synchronizes scene changes; confirm the editing handles remain visible on the edited line and that clicking a segment midpoint adds a point at that segment.

Verify that, with a line selected, moving the pointer over the line away from every point or midpoint no longer causes hover flicker or an error, whereas before the missing midpoint positions were not safely treated as equal, and confirm this result is intended.

Verify that a selected line with three or more points shows no segment midpoint handles before you enter point-editing mode, whereas before a midpoint was available, and confirm this result is intended.

Verify that, while editing a round three-point line with a visibly bowed segment, its midpoint handle sits on the curve rather than halfway between the endpoints as before, and confirm this result is intended.

Verify that clicking the midpoint of the last segment of a four-point line inserts the new point into that segment, whereas before that midpoint could be matched to its position, and confirm the new insertion result is intended.

Verify that hovering over a segment midpoint on a selected three-point line outside point-editing mode no longer shows midpoint-hover feedback, whereas before the midpoint could be detected, and confirm this result is intended.

Verify that clicking the midpoint between the second and third points of a four-point line inserts a point there, whereas before a midpoint click inserted it near the start, and confirm this result is intended.

Verify that editing a round three-point line with a strongly bowed segment shows a midpoint handle when the curve is long enough even though its endpoints are close, whereas before no handle appeared, and confirm this result is intended.

Verify that, while editing a line with two adjacent points closer than the handle-size threshold, no midpoint handle appears on their tiny segment, whereas before a midpoint was calculated for it, and confirm this result is intended.
Verify that, when a later-drawn shape overlaps a point handle on an edited line, the shape covers the handle, whereas before the handle remained on top, and confirm this result is intended.

Verify that editing a bent line with three or more points displays a midpoint handle on each eligible segment, whereas before there was only one overall midpoint handle, and confirm this result is intended.

Verify that editing a rounded line with several bends and adding a midpoint handle on a later segment now places it on that segment’s curve rather than at the straight midpoint used before this release, and confirm the new placement is intended.

Check a rounded line with a strongly bowed segment: before this release its editing behavior followed the straight connection between the endpoints, so confirm the new behavior follows the curved path as intended.
Confirm that editing a rounded segment with endpoints close together but a pronounced bend now counts the curved path rather than the short straight distance used before this release.
Verify that a rounded segment with a short straight gap but a long curved path now remains editable where it was treated as too short before this release, and confirm this is intended.

Check a rounded segment with an asymmetric curve and inspect its midpoint handle: before this release it sat at the straight endpoint midpoint, so confirm that it now follows the calculated curve point.

Verify a rounded line with four distinct curve points at its two ends: before this release the curve calculation ran from the first point to the last as the parameter increased, so confirm the reversed calculation now produces the intended visible curve.

Check a rounded segment with most of its bend near one end: before this release its midpoint handle was placed at the straight endpoint midpoint, so confirm it now appears halfway along the curve’s length as intended.
Verify that immediately after leaving line-edit mode, moving the pointer no longer fails while checking an unfinished point as it could before this release, and confirm this result is intended.

Verify that hovering over the midpoint of the second segment of a selected three-point line now shows an interactive pointer, whereas before this release no midpoint target was identified, and confirm this is intended.

Confirm that after changing zoom on a selected curved line, its midpoint handle stays on the curve; before this release the midpoint was based on the endpoints, and confirm the new placement is intended.

Verify that hovering at the visual halfway point along a curved two-point line now finds its midpoint handle, whereas before this release the handle was at the endpoints' chord center, and confirm this change is intended.

Check that moving the pointer with no line being edited leaves all lines unchanged; before this release pointer movement expected an editor to be supplied, and confirm the new no-editor behavior is intended.
