report.summary: The release improves how lines and arrows are selected and edited in the drawing editor.
keyChanges: When one unlocked line or arrow is selected for point editing, the editor shows point handles instead of the usual selection box; handles are larger while editing points and use a purple color scheme.

Line and arrow resize and rotation handles are now omitted, which may also affect horizontal and vertical flipping that relies on those handles. A hovered point receives a translucent highlight without an outline.

Previously, point editing relied on an active editing state; now selecting a line or arrow—including through its context menu or a box selection containing exactly one line or arrow—enables point interaction, and releasing an edited endpoint can update its connection to a shape.

For a selected line or arrow, clicks are now tested against its actual geometry rather than its entire bounding box, so empty space inside the box no longer counts as a hit; stale point-editing state is also cleared when the element is no longer selected.
Finishing a multi-point line now selects it for point editing, and selecting all when exactly one line or arrow is selectable also opens point editing.
Point handles shrink from 20 px to 10 px, while the point hit threshold remains distance × zoom < 11 px.
Locking a selected element now clears its active point editor.
qaChecks: Verify selecting one unlocked line or arrow for point editing shows point handles instead of a selection box, and that the handles are larger while editing points and purple rather than red.

Check the point-hover highlight on a line or arrow: an unselected hovered point should show a translucent highlight without an outline, while a point already selected for editing should not receive that extra highlight.
Test horizontal and vertical flipping on the two-point diagonal arrow; each operation should visibly reverse its orientation in place.

Verify on the canvas that after you hover over a point on a line and reload the browser, the hovered-point state can return; before this release it cleared on reload, so confirm restoring it is intended.

Verify by opening a scene saved before linear-point selection was introduced that the scene still loads correctly; before this release its app state had no linear-point-selection value, while now that value defaults to empty, so confirm this compatibility behavior is intended.

Verify on the canvas that selecting a horizontal line and choosing the horizontal flip command leaves the line unchanged; before this release the line flipped, so confirm that the new result is intended.

Verify on the canvas that selecting one unlocked line while its point-selection state is active shows point handles instead of a selection bounding box; before this release it showed the bounding box, so confirm the new display is intended.

Verify on the canvas that hovering over a point on a line that is not selected for editing shows a fill-only highlight; before this release the highlight circle had an outline, so confirm removing it is intended.

Verify on the canvas that hovering over a line point that is not selected for editing displays a translucent purple highlight; before this release there was no separate highlight, so confirm the new highlight is intended.

Verify on the canvas that editing a line’s points and selecting one vertex shows larger handles with purple outlines and fill; before this release the handles were smaller and red, so confirm these changes are intended.

Verify on the canvas that deleting a selected line with visible point handles previously could leave stale line-editing behavior, and confirm that the handles and editing behavior now disappear as intended.
Verify on the canvas that right-clicking an unselected line previously selected it without enabling point handles, and confirm that the handles now appear after closing the menu.
Check on the canvas that moving over the middle of a selected, non-editing line previously did not show the line move cursor, and confirm that it now does.
Confirm on the canvas that hovering directly over a selected line’s point previously gave no point-hover feedback, and verify that the pointer cursor now appears as intended.
Verify on the canvas that pressing a point on a selected line previously did not start point editing unless the line was already being edited, and confirm that it now responds as intended.
Check on the canvas that dragging a point on a selected, non-editing line previously did not move the point, and confirm that it now moves as intended.
Verify on the canvas that clicking an unselected line previously selected it without showing point handles, and confirm that the handles now appear as intended.
Confirm on the canvas that clicking empty space inside a selected line’s bounding box previously hit the line, and verify that it no longer does.

Verify the canvas by finishing a line or arrow with multiple points; before this release it was finalized without its point editor selected, and confirm that it now remains selected for point editing as intended.

Verify Select All on a canvas containing only one unlocked line or arrow; before this release the element was selected without its point editor, and confirm that the point editor is now active as intended.
Verify locking a selected line or arrow with its point editor active; before this release the point editor remained selected after locking, and confirm that it now clears as intended.
Verify a selected line or arrow on the canvas; before this release its point handles were larger, and confirm that the smaller handles are now intended.

Verify selecting a line while the pointer is away from its vertices; before this release its hover-point status started unset until the first pointer move, and confirm that it now starts with no point hovered as intended.

Verify selecting a line without double-clicking it and dragging a point handle; before this release the point did not move unless point-editing mode was active, and confirm that it now moves as intended.
Verify selecting a line without double-clicking it and clicking one of its point handles; before this release the click did not select the point, and confirm that it now does as intended.
Verify that after selecting a line or arrow, hovering a point shows point-editing interaction and dragging that point changes its position.
Check that dragging an arrow endpoint onto the nearby shape and releasing updates the arrow’s connection to that shape.

Test the old bounding-box-only case: select a line or arrow, then click inside its bounding rectangle where there is no stroke or point; confirm that the empty area is not treated as a hit on the line or arrow.

Confirm that selecting a line or arrow through its context menu, or box-selecting exactly one line or arrow, still allows point editing; after deselecting it, ensure its point-editing state does not linger.
Verify that pressing Ctrl/Cmd+A in a drawing containing exactly one selectable line or arrow selects it for point editing.
Check that finishing a multi-point line or arrow leaves it selected for point editing.

Confirm that, with a selected line or arrow not already in point-edit mode, dragging an endpoint moves it; check that handles appear 10 px in size and a point can still be targeted within 10 screen pixels after zoom.
Ensure that locking a selected line or arrow clears its point editor, and unlocking it does not restore the cleared editor.
uncertainty: Flipping may no longer work for lines or arrows because the flip operation relies on corner handles that this change omits; confirm whether flipping these elements is still supported.
The supplied context does not document whether clicking empty space inside a line or arrow’s bounding rectangle is intended to select it; the new hit test no longer counts that space as a hit.

report.summary: The release makes importing and loading design assets more reliable across the editor and its integrations.
keyChanges: File conversion can now use a browser-compatible reading method when the usual Blob reading method is unavailable, supporting image import, file identification, and encryption.
Files without a declared type are identified by drawing or library suffix, or by PNG, JPEG, or GIF signature; supported images with a conflicting declared type are corrected.
Dropped drawings can carry their originating file access through scene restoration when the browser provides it.

Drawing-file loading now corrects a supported image file’s declared MIME type when it disagrees with the image’s actual format, so PNG drawings with misleading file types can be recognized during import.
The embeddable-editor example adds local scene or library file loading, and the file-loading helper is now publicly available to integrations.

Dropped, launched, or shared files now use a common importer that can recognize a drawing or reusable-item library by its contents, rather than relying on the dropped file’s name or MIME type to select library import.
The utility package now exposes additional file-type constants and a combined drawing-or-library importer for integrating developers.
qaChecks: Verify in that browser that dropping a supported image reads and displays it on the canvas even when the usual Blob reading method is unavailable.
Check a file with no declared type and the exact .excalidraw suffix, then a no-type file with the exact .excalidrawlib suffix; confirm the drawing loads and the library imports.
Test a no-type image containing PNG, JPEG, or GIF signature bytes, then a supported image whose declared type conflicts with its signature; confirm each image displays on the canvas.
Verify in Safari that exporting a drawing as a PNG with embedded drawing data used to fail when the browser could not read the file, and confirm the export now succeeds.
Verify in Safari that inserting the same image file twice used to create separate image entries when file reading failed, and confirm the second insertion now reuses the image as intended.
Verify that importing a PNG image mistakenly labeled as JPEG used to retain the JPEG type, and confirm it is now recognized and handled as a PNG.
Verify that dropping a PNG with a blank file type and the name image.dat used to be rejected as an image, and confirm it is now inserted as an image.

Verify in a browser with file-system support that editing a scene file dragged from your computer used to leave no way to save directly to that original file, and confirm that saving to it is now available.
Verify that opening a scene embedded in a dropped PNG used to lose the connection to the original file, and confirm the scene now retains it for saving.
Verify that opening a valid library file used to show an invalid-file error, and confirm its shapes are now imported into the library.
Verify that dropping a PNG with a blank file type and the name image.dat used to leave it unrecognized, and confirm it is now treated as an image.
Verify in Safari that encrypting a Blob-backed file used to fail when the browser could not read the file, and confirm the encrypted sharing flow now succeeds.
Verify that opening a saved-drawing PNG with no MIME type used to fail as invalid, and confirm it now loads the drawing from the image as intended.
Check the example sidebar, where there was no scene-or-library loading control before this release, and confirm the new control is intended.

Verify that selecting a library file through the new sidebar control previously was not possible, and confirm whether sending its contents to the scene updater instead of importing its items is intended.
Confirm that a project embedding the drawing component could not access this scene-or-library loading capability through the public package before this release, and that exposing it now is intended.
Verify that dropping a valid shape-library file renamed with a .txt extension previously failed as an invalid scene, and confirm it now imports the library as intended.
Verify that opening a valid shape-library file through the installed drawing app previously produced an invalid-file error, and confirm it now imports the library as intended.
Verify that loading a valid shape-library file from the app previously failed as a scene, and confirm it now imports the library as intended.
Verify that sharing a valid shape-library file to the drawing app previously failed as a scene, and confirm it now imports the library as intended.
Verify importing that image loads its embedded drawing instead of treating the file as ordinary text or rejecting it.
Verify loading the .excalidraw file updates the drawing shown in the editor.
Check that loading the .excalidrawlib file makes its reusable items available in the editor.
Verify dropping library.json imports its contents as reusable items rather than treating it as a drawing file.
Check that the same library.json is imported as reusable items when supplied through file launch or Web Share, if those entry points are available in the test environment.
Verify the integration can access the newly exposed file-type constants and the combined drawing-or-library import capability.
uncertainty: The previous behavior of the added file-normalization and file-access handling is not established by the supplied before-and-after code, so it is unclear whether type correction and retained file access differ from earlier behavior.
The example passes drawing and library data through the same scene-update call; the supplied evidence does not establish whether library items become available as expected.

report.summary: The release changes how embedded editors integrate and present footer content.
keyChanges: The Excalidraw.com app now supplies its Excalidraw+ link and encryption indicator as footer content; previously the desktop promotion was shown only to signed-in users, while the mobile footer showed the language list.
Custom footer content supplied by an embedding application is no longer passed through to the editor footer, while child content supplied to the editor is now rendered within its UI.
Footer customization changes from a callback used on desktop and mobile to child content placed in the centered desktop footer; the mobile menu no longer renders the previous custom footer callback.
A link to Excalidraw+ is now available only to signed-in Excalidraw+ users and opens in a new tab.
The editor now accepts custom footer content as child content and displays it in the centered footer region instead of using the previous footer-rendering option.
The Excalidraw+ destination is gated by the presence of the auth-state cookie, so verify its availability for both signed-in and signed-out states.
Embedding applications can now supply child content to the editor and use the package’s standard footer component as that content.
The editor no longer forwards the former custom-footer renderer, so integrations relying on that customization should verify their footer presentation.
qaChecks: Check the desktop footer with a signed-in account and then a signed-out account; confirm the Excalidraw+ promotion is shown only to the signed-in account, as before.
Check the footer at a mobile-sized viewport; confirm whether the former language list is still accessible, since its mobile-footer rendering was removed.
Verify the encryption indicator appears in the footer.
Verify supplied child content appears within the editor UI.
Check that supplied custom footer content is no longer displayed in the editor footer.
Verify an embedded drawing with a small custom child element; before this release it was not shown inside the interface layer, and now it is, so confirm this new placement is intended.

Verify an embedded drawing with a custom footer callback that displays a short message; before this release the message appeared in the center of the footer, and now it does not, so confirm this is intended.

Verify the app on a desktop browser while signed in to Excalidraw+; before this release the footer showed a “Go to Excalidraw+” link, and now the link is provided through the new footer content, so confirm its visibility and destination are intended.
Verify the app on a phone-sized screen; before this release the footer showed a language label and language choices, and now that content is no longer supplied there, so confirm this is intended.
Verify the app on a phone-sized screen and look for the language choices in the footer; before this release the choices appeared there, and now they do not, so confirm this is intended.
Verify on the desktop canvas that a plain div supplied directly as custom footer content was displayed before this release but is now missing, and confirm that ignoring it is intended.

Verify on the desktop canvas that changing the footer from empty to a footer component without changing the canvas was reflected before this release but may now leave the footer unchanged, and confirm that this is intended.
Verify on a phone that custom footer content appeared below the canvas actions before this release but is now absent, and confirm that removing it is intended.
Verify on the desktop canvas that content returned by the custom footer callback appeared in the center of the footer before this release but is now absent, and confirm that this is intended.
Verify in the app while signed in to Excalidraw+ that no direct link was present before this release but a “Go to Excalidraw+” link now appears, and confirm that this is intended.
Verify on the desktop canvas that footer content wrapped in a fragment was displayed before this release but is now missing, and confirm that not recognizing it is intended.

Verify on a page embedding the drawing that custom footer buttons supplied through the former footer-rendering option appeared before this release but now need to be supplied as child content in the centered footer, and confirm this replacement is intended.

Verify in the app that opening it without the authentication cookie and then signing in without reloading left the redirect link available before this release but may now leave it hidden, and confirm that requiring a reload is intended.
Check the app with the authentication cookie absent and confirm that the redirect link, which was visible before this release, is now hidden as intended.

Verify in a host application that embeds the drawing canvas that you can add the built-in centered footer using the package’s public imports; it was not available that way before this release, so confirm that it is now available as intended.

Verify that when you embed the drawing canvas with a custom footer callback that returns visible text, the text no longer appears in the footer area; it appeared there before this release, so confirm that this new result is intended.
Verify the custom footer content appears in the centered footer on desktop when supplied through the new child-content approach.
Check the same prior callback-based integration on a phone and confirm its custom footer content remains available in the mobile menu as before.
Verify an embedded editor supplied its footer content as child content rather than through the previous footer-rendering option displays that content centered in the footer.
Confirm the custom comment control still selects the comment tool and changes the cursor to its comment icon.
Verify a signed-in Excalidraw+ user sees the Excalidraw+ link and that selecting it opens the configured Excalidraw+ destination in a new tab.
Confirm a signed-out user does not see the Excalidraw+ link.
Verify the Excalidraw+ destination is available when the auth-state cookie is present and absent when it is missing.
Verify supplied child content, including the standard footer component, appears within the embedded editor.
Check an integration using the former custom-footer renderer and confirm its custom footer is no longer presented through that option.
uncertainty: The new Excalidraw+ link implementation is not included, so it is unclear whether signed-in-only visibility is preserved; the new location of the mobile language list is also unknown.

The previous footer callback explicitly provided content to the mobile menu, but the replacement child-content path is only shown in the centered desktop footer; confirm whether mobile footer content is still a supported integration requirement.
The evidence does not establish where supplied child content appears or the intended visible outcome when the former footer customization is no longer forwarded.

report.summary: The release standardizes how the drawing editor identifies selected objects across actions, with no broad user-visible behavior change indicated.
keyChanges: Canvas selection and selection-dependent interactions—including dragging, resizing, text editing, context menus, and color sampling—now resolve selected elements through the drawing scene.

Frame-membership and group selection also use the scene-based lookup, reaching alignment, distribution, flipping, and group workflows while retaining explicitly supplied drawing elements where needed.
Horizontal and vertical flips now supply editor scene context when updating frame membership, so an object moved outside its frame by a flip can be removed from that frame’s contents.

Adding selected objects to the Library now resolves them from the live scene and retains the existing inclusion of bound text and frame contents; no different result for ordinary selections is established by the evidence.
Both selection-to-fit zoom actions now get selected elements from the current scene; when nothing is selected, they still fit the full drawing.
Contextual editing hints on desktop and mobile now determine the selection from the current scene. No visible change to the available hints is established by the supplied evidence.
Selection lookup and editor action callbacks were redirected through the editor instance, but the supplied changes do not establish a different result for users.
The six alignment controls now determine availability from the current drawing selection; alignment remains limited to more than one selected, non-frame object.
Lock-menu wording, shortcut eligibility, and lock or unlock execution now read the current drawing selection, while retaining the existing bound-text and frame-content selection rules for execution.
Alignment now uses the active drawing scene’s selection and passes the editor context into frame-membership updates; the six edge and center alignments remain the affected operations.

Copy, cut, PNG/SVG clipboard export, and selected-text copying and eligibility now read selection through the active drawing scene, retaining the explicit inclusion of attached text and, where enabled, frame contents.

Group, ungroup, and horizontal or vertical spacing now read selected objects from the current drawing; no change to their intended visible outcomes is established when the selection and drawing state match.

Binding, unbinding, wrapping text in a container, and selecting or clearing frame contents now use the current scene’s selection instead of the element list supplied to the action; when those sources differ, the actions may target different elements.

uncertainty: The supplied changes show selection lookup being redirected and cached, but do not establish a concrete input that produces different selected elements before and after; the checks are regression coverage rather than a demonstrated behavior-change case.

The evidence does not establish a concrete user-generated input that makes live-scene selection for Library additions differ from the previous selection source, so a differential manual check cannot be derived; navigation to the Library workflow was not supplied.

The supplied evidence does not establish a concrete user input that the old selection lookup handled differently from the new scene-based lookup, so these checks cannot target a confirmed regression-triggering input.

No concrete user input that the old code handled differently from the new code can be identified from the supplied diff; affected areas and navigation were not provided, so the context-menu check is only a smoke check.

The evidence shows a difference only when the current drawing and the action-provided element list disagree; it does not identify a user action that creates this state, so a concrete ordinary manual input that distinguishes the old and new behavior is unknown.

report.summary: The release improves drawing-editor navigation and tool handling across desktop and mobile.
keyChanges: A hand tool is available in the editor controls; it pans the canvas, uses a grab cursor, and hides shape actions when nothing is selected.
Tool state now remembers the active tool under a shared value, and finishing erasing returns to that remembered tool; restored state starts with no remembered tool.
Toolbar shortcut badges now fall back to a capitalized letter when a tool has a letter shortcut but no numeric shortcut.
A hand tool control is added to the desktop and mobile toolbars, and the Help dialog now lists its H shortcut; verify the control can be selected and its active state is shown.
Shortcut keys shown in the Help dialog now capitalize the first standalone lowercase letter, while other shortcut text remains unchanged.
On mobile, the Library control moves ahead of the pen and lock controls, and the hand tool appears after them.
A hand-tool control is wired into the editor; with the hand tool active, a primary-button drag pans the canvas instead of following the normal element-creation or pointer-move editing path.
Pressing H now toggles the hand tool: entering it clears the selection and changes the cursor to grab, while leaving it restores the previous tool or falls back to selection.
The eraser now saves and restores the previous tool using the updated tool state, including when that previous tool is hand.
A saved drawing state with the hand tool selected is now allowed during restoration; previously, hand was not in the restore allowlist. No affected page or workflow was identified.
qaChecks: Verify that with no elements selected, switching to the hand tool hides shape actions and dragging the canvas pans the drawing with a grab-style cursor.
Check the eraser round trip: select a drawing tool, switch to the eraser, erase an element, and finish; the previously active drawing tool should return.
Confirm that a toolbar tool configured with a letter shortcut but no numeric shortcut displays the capitalized letter as its shortcut badge.

Verify that after selecting the hand tool, switching to the eraser, and finishing the eraser action, the app returns to the hand tool; before this release it returned to selection, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that with the hand tool selected and nothing selected, the shape actions are hidden; before this release they were shown, so confirm the new result is intended.

Confirm that after selecting the hand tool and ending a pan, moving the pointer over the canvas shows a grab cursor; before this release the previous tool's cursor could remain, so confirm the new result is intended.

Check that using the eraser after the hand tool and then finishing the eraser returns to the hand tool; before this release the hand tool could not be remembered this way, so confirm the new result is intended.
Verify that opening the help dialog now shows the hand tool with its H shortcut; before this release the tools list had no hand-tool shortcut, so confirm the new entry is intended.

Verify on a phone in view-only mode that tapping the hand control lets you pan the canvas; before this release the mobile menu could not switch into hand mode, so confirm the new behavior is intended.

report.summary: The release makes drawing and scene updates more consistent across editing, undo and redo, saving, and collaboration.
keyChanges: The editor now reuses snapshots when tracked drawing elements or app-state have not changed, while recording detected changes as store increments; verify edits and selection changes still appear correctly in undo and redo.
A new safeguard reports more than three scheduled store actions at once and throws in development and test environments; no normal user workflow for reaching that condition is established.
History handling now distinguishes capturing a new undo step from updating the current snapshot; pointer-up cleanup and color picking explicitly choose which behavior to use.
Scene changes without an explicit history choice no longer schedule a history action, unlike the previous behavior for element or app-state changes.
Importing a drawing now refreshes the existing snapshot before recording the import, intended to keep element ordering stable during undo.
Local image-status updates after saving or loading failures and refreshes from browser storage now explicitly use an update action, so verify those changes appear in the drawing.
Restoring a drawing after a hash change now uses a capture action instead of the previous commit option, and scene loading no longer explicitly opts out of store commits.

Incoming drawing changes, new-room setup, confirmed collaboration shutdown, and completed image uploads now apply an explicit update action to the scene; verify drawing synchronization and image sharing remain intact across these workflows.
Drawing updates are now committed according to scheduled actions, with capture taking priority over snapshot-only updates; clearing the store also clears pending actions.
The public action values are now lowercase, such as “update” instead of “UPDATE”, and the action constants are exported for integrations to use.
qaChecks: Verify that drawing one shape and then changing the selection updates the canvas as expected, and that undo and redo restore the drawing and selection state.

Verify that after editing or selecting a point on a line, reusing the captured app state preserves that editing or selection through the next update; before this release it could be cleared, and confirm the preserved result is intended.

Verify that when a previously captured state with a line-point selection is reused in a later update, the selection remains; before this release the captured state was not marked for reuse, and confirm this preservation is intended.
Confirm that reusing a captured app state after selecting or editing a line point keeps that state; before this release it could be treated as a full app state and lose the line-point identifiers.

Verify in a development build that rapidly overlapping updates which leave four actions pending now produce an error; before this release this check did not throw, and confirm the new failure is intended.

Verify that after making two different edits quickly, one undo reverses only the most recent edit; before this release the updates could be captured together, so confirm the separate undo result is intended.

Verify that when you draw a very short stroke and put a second finger down before lifting the first, undo no longer brings the discarded stroke back; before this release it could, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that after importing a scene with conflicting ordering positions onto a canvas with existing shapes, undo leaves the existing shapes in the correct order; before this release duplicate positions could result, so confirm the corrected ordering is intended.

Verify that when finishing a resize removes the temporary element, undo does not bring that element back; before this release the removal could be an undoable change, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that sampling a new color for a selected shape is undone in one step and restores its original color; before this release the color change was also undoable, so confirm the same result is intended.

Verify that adding a shape through the public scene-update interface without a history action leaves it in place after undo; before this release the addition was captured and undoable, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that when a collaborator update arrives while you are finishing a local edit, the next undo affects only your local edit and does not undo or absorb the collaborator's change; before this release history requests used separate flags, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that changing a selected shape's color with the eyedropper and immediately undoing restores its previous color in one step; before this release the capture flag was set directly, so confirm the scheduled capture gives the intended result.

Verify that after a collaborator moves a shape while you have a local edit pending, undo reverses your edit without reverting the collaborator's movement; before this release the snapshot-update flag was set directly, so confirm the scheduled update gives the intended result.
Verify that after adding an image and waiting for it to save, undo no longer reverses only the saved-status change, which it could do before this release, and confirm that result is intended.

Verify that after changing the saved scene in another tab and returning to the drawing tab, undo does not undo only the cross-tab refresh, which it could do before this release, and confirm that result is intended.
Verify that when an image file fails to load, undo no longer reverses only the error-status change, which it could do before this release, and confirm that result is intended.

Verify that after opening a scene from saved local data and pressing undo before editing, the result differs from the previous release, when the loaded scene was explicitly excluded from the store, and confirm the new undo behavior is intended.

Verify in a shared room that when another person adds or edits an element, it appeared on your canvas before this release and is now also reflected in the saved scene after reloading, and confirm this new result is intended.

Verify that when you start a new room from a drawing with a saved image, the image was marked for upload before this release and its pending-upload state is now reflected in the saved scene, and confirm this new result is intended.

Verify that after you confirm stopping collaboration while keeping a scene with a saved image, the image was marked for upload before this release and its pending-upload state is now reflected in the saved scene, and confirm this new result is intended.

Verify in a shared room that after you add an image and its upload finishes, it was marked as saved on the canvas before this release and its saved status is now reflected in the saved scene after reloading, and confirm this new result is intended.

Verify in a host app that imports the package through its main entry point that the store-action choices are now available there, whereas they were unavailable before this release, and confirm this new public export is intended.
Verify an integration that requests a capture using the old value "CAPTURE": before this release it matched the capture action, but the action now uses "capture"; confirm this change is intended.

Verify a host integration applies an app-state-only update with no elements supplied; before this release snapshot updates required both, and confirm that the app-state-only update now works as intended.

Verify a host integration that completes a scheduled capture through the store’s former capture operation; before this release that operation was available, and confirm the new commit flow is intended to replace it.
Verify clearing the canvas after a capture has been scheduled but before it is committed; before this release the pending capture remained, and confirm it is now discarded as intended.
Verify a host integration commits an elements-only update with app state omitted; before this release both were required, and confirm the partial update now works as intended.

Verify a collaboration integration that filters incoming updates while a shape is still being drawn locally; before this release it used the store’s former filtering operation, and confirm the renamed operation preserves the intended filtering.

Verify that a freehand stroke with at least 10 points remains when a second touch begins before the stroke ends, and that this pointer cleanup adds no separate undo step while later drawing edits remain undoable and redoable.
Check a scene change submitted without a history choice: the changed drawing should appear, no new undo step should be added for that update, and existing undo/redo should remain usable.
Confirm that choosing a visibly different color for a selected shape changes its color, Undo restores the previous color, and Redo reapplies the chosen color.
Test importing an Excalidraw drawing into a canvas that already contains objects, then Undo and Redo; confirm the drawing order remains stable and objects are not duplicated.
Verify that after an image saves locally, it remains in the drawing with its saved status.
Check that when an image file fails to load, the image remains in the drawing and receives an error status.
Confirm that restoring a previously saved drawing displays its scene.
Verify that the failed image remains in the shared drawing and receives an error status.
Verify that when one participant changes the drawing, the other participant receives and sees that scene update.
Check that starting a new collaboration session with an existing drawing makes that drawing available to the other participant.
Confirm that after stopping collaboration and accepting the override confirmation, the drawing remains visible.
Test uploading an image during collaboration and verify it remains visible to the uploader and the other participant after the upload completes.
Verify changing the shape and then undoing and redoing the change updates the drawing correctly.
Check that after clearing or reinitializing the drawing, a new shape change is recorded and remains visible.
Verify an integration replacing the former literal action value “UPDATE” with the exported StoreAction.UPDATE value “update” has its scene update applied.
uncertainty: For most changes, the supplied diff contains added code but not the prior implementation, so no concrete input that was handled differently before and after can be established; the user-visible effect of the snapshot and history updates needs confirmation.

The new scene-update option is documented as defaulting to capture, but the code schedules no history action when the option is omitted; confirm whether omission or the older history flag should still create an undo step.

The evidence does not define how the new store actions or removal of the commit opt-out affect undo history, and does not establish a concrete input that behaves differently before and after; confirm the expected history behavior.
The evidence does not explain how the explicit update action differs from the previous unspecified action, so any additional user-visible effect beyond these synchronization checks is unclear.
The supplied evidence does not establish whether integrations that still send the former uppercase literal values are supported; verify compatibility expectations for existing integrations.

report.summary: The release refines editor sidebars and library behavior, content insertion, and focus handling across standard and embedded experiences.
keyChanges: Older drawings that saved the Library sidebar as open now restore the default sidebar even when the saved dock preference is off.
The editor no longer takes focus automatically at startup unless startup focus is enabled, and library updates no longer steal focus unless the user confirms a prompt.
Embedded integrations now have a sidebar control that can toggle a named sidebar, force it open or closed, and select an optional tab.
With an empty Library and no pending drawing elements, the Library controls now include the dropdown alongside the browse link; the empty-state layout also removes its bottom border.

Library removal and reset handling now uses the dropdown controls; removing selected items should still remove them and clear the selection, while reset no longer explicitly restores focus to the editor container.
The welcome screen’s center content and help, menu, and toolbar guidance now use renamed render channels; the supplied changes do not establish a user-input case that behaves differently.
The Library content now sits within the standard sidebar, and its controls combine library browsing with actions for selected items; verify adding, inserting, and managing library items there.
When the last host-provided wrapped component unmounts, the internal fallback is now eligible to render again; previously the host preference was not reset on unmount.
The standard sidebar now uses the saved docking preference by default, while an explicit docking value without a change handler disables manual docking.

An open sidebar is now retained after pasted, dropped, or Library-inserted elements only when the default docked preference is enabled and the device can fit the sidebar, instead of checking its current docked state; the embedded-editor insertion capability places supplied elements at the canvas center.
Confirming or cancelling a clear-canvas or Library removal/reset dialog now returns focus to the editor container.
Sidebar toggling now targets a named sidebar and can select a tab, replacing the former Library or custom-sidebar toggle behavior.

Sidebar triggers now open or close the matching panel, and tab selection updates which panel content is shown; sidebar state changes are reported through the state-change notification, replacing the previous close notification on unmount.

Outside clicks and Escape close an undocked sidebar, or one that does not fit the device, unless a dialog is open; docking controls appear only when the device fits the sidebar and docking state and an action are both supplied.
Buttons now show a selected state when requested and run their supplied click action before selection; if that action prevents the default, selection no longer runs, unlike before.
The editor now renders a default sidebar and routes its library trigger through shared toolbar placements; when that sidebar is docked and open, its trigger is hidden to avoid a duplicate control.
Choosing a chart preview in the paste dialog now inserts its chart elements through the editor’s shared insertion pathway and closes the dialog.
On devices that cannot fit a sidebar, editing hints were previously hidden only when the Library sidebar was open; they are now hidden whenever any sidebar is open.

Custom sidebars are now supplied as editor children with named tabs and triggers instead of through the removed sidebar-rendering property, so verify the embedded editor still presents and controls the custom sidebar and main menu.
The sidebar header no longer renders its former dock control; its close control now sends a close request.
Sidebar triggers now open or close a named sidebar, and selecting a tab updates the active sidebar tab.
The former Library toolbar control was removed; the evidence does not show where users access the Library instead.
qaChecks: Verify an older drawing with the Library sidebar saved open and the dock preference off restores with the default sidebar open.
Verify a drawing saved with only the older Library-open setting and a docked sidebar preference still reopens the Library sidebar, as it did before.
Confirm importing a library with the sidebar requested opens the sidebar on its Library tab.
Verify the editor does not take focus from the host control when it first loads with startup focus disabled.
Check that canceling the library update confirmation leaves focus in the host control.
Confirm the embedded sidebar control can open a named sidebar and tab, force the sidebar open, and then force it closed.

Verify that with automatic focus disabled and a text field focused outside the drawing, opening the app used to move focus into the drawing but now leaves focus in the text field, and confirm this is intended.
Check an embedded drawing using the previously exposed menu-opening control; before this release it toggled a menu, and confirm the replacement sidebar control is the intended change.
Verify that restoring an older drawing with the library sidebar recorded as open and docking disabled used to leave it closed but now opens the default sidebar, and confirm this is intended.
Confirm that closing the hyperlink popup for a selected linked shape now updates the drawing state and closes the popup; before this release it had no direct state-update callback.
Verify that with automatic focus disabled, selecting a focused toolbar tool used to leave focus on the tool but now moves focus to the drawing, and confirm this is intended.
Check an unprompted library update while another control has focus; before this release completion moved focus to the drawing, and confirm that focus now remains on the other control.
Verify that restoring an older drawing with only the library-specific docking flag enabled used to retain that preference but now uses the default preference, and confirm this is intended.
Check an older drawing with the library-open flag enabled and no other sidebar setting; before this release it reopened the library, and confirm it now stays closed.

Verify that restoring an older drawing with general sidebar docking enabled used to preserve that setting and now applies it as the default docking preference, and confirm the resulting sidebar docking is intended.
Confirm that requesting the library sidebar twice without forcing it now opens and then closes that sidebar; before this release the exposed control toggled a menu instead.
Verify a screen with a button in its active state; before this release it had no active-state styling from this component, and confirm the new selected appearance is intended.
Verify the library in a floating, undocked sidebar and press Escape; before this release it closed the library, and confirm that it now staying open is intended.
Verify resetting the library from its dropdown with the keyboard; before this release focus returned to the library panel, and confirm the new focus behavior is intended.

report.summary: The release improves how users discover and control editor actions, with refreshed interaction and dialog behavior.
keyChanges: The command palette builds commands using drawing-aware labels and icons, marks unavailable commands as disabled, and supports keyboard selection and execution; running a command closes the palette and clears its search.

Shortcut lookup can now request a specific shortcut: requesting position 1 returns the second shortcut when available, otherwise it falls back to the first; previously every request returned the first.
Dialog focus is deferred until after the dialog mounts, and the close button is now shown only on fullscreen mobile dialogs.
The editor adds a command-palette entry and lists its shortcuts in Help; Ctrl+P or Cmd+P without Shift or Alt now shows a temporary shortcut hint instead of continuing to browser handling.
Canvas context-menu labels now come from each action’s current label rather than its legacy context-menu label, so entries relying only on the old label may display without text.
Double-clicking a selected line or arrow that is already being edited no longer exits early, so it continues through the editor’s remaining double-click handling.
Opening a drawing link now requests a new window without opener or referrer access; the destination still needs to open normally.
Dialogs receive a no-animation class when animations are disabled at the time the dialog first renders.
The palette opens and closes with Ctrl+/ or Ctrl+Shift+P, and its commands can be searched and run from the editor.
With a drawing element selected, the palette includes commands for changing its stroke and background colors; the relevant color controls are also shown in the selection properties when supported.

The main menu now exposes a command palette with collaboration, sharing, Excalidraw+ promotion and export, community links, and theme commands; the available Excalidraw+ entries differ for signed-in and unsigned users, and the session-ending command is limited to active sessions.
Element-lock commands now reflect the selection in their availability, label, and icon: the toggle requires a selection, while unlocking all is offered only when nothing is selected.
The sharing or collaboration dialog now closes when another editor dialog becomes active.
The command palette now includes a theme-toggle command and theme search terms; activating it runs the theme action, whose label and icon reflect the current light or dark theme.
Choosing the image command by keyboard now requests direct insertion, while choosing it by mouse selects the image tool without that request.
Canvas, alignment, hand-tool, and link actions now supply labels, names, or icons for command and action presentation; alignment eligibility and the underlying canvas operations are unchanged.
Frame, grouping, undo, and redo actions now provide labels and icons, so check that these actions are clearly identified while their existing operations remain usable.

Line editing is categorized with element commands, and its label now safely handles a missing selection instead of dereferencing it; the label still distinguishes entering from exiting line editing when a line is selected.
Editor actions now have labels and, for many commands, icons; command-palette shortcuts are added as Ctrl+Shift+P or Ctrl+/ on Windows/Linux and Command+Shift+P or Command+/ on Mac.

New keyboard shortcuts cover zoom reset and in/out, fitting the drawing or selection, eraser/hand/frame tools, saving, and showing shortcuts; object snapping is no longer available in view mode, where it was previously allowed.
Menus now remove their Escape-key listener with the same capture setting used when adding it, improving cleanup when menus close and reopen. The embedding tool is also identified as a tool action.

Registered actions across selection, editing, arranging, collaboration, and library workflows now use action labels; several also gain icons, and clipboard actions gain search keywords, so verify these controls remain recognizable and discoverable.
Save, load, project-title, and image-export controls also receive action labels or icons; the supplied changes do not alter what those operations do.
qaChecks: Verify that pressing Control/Command+P shows the command-palette hint with both configured shortcuts, with the second shortcut distinct from the first when one exists.
Check that with view mode enabled, a command unavailable in view mode is visibly disabled and clicking it does not run it.
Confirm that after running a command, reopening the palette with an empty search and pressing ArrowDown selects the last-used command; pressing Enter runs it and closes the palette.
Verify Ctrl+/ opens the palette and pressing it again closes it; also verify Ctrl+Shift+P opens it.
Check that searching for “color” with a rectangle selected offers stroke- and background-color commands, and that choosing the background-color command opens its control.
Confirm that searching the palette and choosing an available drawing command runs that command.

Verify that searching the command palette for dark, light, mode, or theme finds the theme-toggle command; activate it in light and dark themes and confirm the theme changes and the command’s indicated next theme updates.

Check the image command using the exact keyboard input: select it with a keydown event and confirm it requests direct image insertion; select it with a mouse click and confirm it activates the image tool without requesting direct insertion.
Verify that opening the dialog moves focus to its first eligible field after it appears.
Check that a desktop dialog has no top-right close button, while a fullscreen mobile dialog has a close button that dismisses it.

Verify the shortcut hint shown after pressing Command-P on a Mac includes the alternate key combination; before this release it repeated the first combination, so confirm showing the alternate is intended.

Verify that searching for a built-in action in the command palette shows it with its shortcut and selecting it runs it; before this release, actions could not be launched from this palette, so confirm this new access is intended.

Verify that opening the command palette with an element selected shows the context-sensitive action label for that selection; before this release, the palette did not provide selection-based labels, so confirm the new label is intended.

Verify that the icon for a state-dependent action reflects the current drawing when you open the command palette; before this release, the palette did not provide drawing-dependent icons, so confirm the new icon is intended.
Verify that after searching for a command and closing the palette, reopening it shows an empty search field; before this release, the search was retained, so confirm clearing it is intended.

Verify that selecting a drawing-changing command closes the palette and applies the change; before this release, you could not run that command from this palette, so confirm this new execution flow is intended.

Verify that commands from different categories appear under separate category headings in the palette; before this release, those commands were not grouped this way, so confirm the new grouping is intended.

Verify that after running a command, reopening the palette with no search and pressing Down selects that last-used command first; before this release, navigation skipped it, so confirm this new order is intended.

Verify that an editing-only command is unavailable in the palette while viewing a drawing in view mode; before this release, view mode was not checked here, so confirm hiding or disabling that command is intended.

Verify that clicking an editing-only command while in view mode does nothing and the item indicates it is unavailable; before this release, the item did not block those interactions, so confirm the disabled behavior is intended.

Verify that a command with a Control-Shift-P shortcut shows three separate keycaps; before this release, the palette did not split the shortcut into keycaps, so confirm the new presentation is intended.
Verify that opening a dialog on a desktop browser no longer shows a title-area close button; before this release, that button was present, so confirm removing it on desktop is intended.

Verify that after entering point-editing mode on a selected line or arrow, double-clicking it again without Control or Command now continues normal canvas handling; before this release it did nothing, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that clicking an external link icon in Chrome on desktop still opens the destination; before this release it opened the destination, so confirm the new result is intended if a blank tab appears.

Verify that right-clicking an element still shows the text for menu items whose wording depends on the selected element; before this release those items displayed their context-specific text, so confirm the new result is intended.
Verify that opening the help dialog now shows a Command Palette entry with its shortcuts; before this release the entry was absent, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that opening a dialog while the page’s animations-disabled setting is already active skips the modal animations; before this release the dialog used its usual animations, so confirm the new result is intended.
Verify that the Library button’s icon now appears thinner; before this release it had a thicker stroke, so confirm the new appearance is intended.
Verify that selecting Command Palette from the main menu opens it; before this release the menu had no such item, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that with one rectangle selected, searching “change background” in the command palette finds a background-color command; before this release the selected-shape panel had the control but no palette command was available, and confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that with one image selected, searching “change stroke” in the command palette finds no stroke-color command; before this release the selected-shape panel hid that control and no palette was available, and confirm the new result is intended.
Verify that opening the command palette and searching “Export image” shows an export command; before this release there was no palette to search, and confirm this new search result is intended.
Verify that after drawing a rectangle, running “Undo” from the command palette removes it; before this release there was no palette command to do this, and confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that opening the command palette without a search shows App, Export, Editor, Tools, and Elements in that order; before this release there was no palette with ordered sections, and confirm the new order is intended.
Verify that searching for “rectángle” in the command palette finds the Rectangle tool; before this release there was no palette search, and confirm that accent-insensitive matching is intended.

Verify that after making a drawing change, searching “Undo”, replacing it with “Redo”, and pressing Enter runs Redo and restores the change; before this release there was no palette keyboard flow for these commands, and confirm that using the latest search result is intended.

Verify that, as an unsigned user, searching the command palette for “GitHub” now shows an option that opens the Excalidraw GitHub page; before this release there was no GitHub option, so confirm this new result is intended.

Verify that, while signed in to Excalidraw+, selecting “Sign in / Go to Excalidraw+” in the command palette opens the Excalidraw+ app in a new tab; before this release that command was not available, so confirm this new result is intended.

Verify that, while unsigned, selecting “Excalidraw+” in the command palette opens the Excalidraw+ landing page in a new tab; before this release that command was not available, so confirm this new result is intended.
Verify that selecting the command-palette option in the hamburger menu opens the palette; before this release the option was absent, so confirm its addition is intended.

Verify on the error screen that selecting the GitHub issue link opens a separate tab that cannot access the original error page through its opener; before this release the opened tab had that access, so confirm removing it is intended.
Verify that opening the scene-loading dialog while the share dialog is open now closes the share dialog; before this release it stayed open, so confirm this new result is intended.

Verify that with no elements selected and at least one locked element, searching the command palette for “Unlock all elements” now shows the unlock action; before this release there was no such palette entry, so confirm this is intended.
Verify that selecting one unlocked shape now shows a locked-padlock icon for the lock-toggle action; before this release the action had no lock-state icon, so confirm the new icon is intended.
Verify that selecting exactly one unlocked shape now labels the action “Lock”; before this release the label did not describe the selected shape’s lock state, so confirm this new wording is intended.
Verify that with every canvas element deselected the lock-toggle action is now unavailable; before this release it remained available, so confirm this change is intended.
Verify that with a locked element on the canvas, selecting an element now hides or disables the unlock-all action; before this release it was available, so confirm this new result is intended.
Verify that with the command palette open, searching for “Align top” now shows the command with its icon, whereas before this release it had no named palette entry, and confirm this is intended.
Check that in view-only mode, searching the command palette for the hand tool no longer shows it; before this release it had no view-only restriction, and confirm hiding it is intended.
Verify that the theme action shows a moon in light theme and a sun in dark theme, whereas before this release it had no theme-dependent icon, and confirm the change is intended.
Confirm that the theme action offers dark mode in light theme and light mode in dark theme; before this release its label did not identify the mode to switch to, and confirm this is intended.
Verify that searching for the link action in the command palette now shows a link icon, whereas before this release the action had no icon, and confirm this is intended.
Check that selecting a rectangle with an existing link makes the action offer to edit it; before this release its label did not reflect the link state, and confirm this is intended.
Verify that pressing Enter on the image-tool result starts direct insertion rather than only selecting the tool, as happened before this release, and confirm this is intended.
Verify that searching for “Toggle theme” in the command palette now shows the command under App; before this release it was absent, and confirm adding it is intended.
Confirm that selecting “Toggle theme” in the palette switches the theme; before this release there was no palette command to perform that action, and confirm this result is intended.

Verify that displaying the link label with nothing selected now shows the create-link option without an error; before this release an empty selection could cause an error, and confirm this is intended.
Verify the available tools in a view-only drawing; before this release the frame tool had no explicit view-mode restriction, and confirm that it is now hidden.
Verify the command palette with two separate shapes selected; before this release the grouping action had only a context-menu label, and confirm that it now appears with a readable label.
Verify the group action in dark theme; before this release it had no supplied icon, and confirm that the new themed icon is visible and legible.
Verify the ungroup action in dark theme; before this release it had no supplied icon, and confirm that the new themed icon is visible and legible.
Verify redo in a view-only drawing after undoing a change; before this release it had no explicit view-only restriction, and confirm that it is now unavailable.
Verify undo in a view-only drawing after making a change; before this release it had no explicit view-only restriction, and confirm that it is now unavailable.
Verify the command palette’s element actions; before this release the line-editing action had no assigned category, and confirm that it now appears with the element actions.
Verify the context menu for a selected line while its points are being edited; before this release it specifically said to exit line editing, and confirm that the new label shown is intended.

Verify the command palette with nothing selected; before this release the line-editing action had no general label and an empty selection could fail label lookup, and confirm that it now displays the edit label.

Verify searching for “strasse” when the drawing contains “Straße”; before this release the search could match by expanding sharp s to “ss”, and confirm that the new single-letter normalization is intended.
Verify the slash-key shortcut on the canvas; before this release slash was not available as a recognized shortcut key, and confirm that its new shortcut behavior is intended.

Verify that, with a shape selected, searching the command palette for “Copy styles” now shows the action with a paint icon; before this release it was available from the context menu but not the palette, so confirm the new result is intended.
Check that searching the command palette for “Show grid” now finds the grid toggle; before this release it was not discoverable there, and confirm the new result is intended.
Verify that, when viewing a drawing in view-only mode, the object-snapping toggle is no longer available; before this release it was available, so confirm this change is intended.
Confirm that searching the command palette for “Toggle stats” now finds the stats toggle; before this release it was not listed there, and confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that searching the command palette for “Toggle view mode” now shows the view-mode toggle with an eye icon; before this release it was not discoverable there, so confirm the new result is intended.
Check that searching the command palette for “Toggle zen mode” now finds the toggle with a coffee icon; before this release it was not listed there, and confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that, with the top shape selected among overlapping shapes, searching the command palette for “Send backward” now shows the action with an icon; before this release it was available from the selection controls but not the palette, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that after opening and closing a dropdown menu several times, pressing Escape while it is closed does not trigger repeated close behavior; before this release, leftover handlers could accumulate, so confirm this new result is intended.

Verify that searching the command palette for the embeddable tool now finds it as a tool; before this release it had no label or tool target for this discovery route, so confirm the new result is intended.
Verify on a canvas that searching the command palette for “add to library” previously did not show the action and now does, and confirm this new search result is intended.
Verify that with a text element selected, searching the command palette for “wrap text in container” previously did not show the action and now does, and confirm this new search result is intended.
Verify with an element selected that searching the command palette for “SVG” previously did not show the copy-as-SVG action and now does, and confirm this new search result is intended.
Verify with an element selected that searching the command palette for “delete” previously did not show the delete action and now does, and confirm this new search result is intended.
Verify with three elements selected that searching the command palette for “distribute horizontally” previously did not show the action and now does, and confirm this new search result is intended.
Verify with an element selected that searching the command palette for “duplicate selection” previously did not show the action and now does, and confirm this new search result is intended.
Verify that searching the command palette for “save to disk” previously did not show the disk-save action and now does with an icon, and confirm this new result is intended.
Verify with an element selected that searching the command palette for “flip horizontally” previously did not show the action and now does with an icon, and confirm this new result is intended.
Verify that searching the command palette for “help” previously did not show the help action and now does with an icon, and confirm this new result is intended.
Verify while a collaborator is connected that searching the command palette for “Go to a collaborator” previously did not show the action and now does, and confirm this new search result is intended.
Verify with an element selected that searching the command palette for “opacity” previously did not show the action and now does, and confirm this new search result is intended.
Verify that searching the command palette for “select all” previously did not show the action and now does with an icon, and confirm this new result is intended.
Verify Ctrl+P or Cmd+P without Shift or Alt shows a temporary shortcut hint and does not open the browser’s print dialog.
Check that the default-menu command-palette entry opens the searchable list of editor commands.
Confirm Help lists the command-palette shortcuts.
Verify that the action displays its translated name in the context menu.
Check the specific case of double-clicking that same selected, already-edited line or arrow; confirm the existing point editor remains usable and no unintended drawing is added.
Verify clicking the external link opens its destination and leaves the original drawing available.
Confirm the dialog follows the no-animation setting when it first opens.
Verify the main menu provides access to the command palette and that it offers commands for collaboration, sharing, Excalidraw+ promotion and export, community links, and theme changes.
Check with no active collaboration session that searching for “stop” does not offer the session-ending command; start a session and confirm it becomes available and ends the session when selected.
Confirm the Excalidraw+ entries differ by account state: unsigned users see promotion and sign-up options, while signed-in users see one combined sign-in or destination option.
Test the Excalidraw+ export command with a drawing containing an image and confirm the export flow receives the current drawing and its image.

Verify with nothing selected and a locked element present that the unlock-all action is available and the selection toggle is unavailable; select the unlocked element and confirm the toggle indicates locking, then indicates unlocking after the element is locked.
Check the specific case where the unlocked element is selected while a different element is locked: the unlock-all action should not be offered, even though a locked element remains in the drawing.
Verify that when another editor dialog becomes active while the sharing or collaboration dialog is open, the sharing or collaboration dialog closes.
Confirm that alignment actions are available for two selected non-frame elements and that their action presentation has labels and icons; do not expect alignment eligibility to change.
Verify that canvas background, clear-canvas, zoom, hand-tool, and link actions provide their updated action presentation; confirm their existing canvas operations remain available.
Verify that selecting one frame offers the frame-related actions with clear labels, and that selecting all frame contents and removing all frame contents still work.
Check that selecting two elements offers clearly identified group and ungroup actions, and that grouping then ungrouping restores the separate elements.
Confirm that after making an edit, undo reverses it and redo restores it, with both actions clearly identified.
Verify that with a line selected, the command label distinguishes entering line editing from exiting it, and that invoking the command enters and exits line editing.
Check the command palette with no element selected; it should remain usable without an error, and the line-editing command should not be offered.
Verify Ctrl+Shift+P or Ctrl+/ on Windows/Linux, and Command+Shift+P or Command+/ on Mac, opens the searchable command palette; confirm searches can find the newly labeled editor actions.

Check Ctrl/Cmd+0 resets zoom, Ctrl/Cmd+- zooms out, and Ctrl/Cmd++ zooms in; confirm Shift+1 fits the drawing, Shift+2 fits the selected elements in the viewport, and Shift+3 fits the selected elements.
Confirm E, H, and F activate the eraser, hand, and frame tools respectively; verify Ctrl/Cmd+S saves and ? opens the shortcuts view.
Verify that with view mode enabled, object snapping cannot be toggled; this mode previously allowed the action.
Check that pressing Escape dismisses an open menu after it has been closed and reopened.
Verify available controls for selection, copying, deletion, duplication, formatting, arranging, and library actions identify their purpose, with icons where supplied.
Check the help, menu, and collaborator-follow actions remain identifiable in their available editor controls.
Confirm save, load, project-title, and image-export controls remain identifiable, and that export settings for scale, background, embedded scene, and dark mode still identify their purpose.
uncertainty: Desktop dialogs no longer show a close button, and the supplied evidence does not establish whether every affected dialog has another clear way to close.

The supplied context does not identify how to enable disabled animations or confirm their visible effect, and it does not establish the exact outcome of the newly continued double-click handling beyond the fact that it no longer returns early.
The supplied changes contain additions rather than removed behavior for the palette, so they do not establish a concrete input that worked before but behaves differently now.

Unlock-all was previously available when any element was locked, including while an element was selected; it is now unavailable whenever anything is selected, and the supplied context does not establish whether that restriction is intended.

The supplied context gives no navigation or affected-page mapping for these capabilities, and the image-command change has no previous implementation in the supplied diff, so its prior user-visible behavior cannot be confirmed.
The new text-normalization helper and slash-key constant have no supplied user-facing usage path, so their release effect cannot be confirmed from this group.

The changes only update action labels, icons, and clipboard search keywords; no input-specific change in operation behavior is evident. The supplied context does not establish where these labels and icons appear, so their exact on-screen placement and navigation remain unclear.
