report.summary: The release improves how elbow arrows are routed, styled, edited, and kept connected to shapes as drawings change.
keyChanges: Elbow arrows now use shape direction and bounds to choose connection points, snap dragged endpoints toward shape midpoints, and recalculate routes around drawing elements; this can affect drawing, editing, resizing, rotating, and flipping connected diagrams.
While dragging an elbow-arrow endpoint, points inside a shape’s bounding box can now count as a connection target, even when they are away from its outline.
Elbow arrows now draw rounded bends with a maximum 16-pixel radius, limited to half the length of each adjoining segment; rectangular corner connections are offset by 5 pixels.
New arrows default to the round style, while elbow connectors use an updated obstacle-aware routing path.
Undo and redo now refresh bound arrows using the current drawing, so connector paths should follow restored shape positions.

Elbow arrows now route around shapes and snap their endpoints to connected shapes; editing is focused on the two endpoints, not the intermediate bends, and their point placement no longer follows the grid.

A single elbow arrow connected at either end no longer moves when dragged or nudged with an arrow key, and a connected elbow arrow cannot be resized; grouped transforms can reroute elbow arrows instead of treating them as ordinary lines.

Arrow selections now offer arrow-type controls, elbow arrows no longer offer the line editor, and arrows no longer offer roundness; with the arrow tool active, the hint identifies the A shortcut and pressing A cycles sharp, round, and elbow arrow types.
Opening the editor for a linear element no longer normalizes its points; it only reports an unnormalized element.

Elbow arrows now use fixed attachment points when their connected shapes move or resize, and copying a connection preserves those points; check that the connector stays attached to the same locations.
Elbow arrows no longer show rotation handles or a selection bounding box, and their interior route points are hidden while editing; only endpoint handles remain visible.
Elbow-arrow routing avoids rectangular-shape corners, and the binding highlight now has a fixed 10-pixel thickness instead of varying with the shape’s binding gap.
Negative angles now convert to degrees by adding 360 once, so -90° converts to 270°.
Elbow arrows no longer have an angle control in the Stats panel, while position and size edits now pass the current drawing through connection updates.
Restored elbow-arrow bindings receive a default fixed point of [0, 0] when none was saved, while non-elbow bindings have their fixed point cleared.
Arrow conversion now uses arrow-specific creation and preserves the arrow’s elbowed setting when restoring it.
Arrows can now be set to sharp, round, or elbow styles; changing a bent arrow to another style keeps its endpoints and removes intermediate bends.
Elbow arrows use routed paths and shape-attached endpoints, and are excluded from the ordinary roundness and linear-editing controls.
Moving or resizing connected elements and flipping selected arrows now refreshes their connections using the drawing’s current elements.
Elbow arrows now use unsnapped canvas positions even when grid snapping is enabled, and a third click after setting their two endpoints finalizes them rather than adding another point.
Deleting a shape connected to an elbow arrow clears that connection and recalculates the arrow route; undo and redo now recalculate connected arrows as drawing changes are restored or reapplied.
qaChecks: Verify dragging an arrow endpoint to within 5 px of the midpoint line of a 100-by-100 rectangle snaps the connection toward the midpoint and keeps it attached.
Check an elbow arrow connecting two shapes with a third shape between them routes around the intervening shape rather than through it.
Confirm a connected arrow remains attached and reroutes after rotating the diamond, editing the arrow’s points, resizing the shapes, and flipping the selection.

Verify on the canvas that dragging an elbow-arrow endpoint near the middle of a shape’s edge, with the other endpoint diagonally across the canvas, changes its direction as described; before this release it did not use the nearby edge this way, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify on the canvas that dragging an arrow endpoint inside a rectangle while the other endpoint is to its right snaps it near the right-edge midpoint; before this release it did not snap there, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify on the canvas that dragging an arrow endpoint close to the middle of a large rectangle’s edge snaps it to the midpoint; before this release it did not use a size-based midpoint snap, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify on the canvas that an arrow attached from directly above a shape uses the upward edge consistently; before this release direction matching did not require an exact coordinate match, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify on the canvas that an elbow arrow approaching a diamond from above and to its right at an angle between 45 and 135 degrees binds with a rightward direction; before this release it was not classified with these angle ranges, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify on the canvas that an elbow arrow approaching a rotated rectangle just beyond its upper-right corner chooses the direction for that region; before this release it did not use these search regions, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify on the canvas that an exactly diagonal arrow segment is treated as upward when its direction is evaluated; before this release it was not classified using this tie-breaking rule, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify on the canvas that an elbow arrow connecting two shapes around a third shape avoids passing through it and favors the route with fewer bends; before this release routing did not apply these checks and penalties, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify on the canvas that an elbow arrow with two consecutive shallow-angle segments pointing in the same cardinal direction loses the redundant bend; before this release those segments were not merged this way, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify on the canvas that an elbow arrow leaving its first shape horizontally and entering its second vertically routes around an obstacle between them; before this release the grid did not include these direction-based coordinates, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify on the canvas that an elbow arrow routing around two obstacles on opposite sides considers the full space they span; before this release their shared area was not calculated from both outermost bounds, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify on the canvas that an elbow arrow connecting a lower-left shape to an upper-right shape can route around both shapes; before this release routing did not adjust and split the obstacle areas for this arrangement, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify on the canvas that rerouting an attached elbow arrow while its shape is being moved follows the shape’s current position; before this release routing used the existing scene list without the changed version, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify on the canvas that an attached elbow arrow rerouted during a shape move uses the shape’s current position rather than its old position; before this release the routing map used the old version, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify on the canvas that dragging an unbound elbow-arrow endpoint toward a shape from just outside its edge chooses an appropriate approach direction; before this release it did not use bounds expanded by the binding distance, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify on the canvas that after deleting a shape attached to an elbow arrow, rerouting does not attach the arrow to that deleted shape; before this release target resolution did not explicitly reject a missing or non-bindable target, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify on the canvas that a downward-facing binding handle appears on the bottom edge of its shape; before this release its position was not chosen using this direction-to-edge mapping, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify on the canvas that dragging an elbow-arrow endpoint over the middle of a shape’s edge snaps it there and that resizing a bound shape updates an endpoint that is no longer the required distance away; before this release these cases did not use these updates, so confirm the new results are intended.

Verify on the canvas that rerouting an arrow with no external offset keeps its first point at the arrow’s position and preserves the remaining path; before this release omitted offsets were not handled with this normalization, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify on the canvas that an elbow arrow leaving the right edge keeps the requested larger clearance on that side; before this release the clearance was not assigned using this mapping, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify on the canvas that an endpoint positioned just a fraction away from a route-grid intersection does not get treated as exactly on it; before this release lookup did not require exact coordinate equality, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify on the canvas that an elbow arrow routes around the full extent of a rectangle rotated 45 degrees; before this release the bounds did not use the rotated corners, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify on the canvas that two rectangles touching exactly along an edge are treated as touching rather than overlapping; before this release boundary points were not excluded by this strict test, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify on the canvas that an arrow from 100,100 to 110,100 is treated as pointing right when its direction is evaluated relative to its starting point; before this release the conversion did not use that supplied origin, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify on the canvas that a point above a shape’s center moves twice as far from that center when its distance is doubled; before this release scaling did not use the chosen center, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify on the canvas that reversing an elbow-arrow direction vector with a negative scale makes it point the opposite way; before this release vector scaling did not apply this multiplication, so confirm the new result is intended.
Verify that binding an arrow endpoint near the top-left corner of a rectangle used to snap it to the corner and now offsets it from an adjoining edge, and confirm this new placement is intended.
Verify that moving a shape with an attached arrow endpoint used to leave the endpoint behind and now moves it with the shape, and confirm this correction is intended.
Verify that dragging an elbow-arrow endpoint into the middle of a rectangle used to miss it and now detects it, and confirm this new interior binding behavior is intended.
Verify that dragging an arrow end onto a newly added shape used to leave it unbound and now binds to it, and confirm this change is intended.
Verify that dragging an arrow shaft or middle joint near a newly added shape used to leave the endpoint unbound and now considers that shape, and confirm this change is intended.

Verify that rotating a selection with an elbow arrow attached at both ends used to move the arrow without preserving its attachment points and now keeps those points attached, and confirm this is intended.
Verify that an elbow-arrow endpoint just beyond a shape’s binding gap used to keep the near-edge heading and now uses the direction toward the shape’s center, and confirm this change is intended.
Verify that binding an arrow to the upper-right sloping area of a diamond used to choose a different side and now selects the side for that region, and confirm this is intended.
Verify that snapping an arrow to the midpoint of a very large rectangle used to accept a wider range of pointer positions and now uses a capped range, and confirm this is intended.
Verify that an elbow arrow with a very short segment used to render a sharper turn and now rounds the turn only as far as the segment allows, and confirm this is intended.
Verify that binding an arrow near a corner of a rotated shape used to choose a heading without using the bounds midpoint and now chooses one using that midpoint, and confirm this is intended.

Verify that resizing or rotating a shape at a nonzero canvas position used to calculate its geometry without this translation and now shifts the geometry by the requested offset, and confirm this is intended.
Verify that binding at a point exactly on a diamond’s sloping boundary used to choose one side and now may choose the neighboring side, and confirm this boundary result is intended.
Verify that an elbow arrow with a right-angle turn used to render with the generic path and now renders with rounded elbow turns, and confirm this new appearance is intended.
Verify that an elbow arrow with a long segment followed by a short segment used to have a sharp turn and now has a rounded turn limited by the short segment, and confirm this is intended.

Verify that after moving a shape with an attached elbow arrow, undoing, and redoing, the arrow follows the restored shape; before this release its route could remain stale, so confirm the refreshed route is intended.

report.summary: The release changes how the editor tracks and restores drawing changes.
keyChanges: Text attached to a rotated shape now follows the shape’s angle when its text layout is redrawn, so verify the text remains aligned after editing or resizing.
Connection cleanup and restoration now handle attached text and arrows during deletion and drawing changes; undo and redo should leave connections consistent.
Text editing, text formatting, binding, deletion, style pasting, and copy/export actions now use the editor’s store-action controls, making history behavior the main visible check for these updates.

Undo and redo now use recorded drawing and app-state changes; an app-state-only change such as changing the background color should no longer discard redo, while a drawing-element change still clears redo.
Grouping and ungrouping now capture their changes in the editor’s store, so verify that both operations remain reversible and preserve the grouped elements’ drawing order.
Loading a scene after a non-library hash change now commits the restored scene to the store; verify that the scene is restored intact.
Undo and redo controls now disable when their respective history stacks are empty, instead of remaining enabled when there is nothing to reverse or reapply.

Undo and redo now apply changes using the current drawing and saved snapshot; verify that drawing elements, selection, and links between elements remain consistent when changes are reversed and reapplied.

Undo and redo now apply scene and selection changes together, filtering selections and editing state that refer to deleted elements; verify that visible drawing changes still reverse and reapply correctly.
Applying drawing changes now accounts for restored elements, element ordering, connector bindings, and text attached to shapes, so these relationships need checking during history use.

Scene snapshots now track observed selection and editing state as well as element changes, including elements missing from a later scene; verify that restoring or changing a drawing does not leave stale selections or bindings.
Pasting or inserting items, erasing, recoloring, editing lines, and changing frame selection now use the revised change-recording process, affecting what undo and redo restore.
Scene updates now use a store-commit setting instead of the previous history-commit setting; local updates without the new setting may not be undoable.
When a drawing file is imported into an existing drawing, element ordering is synchronized before the imported content is applied.
Live collaboration no longer clears the undo history when a peer’s scene update arrives, so existing local undo and redo should remain available.

Drawing edits, clearing and loading a scene now request history capture, while view, theme, export, and save-state changes request no capture; verify these actions retain their expected undo behavior.
The zoom-in control is disabled at 3000% and the zoom-out control at 10%.
Finalizing a drawing now captures a history state for non-freehand tools too; previously, finalization was recorded only for freehand, so completing a line or shape can now affect Undo and Redo.
Entering or leaving line-point editing is now captured for history, and finalizing that edit clears the selected line-editing state.
Undo and redo now apply against the current drawing and store snapshot; clipboard, library, and editor-mode actions use explicit no-store updates instead of history flags.
Aligning, distributing, duplicating, locking, flipping, and changing layer order now request a captured store update, while opening or closing menus and the help dialog requests no capture.
Duplicating elements now synchronizes moved ordering indices using the duplicated elements only, rather than both the originals and duplicates.

New snapshot bookkeeping exposes snapshot state and marks snapshot or increment updates; reconciliation removes previously unseen pending elements and restores a snapshot version when it is older than the prior local version.

uncertainty: The supplied context does not identify navigation steps or visible labels for the editor, so the tester must locate the canvas through their available application entry point.

The old history explicitly excluded an unfinished line or arrow with only one point and omitted an uncommitted last point, but the supplied evidence does not establish how the new history handles those in-progress points; verify the draft-point check and clarify whether its undo behavior is intended to remain unchanged.

The supplied evidence does not include before-versions of the history change-calculation routines, so it does not establish which linked-element or later-edit edge cases behave differently; verify linked-element undo and redo without assuming a specific failure.

The supplied changes contain no removed-code versions, so the previous behavior cannot be compared to the new behavior to identify a concrete input that changed paths; the checks above cover the new behavior, but a specific regression-triggering old input cannot be established.
The effect of overlapping local and collaborator updates on undo history is not established, so confirm the intended result for concurrent changes.
The supplied evidence does not define the new store-capture policy, so it cannot confirm whether all migrated history behavior is preserved; prioritize the undo and redo checks above.

The prior behavior of the newly added array-to-object conversion is not included, so the supplied evidence does not identify an exact input that previously worked but may now merge distinct entries in drawing history.
The supplied evidence does not show an input where changing the edit-capture flags alters the old behavior, and it supplies no user-facing route for checking the new snapshot-reconciliation helpers.

report.summary: The release makes canvas selection and related interactions more consistent across devices, especially for touch users.
keyChanges: On devices detected as mobile or tablet, the default selection tool is now lasso; adding drawing items from the Library, pasting, finishing text entry, or finishing certain drawing actions returns to that default instead of always switching to standard selection.

Lasso pointer handling now supports immediate selection of a tapped object on mobile or tablet and permits dragging it; on desktop, starting a lasso on empty canvas blocks dragging until the next pointer-down.

Ctrl+Alt pointer-down from selection now starts lasso selection and closes an open element-link dialog; context-menu and double-click handling also accept the device’s default selection tool, including lasso on mobile or tablet.

When lasso is the default selection tool, it takes the primary selection-tool position, the separate lasso menu item is hidden, and keyboard shortcuts and returns from laser mode or unlocking use lasso.
On mobile and tablet, pasted drawing elements are placed at the canvas center instead of the pointer; desktop paste placement remains at the pointer.
With lasso active and no elements selected, hovering over an element no longer shows the move cursor; selected elements can still show it.
When a drawing opens on a mobile or tablet device, a saved selection, lasso, or image tool is replaced by lasso; canceling image insertion also returns to lasso instead of standard selection.

Canvas actions that previously returned to standard selection now use the configured default selection tool, including clearing while the image tool is active, exiting the eraser without a saved prior tool, deleting selected elements, and finalizing; the lasso-toggle action is suppressed when lasso is already the default.
Snapping was previously disabled whenever lasso was active; it is now enabled while selected elements are being dragged, but remains off during lasso selection.
iOS platform matching is now case-insensitive, and mobile detection recognizes additional browser and platform identifiers; this may affect device-specific resize and rotation controls.
qaChecks: Verify on a touch-oriented device that, with the default lasso tool active, touching and dragging an unselected object selects it immediately and moves it; the object should not be displaced by lasso selection instead.

Check on desktop that with lasso active, pointer-down on empty canvas followed by a drag makes a lasso selection without moving selected objects, and that a new pointer-down permits subsequent dragging.

Confirm that Ctrl+Alt pointer-down and drag from standard selection starts a lasso outline and selects objects within it; if the element-link dialog is open, confirm it closes as lasso selection starts.

Verify on mobile or tablet that long-pressing the canvas opens the context menu and that double-clicking while the default lasso tool is active reaches the normal selection-mode double-click handling.
Verify that after pasting drawing items or inserting them from the Library, the default lasso tool is active rather than standard selection.
Check that after creating text and after finishing a newly drawn object, the editor returns to the default lasso tool on mobile or tablet.
Verify on a mobile device that uses lasso by default, paste an element and confirm that the app now switches to lasso instead of regular selection, as intended.
Verify on a mobile device with lasso active that long-pressing the canvas now opens the context menu, whereas it did not before, and confirm this is intended.
Verify on a mobile device with lasso active that double-tapping an existing text element now performs its double-click action, whereas it was ignored before, and confirm this is intended.
Verify on a mobile device or tablet with lasso active that tapping an unselected element now selects it immediately, rather than only starting a lasso trail as before, and confirm this is intended.

Verify with regular selection active that holding Ctrl and Alt while pressing on an element now starts a lasso trail and switches to lasso mode, whereas it did not before, and confirm this is intended.
Verify on a mobile device that uses lasso by default that starting text now leaves lasso active instead of regular selection, as intended.

Verify on a touchscreen tablet or convertible computer that the app now defaults to lasso instead of regular selection, whereas it previously could default to regular selection, and confirm this is intended.
Verify on a desktop that dragging a selected element while lasso is active now moves it, whereas it could not be moved before, and confirm this is intended.
Verify on a mobile device that uses lasso by default that completing a shape now switches to lasso instead of regular selection, as intended.
Verify that with lasso set as the default selection tool, lasso is absent from the extra-tools menu; before this release it was there, so confirm that removing it is intended.
Check that with lasso active and nothing selected, hovering over a shape no longer shows a move cursor; before this release it did, so confirm that this new cursor behavior is intended.

Confirm that with lasso active, no elements selected, and a line’s point-editing handles still visible, hovering over its body no longer shows a move cursor; before this release it did, so confirm that the change is intended.

Verify that pressing K while laser mode is active switches to lasso when lasso is the default selection tool; before this release it switched to the regular selection tool, so confirm the new result is intended.
Check that on a phone or tablet, pasted elements appear at the canvas center rather than at the pointer; before this release they appeared at the pointer, so confirm the new placement is intended.
Verify that an empty scene shows the welcome screen when lasso is the default selection tool and is active; before this release it did not, so confirm that showing it now is intended.
Confirm that unlocking a drawing tool switches to lasso when lasso is the default selection tool; before this release it switched to the regular selection tool, so confirm the new result is intended.
Verify that pressing V selects lasso when it is the default selection tool; before this release it selected the regular selection tool, so confirm the new shortcut behavior is intended.

Check that the main toolbar shows lasso instead of the regular selection tool when lasso is the default selection tool; before this release it showed the regular selection tool, so confirm this replacement is intended.
Verify on a phone or tablet that opening the app now starts with the lasso tool instead of the standard selection tool as before, and confirm this is intended.

Check on a desktop browser that opening a saved scene with the lasso tool active now switches to the standard selection tool, whereas it kept the lasso tool active before, and confirm this is intended.
Confirm that on a phone or tablet, cancelling the image file picker now returns to the lasso tool instead of the standard selection tool as before, and that this is intended.

Verify in Excalidraw on an Android phone that mobile-specific behavior is applied; before this release the shared device detection did not identify Android as mobile, so confirm the new Android behavior is intended.

Verify that with the default selection tool set to lasso, activating the image tool and clearing the canvas returns to lasso; before this release it returned to regular selection, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that when the default selection tool is lasso and no previous tool is remembered, turning off the eraser switches to lasso; before this release it switched to regular selection, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that with lasso set as the default selection tool, the lasso-toggle action is unavailable in the tool controls; before this release it remained available, so confirm the new result is intended.
Verify that with the default selection tool set to lasso, deleting a selected shape switches to lasso; before this release it switched to regular selection, so confirm the new result is intended.
Verify that with the default selection tool set to lasso, finishing a rectangle switches to lasso; before this release it switched to regular selection, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that with object snapping enabled, dragging lasso-selected elements near another element’s alignment produces a snap; before this release lasso-tool dragging did not snap, so confirm the new result is intended.
Verify that lasso occupies the primary selection-tool position and is not also listed as a separate extra tool.
Check that pressing 1 activates lasso, rather than the regular selection tool.
Confirm that pressing K to exit laser mode, or unlocking a locked tool, returns to lasso.
Ensure the welcome screen appears on an empty drawing when lasso is the active default selection tool.
Verify that hovering over an unselected element with lasso active does not show the move cursor, while hovering over a selected element can still show it.
Test pasting copied drawing elements with the pointer away from the canvas center; verify they are placed at the center rather than at the pointer.
Verify that opening the saved drawing on a mobile or tablet activates lasso selection instead of the saved standard selection, and that dragging around drawing elements selects them.
Check that starting image insertion and canceling the file picker on a mobile or tablet returns to lasso selection, and that drawing elements can still be selected by lasso.
Verify that with lasso as the configured default and the image tool active, clearing the canvas leaves lasso active; confirm the lasso-toggle action is suppressed when lasso is already the default.
Check with lasso as the default and no saved prior tool: switch the eraser on and then off, and complete a finalized editor interaction; each returns to lasso rather than standard selection.
Confirm that deleting selected elements, including via cut, removes them and leaves the configured lasso default active.

Test with lasso active, selected elements being dragged, object snapping enabled, and no modifier key: dragging near another element aligns to it and shows snap guides; lasso-selecting without dragging selected elements does not snap.

Verify that selected-element resize and rotation controls follow the iOS-specific layout when the platform value is lowercase iphone; the previous case-sensitive match did not identify this value as iOS.
uncertainty: The supplied context does not identify a navigation path or specific devices for QA; mobile behavior requires a device detected as mobile or tablet, including touch capability with a coarse pointer.

The supplied context does not explain how to configure the default selection tool or produce a lowercase iOS platform value, so those edge cases may require a specially configured editor or browser test setup.

report.summary: The release adds lasso selection to the editor and updates related selection and drawing interactions.
keyChanges: Shape geometry used for hit-testing now follows curves, rounded corners, rotated sides, and a 90-segment ellipse outline instead of the earlier coarse ellipse and bounding-edge segments; this can change which shapes lasso paths and frames touch.

Lasso selection now refreshes enclosed elements as the path changes, checks path intersections with a tolerance of 1, and normalizes selection so bound text selects its container and selected frames exclude their children.

Lasso feedback is now an animated dashed stroke; its displayed path uses only the outline points from index 6 up to half the outline, and completed trail paths are cleared during updates and when the lasso ends.
When the lasso is activated with selection retention enabled, existing selected elements and groups remain selected; otherwise the previous selection is cleared.
Newly drawn shapes no longer resize from their starting point when the center-resize modifier is held; they remain anchored at the pointer-down point.
While dragging a selection box, holding Alt switches the gesture to lasso selection; releasing Alt during the drag returns to box selection.

Lasso gestures update the selection as the pointer moves: starting without Shift clears the existing selection, while holding Shift preserves it; the lasso trail and its selection tracking are cleared when a gesture ends or a new one starts.
Restored drawing state now recognizes lasso as an active tool, so a drawing saved with lasso active should retain that tool when restored.
Line-intersection checks can now accept an explicit tolerance; the supplied in-app callers omit it, so they keep the previous default behavior.
The lasso tool can be activated from the toolbar or command palette, and the toolbar reflects the active lasso tool with its own icon.
When lasso mode is active, releasing Space now resets the cursor without clearing the current selection; without a selection, selected-shape actions are hidden.
The deep-selection and empty-canvas hints now use list formatting, which removes a final period from their displayed text.

A new lasso tool can be activated from a non-lasso tool or toggled back to selection when already active; activating it clears the current element and group selections, and a lasso path selects elements it encloses or intersects.
Several existing actions lose their dedicated command-palette names; the supplied evidence does not establish how this affects finding those actions.
qaChecks: Verify a small closed lasso loop centered inside an ellipse does not select it when the loop crosses the ellipse's former center-spanning segments but not its outline.
Check a lasso path that crosses the visible curved outline of an ellipse selects it, including where the curve falls between the old coarse segments.
Confirm that as the lasso path changes and no longer encloses an element, that element is no longer selected unless the path intersects it.
Validate that lassoing bound text selects its container rather than the text alone, and lassoing a frame does not separately select its children.
Verify a very short lasso gesture around the small element shows lasso feedback while drawing and still selects the enclosed element when the gesture ends.
Check that a lasso activation that retains an existing selection leaves that element selected, while an activation without selection retention clears the previous selection.
Verify shapes whose visible curved outlines cross the frame edge are treated as intersecting it.
Check that a lasso or frame interaction confined to the empty area of a rounded rectangle's corner does not treat that area as part of the visible shape.

Verify on the canvas that lassoing a standalone text label with no container uses the new rectangle-like outline; before this release it used the generic outline, and confirm the new result is intended.
Verify by lassoing across a curved freehand stroke that selection follows the curve; before this release its boundary followed the stored stroke points, and confirm the new result is intended.

Verify by lassoing along a rectangle rotated 45 degrees that its sides are detected in the rotated position; before this release its boundary came from the generic outline calculation, and confirm the new result is intended.

Verify by lassoing only across a rounded rectangle's curved corner that the corner is detected; before this release the outline treated that corner as straight, and confirm the new result is intended.

Verify by lassoing across the middle of a wide ellipse's top edge that it is selected; before this release the boundary used duplicated cardinal-point segments, and confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that moving a lasso around an element selects it before you release the pointer; before this release selection did not read the current trail through this accessor during the gesture, and confirm the new result is intended.
Verify by lassoing a frame and the shape inside it that only the frame is selected; before this release both could remain selected, and confirm the new result is intended.

Verify by drawing a lasso that contains just one boundary point of a shape that the shape is treated as enclosed; before this release partial containment was not classified that way, and confirm the new result is intended.

Verify by drawing a lasso around a shape and then moving the in-progress path away so it no longer encloses it that the shape is no longer selected as enclosed; before this release an earlier enclosure could remain recorded, and confirm the new result is intended.

Verify by drawing a lasso edge just under one drawing unit from a shape without touching it that the shape is selected; before this release the near miss was not an intersection, and confirm the new result is intended.
Verify that after finishing a lasso stroke the trail disappears immediately; before this release it remained visible to fade out, so confirm the immediate clearing is intended.
Verify that a lasso stroke now shows a moving dashed line; before this release it had no animated dash treatment, so confirm this new appearance is intended.
Check a very short lasso drag; before this release its complete trace was drawn, and now it may disappear, so confirm that result is intended.
Verify that a lasso stroke now has a purple outline around its pale fill; before this release it had no separately colored outline, so confirm the outline is intended.
Verify that beginning a second laser-pointer stroke clears the first before it fades; before this release both strokes could remain visible together, so confirm clearing the first is intended.
Confirm that a fresh drawing now starts with the selection-origin setting explicitly false; before this release that setting was absent, so verify the new default is intended.
Verify that holding Alt while dragging a new generic shape no longer draws it outward from its center; before this release it did, so confirm drawing from the starting point is intended.
Verify that switching to the lasso tool through the keep-selection action preserves selected elements; before this release switching tools cleared them, so confirm retaining them is intended.

Verify that a long lasso drag now shows a pale purple trail with a purple outline that tapers along its length; before this release it used the ordinary trail appearance and sizing, so confirm the new styling is intended.

Verify that after starting a temporary lasso with Alt-drag and then choosing the lasso tool directly, dragging without Alt keeps lasso selection active; before this release the lasso could switch back to rectangle selection, and confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that an already selected element stays selected while the lasso tool is active and an interaction clears selection for other tools; before this release it was cleared, and confirm retaining it is intended.
Verify that choosing the lasso tool and pressing down on an empty canvas starts a stroke at that point; before this release no lasso stroke started, and confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that during a rectangle-selection drag, holding and then releasing Alt changes the drag from lasso back to rectangle selection; before this release Alt did not change the drag, and confirm the new result is intended.
Verify that after completing and releasing an unlocked lasso gesture, the lasso tool remains active; before this release the tool reset to rectangle selection, and confirm the new result is intended.
Verify that dragging with the lasso tool shows a visible stroke on the canvas; before this release no lasso trail was rendered, and confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that with an element already selected, drawing a lasso while holding Shift keeps that selection as new points are added; before this release lasso movement did not update selection or preserve it, and confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that after finishing a lasso and starting another in a different area, the old stroke does not remain or affect the new selection; before this release there was no lasso-path cleanup, and confirm the new result is intended.
Verify that starting a lasso without Shift clears a previously selected element; before this release there was no lasso-start selection change, and confirm the new result is intended.
Verify that drawing a lasso across a visible shape selects it before you release the pointer; before this release the path did not select elements, and confirm the new result is intended.
Verify that opening a saved scene with lasso active previously restored another tool, and confirm that it now restores with lasso active as intended.

Check the line-intersection test with segments from (0, 0) to (10, 0) and (10.5, -1) to (10.5, 1), using a threshold of 1; it previously reported no intersection, so confirm that it now reports the intersection at (10.5, 0) as intended.
Verify on the canvas with the lasso tool active and no elements selected that the selected-shape actions are now hidden, whereas before this release they could appear, and confirm this is intended.
Verify in the canvas toolbar that choosing the lasso option from the extra-tools menu activates it; before this release the menu had no lasso option, so confirm this addition is intended.
Verify on the canvas that dragging a closed path with the lasso tool shows a trail; before this release no lasso trail handler was created at startup, so confirm this new trail is intended.

Verify on the canvas that after selecting an element and releasing the space bar with the lasso tool active, the selection remains; before this release it was cleared, so confirm preserving it is intended.
Verify in the command palette that searching for the lasso tool finds a command that activates it; before this release no such command was listed, so confirm this addition is intended.

Verify on the desktop canvas with nothing selected that a panning hint ending in a period now appears without that period; before this release it retained the period, so confirm the changed punctuation is intended.
Verify in the extra-tools menu that the embed icon now looks thicker than before this release, and confirm this visual change is intended.
Verify on the canvas that activating the lasso tool changes the pointer to a crosshair; before this release there was no lasso tool to activate, and confirm this new result is intended.
Check the command palette in a non-English language and compare the clear-canvas action with the old fixed English name “Clear canvas”; confirm the translated label is intended.

Verify on the canvas that activating the lasso tool with a shape selected clears the selection; before this release there was no lasso tool to activate, and confirm clearing the selection is intended.
Check the command palette in a non-English language and compare the unlock-all action with the old fixed English name “Unlock all elements”; confirm the translated label is intended.
Check the command palette in a non-English language and compare the statistics action with the old fixed English name “Toggle stats”; confirm the translated label is intended.
Check the command palette in a non-English language and compare the view-mode action with the old fixed English name “Toggle view mode”; confirm the translated label is intended.
Check the command palette in a non-English language and compare the zen-mode action with the old fixed English name “Toggle zen mode”; confirm the translated label is intended.
Verify on the canvas that a closed lasso loop around one shape selects it; before this release there was no lasso tool, and confirm this new selection behavior is intended.
Check on the canvas that a lasso path crossing a shape’s outline selects it without enclosing it; before this release there was no lasso selection, and confirm this new result is intended.
Verify that while holding Alt, dragging from a starting point creates a shape that remains anchored at that point rather than expanding from its center.

Verify the changed input by starting a selection-box drag and then holding Alt while continuing to drag; confirm a lasso path appears and shapes crossed or enclosed by it are selected, rather than continuing the original box selection.

Check the Shift case by starting the same Alt lasso gesture while holding Shift and tracing across another shape; confirm the previously selected shape remains selected along with the lasso-selected shape.
Confirm the Alt-release behavior by releasing Alt while still dragging after the lasso has started; confirm the gesture returns to box selection and completes as a box selection on pointer release.

Test cleanup by completing a lasso gesture and immediately starting another; confirm the previous trail is gone and the new gesture selects according to its own path, without stale trail or selection tracking.
Verify that restoring the drawing with lasso active keeps lasso active rather than falling back to selection.
Verify the toolbar offers a lasso tool and selecting it activates lasso mode; confirm the toolbar shows the lasso icon and the embed icon renders with its updated, thicker stroke.
Check that the command palette includes a lasso command and that choosing it activates lasso mode.
Confirm the changed keyboard behavior with the exact edge case: select a shape, activate lasso mode, then press and release Space; the shape should remain selected and the cursor should reset.
Verify that with lasso mode active and no selected elements, selected-shape actions are hidden.
Check that the empty-canvas hint is displayed without its final period when its translated text ends in a period.
Verify that activating the lasso while an element is selected clears the current selection and changes the active tool to lasso.
Check that drawing a closed path around one element, without touching the other, selects the enclosed element; then draw a path that crosses the other element and confirm it is selected too.
Confirm that activating the lasso action again while lasso is active returns to the selection tool and clears any current selection.
uncertainty: The previous lasso-selection implementation is not included in the supplied diff, so the prior expected selection rules for bound text and frame children cannot be confirmed.
The supplied context does not identify how to activate lasso selection retention or provide navigation steps, so the selection-retention check needs a confirmed way to reach that case.

The new line-intersection tolerance only changes results when a caller supplies it; the supplied in-app callers do not, and no integration surface or tolerance value was provided for a separate app-level check.
The supplied context does not include the translated text for the affected hints, so it is unclear whether either hint ends in a period in a usable language and visibly changes.

The lasso is a new capability, so the evidence provides no prior lasso behavior or old-handled input for a before-and-after regression comparison; it also does not show whether removing dedicated command-palette names changes action discovery, and no navigation for that surface was supplied.

report.summary: The release overhauls flowchart creation, editing, and keyboard navigation in the editor.
keyChanges: Flowchart creation and navigation are now handled through a dedicated keyboard workflow that creates nodes with Ctrl or Command plus an arrow key, commits on modifier release, and selects and reveals the resulting or navigated-to node when needed. The supplied before-and-after code does not show a changed shortcut mapping or a clear change in those outcomes.

Generated flowchart nodes are now positioned to avoid overlapping connected flowchart nodes, while keeping a multi-node cluster grouped around the starting node; this can move new nodes away from their former default positions.
Changing creation direction starts a fresh one-node cluster, and canceling creation clears the saved placement so a later flowchart starts fresh.
Directional flowchart navigation now finds linked nodes through elbow arrows and uses the arrow’s position relative to the selected node to determine direction.

New flowchart nodes are placed one 100-unit gap from their parent and shifted across the flowchart to avoid other nodes in the same connected flowchart, rather than using the previous placement based on direction-linked nodes.
When a pending cluster grows, its existing nodes are intended to keep their positions unless the larger cluster cannot fit there.
Flowchart state is now managed through a dedicated editor component; pending nodes continue to be supplied for rendering, so check that in-progress and completed flowcharts remain visible.
Undo and redo now check the flowchart manager’s in-progress status before applying history, preserving the guard during chart creation.
qaChecks: Verify pressing Ctrl or Command plus an arrow key on a selected flowchart node previews a new node, and releasing the modifier commits the node and selects it.
Check that Alt plus an arrow key on a selected connected node selects the node in that direction, and that a node outside the visible canvas area is brought into view.
Confirm pressing Escape while flowchart creation is in progress cancels the pending creation.

Verify on a flowchart that after exploring a connected node with Alt+Arrow and starting a preview with Ctrl/Command+Arrow, you release the modifiers in another tab and then release a key after returning; before this release both completions were captured separately, so confirm the new single capture and resulting undo history are intended.

Verify that after adding two nodes to the right and switching to create nodes above the same node beside existing linked nodes, the new preview starts in an available position rather than carrying over the previous alignment; before this release the new direction started a fresh preview, so confirm this result is intended.

Check that from a node with no link above but an unvisited elbow-linked node to the left, pressing Alt+Up reaches that left-hand node; before this release the alternate-link search did not reach it, so confirm the new result is intended.

Verify that navigating from a node whose elbow arrow attaches on its left edge, while the linked node sits to its right, now treats the link as leftward; before this release direction followed the linked node’s position, so confirm the new result is intended.

Confirm that pressing Alt+Right on a node with an incoming elbow arrow ending at its right edge can now navigate to its left-positioned predecessor; before this release the predecessor was found by its position to the left, so confirm the new result is intended.

Confirm that pressing Alt+Left on a node with an outgoing elbow arrow starting at its left edge can now navigate to its right-positioned successor; before this release the successor was found by its position to the right, so confirm the new result is intended.

Check that creating several nodes to the right beside an already occupied row places the new nodes clear of connected nodes; before this release the new row could overlap them, so confirm the new placement is intended.

Verify that adding a cluster near a node linked through a two-arrow elbow chain avoids the distant linked node in the proposed row; before this release that node was not accounted for, so confirm the new result is intended.

Check that adding a second node to the right while continuing the same creation sequence keeps the group’s previous alignment when there is room; before this release the growing group was recentered, so confirm the new result is intended.
Verify starting a flowchart without pressing an arrow key first, which placed the first node to the right before this release, and confirm that the new result with no preset direction is intended.

Check creating a flowchart by adding one pending node and then increasing the count, which used the old offset pattern before this release, and confirm that keeping the first node in place as the cluster grows is intended.

Confirm adding a node where an obstacle blocks its ideal position and free space exists on both sides, which used the old linked-node offset pattern before this release, now moves it to the nearest free position with ties toward the positive side.

Check adding a node when a node elsewhere in the same connected flowchart occupies its placement band, which was not considered unless directionally linked before this release, and confirm that the new cluster moves to avoid it.
Confirm placing a cluster whose edge exactly touches an occupied interval, which the old placement checks treated as blocked before this release, is now allowed to use that position.

Verify adding a cluster where two existing nodes' blocked regions touch with no gap between them, which the old offset pattern did not assess as one continuous area before this release, and confirm that the cluster avoids the combined region.
Verify Ctrl/Cmd+Right creates a connected node without overlapping the connected node occupying its default placement space.

Check repeated Ctrl/Cmd+Right presses before releasing the modifier produce a grouped cluster that avoids connected-node obstacles; then change direction and confirm creation starts a fresh one-node cluster in that direction.
Test creating nodes, pressing Escape to cancel, then starting creation from another node; confirm the new flowchart placement does not carry over the canceled cluster’s placement.

Confirm Alt+Arrow navigates to a connected node in the requested direction when linked by an elbow arrow, and that a link positioned in another direction is not treated as being in the requested direction.

Verify creating a node in the occupied direction places it one 100-unit gap from the parent, shifted to the nearest available cross-axis slot with clearance from the existing connected node, and connected to its parent.
Check that adding another node to a pending cluster keeps the already-visible pending nodes in place when the expanded cluster still fits.
Confirm keyboard navigation from a flowchart node with connected nodes still reaches the connected node in the requested direction.
Verify that pending flowchart nodes remain visible while keyboard-driven flowchart creation is in progress, and that completing the operation inserts the nodes and selects and reveals the first node.
Check that requesting undo or redo while flowchart creation is in progress does not apply the history update until the creation is no longer in progress.
uncertainty: The supplied before-and-after code does not identify a concrete input that the old flowchart keyboard handling accepted differently from the new handling, so a behavior regression specific to this change cannot be isolated.
The supplied evidence does not show the previous directional-navigation implementation, so the old-versus-new input difference for keyboard traversal cannot be determined.

The old behavior mapped an unrecognized key to the right direction, while the direction now starts unset; the replacement key handling is not shown, so the result of an unrelated key and the initial creation direction are unclear. The supplied evidence also does not show the replacement for the removed directional relationship lookup.

The supplied before-and-after code shows a relocation of flowchart state and a change in how its in-progress status is accessed, but identifies no concrete input that follows a different path before and after.

report.summary: The release improves text-to-diagram creation with coordinated chat generation, saved history, and more reliable Mermaid previews and controls.
keyChanges: Buttons now honor an explicit disabled setting as well as loading and success states, so the new-chat control is unavailable while diagram generation is in progress.
The text-to-diagram panels support chat history management, diagram preview insertion, and viewing generated content as Mermaid; chat retry becomes available 5 seconds after the recorded attempt.
Mermaid preview errors now use a clearer error presentation and hide the canvas; when error details are hidden, the message is a general syntax explanation instead of the raw error.
Workflow panels can show multiple action types together, including an action button, a link-style action, and rate-limit information; actions are disabled while text is being submitted.

Text-to-diagram chats are saved locally, titled from the first message, and capped at 10 saved chats; titles are trimmed and messages longer than 50 characters are shortened to 47 characters plus an ellipsis.
Text-to-diagram chat actions now create a fresh empty session, restore saved messages, and switch to the first remaining saved chat—or an empty session—when deleting the active chat.

Mermaid preview rendering now queues content during streaming, flushes pending content when generation ends, redraws the selected chat’s last assistant message, and clears the preview when the chat has no assistant messages.
Chat storage now saves the current chat when the last message is not generating; restored message timestamps are converted from serialized values to dates.
Text to diagram now sends conversation messages to a streaming service and assembles generated diagram text from streamed content.
Mermaid preview validation now rejects empty text, unmatched brackets, braces, or parentheses, and final lines ending in specified incomplete syntax.
An empty rate-limit remaining header now produces unavailable quota information instead of being interpreted as zero.
Mermaid previews no longer perform a canvas-to-blob size check, so very large diagrams may behave differently during preview and insertion.
Editor dialogs no longer carry the marker that prevented outside-click handling, and the command palette’s recent-command icon changes to a history-style symbol.
Text-to-diagram generation records prompts and assistant replies, streams generated Mermaid text, and parses it into drawing elements while using recent chat messages as context.
Generation handles aborted requests and parse or network errors in chat; a 429 response produces a rate-limit warning, or a message-limit warning when no requests remain.
Structured error messages are converted into readable message text when they have the expected nested JSON format; other formats remain unchanged.
No QA-visible behavior change can be confirmed from the supplied changes.

The text-to-diagram workflow now coordinates chat prompts, generated responses, retries, AI repair, message deletion, and diagram insertion; verify these actions against the correct chat turn and drawing content.

Mermaid conversion now renders and saves only while its view is active, clears the preview for blank input, and uses the current theme when rendering; verify stored diagrams appear when the view is opened and match the editor theme. The former always-rendered behavior is no longer used for inactive views.
qaChecks: Verify that while generation is in progress, the new-chat control and chat-history menu trigger are disabled and cannot start or open another chat.
Check that a saved chat can be restored or deleted, and that a generated diagram preview can be inserted into the drawing.
Confirm that when a network-error message is the latest chat message, retry is unavailable before 5 seconds have elapsed since its recorded attempt and becomes available after 5 seconds.
Verify a follow-up request that relies on a detail from the prior chat message produces a diagram reflecting the conversation.
Check a response with an empty X-Ratelimit-Remaining header and confirm it is not reported as zero solely because the header is empty.
Verify the full submitted text is 2, 3, 10,000, and 10,001 characters: 2 and 10,001 are rejected by length validation, while 3 and 10,000 pass that validation.
Check a 429 response with zero requests remaining: the pending assistant reply is removed and a message-limit warning appears; with a nonzero remaining value, a rate-limit warning appears.
Confirm aborting an in-progress generation does not show a network or parse error for the aborted request.
Validate an error message containing JSON with a nested message list, such as messages “first” and “second”: the chat error text displays those messages on separate lines.
Verify in the chat header that the New Chat button cannot be clicked while a response is generating; before this release it remained clickable, so confirm the new disabled behavior is intended.
Check the chat header while a response is generating and try to open saved-chat history; before this release the menu could be opened, so confirm it should now be unavailable.

Verify in the chat that reaching zero remaining requests disables the input and displays the rate-limit placeholder; before this release the input remained available, so confirm the new result is intended.
Check the chat input by typing two spaces before and after “diagram”; before this release the prompt did not preserve the exact typed text, so confirm the spaces should now remain visible.
Verify in the chat input that pressing Enter without Shift submits the prompt; before this release Enter did not submit it, so confirm this shortcut is intended.
Check the chat by submitting “  map  ”; before this release the surrounding spaces were sent, so confirm they should now be trimmed and the input cleared.
Verify in the chat input that pasting enough lines caps its height at 120 pixels; before this release it could grow beyond that height, so confirm the cap is intended.
Check the chat with a warning that has custom content; before this release the standard warning text appeared, so confirm it should now be replaced by the custom content.
Verify a chat message timestamp in a browser configured for a 24-hour clock; before this release it used the previous display format, so confirm the localized hour-and-minute display is intended.

Check the last network-failed chat message after a retry attempt and wait five seconds; before this release retry did not become available automatically at the end of the wait, so confirm it should now appear.
Verify in the chat panel that its history controls are unavailable while a response is generating; before this release they remained available, so confirm the new restriction is intended.
Check the chat panel when a rate-limit count is shown but no generated response is available; before this release the count was aligned at the end, so confirm it should now align at the start.

Verify the chat panel after generating a response when no rate-limit count is available; before this release a rate-limit indicator was shown, so confirm it should now be omitted while the Mermaid-view action appears.
Check the diagram preview panel for an Insert button; before this release the panel did not offer that action, so confirm it should now be available.

Verify the preview with error details hidden by entering a Mermaid diagram with a syntax error; before this release it showed “Error!” and the raw parser message, so confirm the localized title and generic message are intended.
Verify the preview after a loaded diagram produces a rendering error; before this release its canvas remained faintly visible behind the error, so confirm that hiding it completely is intended.
Verify the preview panel with no label or top-right content; before this release it included an empty header, so confirm that removing it is intended.

Verify a generated response and select “View as Mermaid”; before this release the panel had only its standard action button, so confirm that this separate link-style action and its result are intended.
Verify opening the chat panel in a browser profile with saved chat history; before this release the history was not restored, so confirm that the saved conversations now appear.

Verify a new chat whose first message has leading and trailing spaces and is longer than 50 characters; before this release this feature did not create a title from the message, so confirm the trimmed, shortened title is intended.

Verify opening chat history after its saved-chat data has been made invalid JSON; before this release the feature did not read this data, so confirm that showing an empty list without interrupting the panel is intended.
Verify saving a chat with browser storage unavailable or full; before this release the feature did not write chat history there, so confirm that a failed save only warns and leaves the panel usable.
Verify sending a non-empty message and waiting for its reply to finish; before this release the conversation was not automatically saved to chat history, so confirm that it now appears there.
Verify starting a new chat after exchanging messages; before this release the current conversation was not saved as part of starting a new one, so confirm that it now remains in chat history.

Verify deleting one conversation while other saved chats remain, then reopen chat history; before this release the feature did not persist chat deletions, so confirm the selected conversation stays removed.

Verify restoring a saved conversation while the current one has messages; before this release the active conversation was not saved first, so confirm that its messages remain in chat history after the switch.
Verify the text-to-diagram chat with saved conversations available and confirm the menu and chat actions behave as intended now; before this release, the dialog managed them itself.

Verify restoring a saved conversation with string timestamps and an error on its last assistant message; before this release the timestamps stayed strings and the error was not restored, and confirm the new result is intended.
Verify deleting the active conversation when it is the only saved one; before this release the current chat state was left in place, and confirm it now starts a fresh empty conversation.
Verify opening and dismissing the conversation menu; before this release this action did not explicitly close it, and confirm it now closes as intended.
Verify pressing the conversation-menu button twice; before this release the menu did not switch state on each press, and confirm it now opens then closes.
Verify choosing a new chat while the menu is open and an error is visible; before this release the menu and error were not both cleared, and confirm they now are.
Verify restoring a saved conversation from the open menu; before this release the menu stayed open, and confirm it now closes after the conversation is restored.

Verify starting a new chat with existing messages, a draft prompt, and a visible error; before this release those values were not all reset, and confirm the new empty conversation and cleared error are intended.
Verify switching to a saved conversation with an assistant diagram while preview is enabled; before this release its diagram was not rendered on switching, and confirm it now appears.
Verify generating a large, complex diagram that takes longer to render; before this release the next update used a fixed delay, and confirm it now uses a longer delay when rendering is slow.
Verify finishing generation while the latest diagram update is waiting for the throttle interval; before this release it was not explicitly flushed, and confirm the final update now appears.
Verify streaming a diagram that temporarily ends with “A -->”; before this release the incomplete text was sent to rendering and could show an error, and confirm it is now held until it is complete.
Verify completing one diagram and immediately generating another; before this release the second generation could inherit the first one's timing, and confirm it now starts with reset timing.
Verify sending a message and waiting for the assistant response to finish; before this release the conversation was not automatically saved on message changes, and confirm it is now saved.

Verify the text-to-diagram dialog when your account is rate-limited: before this release it showed “Too many requests today, please try again tomorrow!”, and now it reports “Rate limit exceeded”; confirm the new message is intended.

Verify the text-to-diagram dialog after generating a diagram and then editing the prompt: before this release the edit updated the prompt while retaining the previous generated response; confirm the new edit behavior is intended.

Verify the text-to-diagram dialog with a prompt whose response takes several seconds: before this release the diagram was handled after the complete response arrived, and now it can appear progressively; confirm the streamed result is intended.

Verify text-to-diagram generation when the service returns HTTP 500 with the body “Service unavailable”: before this release the dialog showed “Request failed,” and now it can show the response text; confirm this change is intended.

Verify text-to-diagram generation when the service supplies an empty remaining-limit header: before this release it was treated as zero and blocked another generation, and now it is treated as missing; confirm that is intended.

Verify text-to-diagram generation when the service ends its stream immediately after the final data line without a trailing newline: before this release a complete response was returned, and now the final content may be lost; confirm the new result is intended.

Verify the live diagram preview while a response temporarily ends with “A -->”: before this release it attempted to render that partial text, and now it waits for more content; confirm the delayed preview is intended.
Verify the recent-command entry in the command palette after using a command; it showed a clock icon before this release and now shows a history-and-bolt icon, and confirm the new icon is intended.

Check the underlying popup or menu while clicking inside a dialog opened over it; that click was marked as protected before this release, and confirm that dismissing the underlying popup or menu now is intended.

Verify a very large generated diagram in the text-to-diagram dialog; before this release a failed preview-image conversion produced an oversized-canvas error, and confirm that the new result without that check is intended.

Confirm the code-font option in the font-family controls: it showed the older, smaller code symbol before this release and now shows the replacement symbol, and verify that this visual change is intended.

Verify the production app with a 2.1 MiB asset, then open it offline; before this release an asset that size exceeded the default cache limit, so confirm that caching it for offline use now is intended.

Verify that a conversation remains visible after switching away from and reopening the text-to-diagram dialog; before this release it was not managed through this shared chat history, so confirm that using shared history now is intended.

Verify the text-to-diagram dialog by submitting “Draw a blue circle.”; before this release the prompt was not added to chat history as a user message, so confirm that showing it in the conversation now is intended.

Verify the text-to-diagram dialog by submitting a valid prompt and checking the conversation before the response finishes; before this release no generating assistant message was added to this history, so confirm that the in-progress message now is intended.

Verify the text-to-diagram dialog by retrying a failed response; before this release the retry action did not record a retry time on the assistant message, so confirm that recording it now is intended.

Verify the text-to-diagram dialog by causing a network failure during generation; before this release the assistant error was not recorded with this generating-state and error-type update, so confirm that ending generation and recording the error now is intended.

Verify the text-to-diagram dialog by submitting a second valid prompt before the first response finishes; before this release generation was not coordinated through this shared chat and request state, so confirm that the first request being aborted now is intended.

Verify the text-to-diagram dialog with a service error containing the nested JSON messages “First issue” and “Second issue”; before this release the error appeared as raw JSON, so confirm that showing the two messages on separate lines now is intended.
Verify the text-to-diagram dialog by stopping a response while it is streaming; before this release this handler did not abort the active request, so confirm that stopping it now is intended.

Verify the text-to-diagram dialog with a prompt that produces invalid Mermaid content; before this release the failure was not classified and recorded here as a parse error, so confirm that recording it as a parse error now is intended.

Verify the text-to-diagram dialog after at least four prior conversation messages by submitting another prompt; before this release the request included the full prior conversation, so confirm that sending only the last three prior messages now is intended.

Verify the text-to-diagram dialog by submitting a 20-character prompt when the remaining message allowance is 0; before this release that valid-length prompt was not blocked by this check, so confirm that refusing to send it now is intended.

Verify in Safari 14 that retrying an assistant response which needs to be removed worked before this release but can now leave the response in the chat, and confirm this compatibility change is intended.

Verify opening the dialog on the Text to Diagram tab with a Mermaid definition already saved did not render it before this release and now leaves it unrendered, and confirm that inactive-tab behavior is intended.
Verify rendering a valid diagram in dark mode produced a light-mode preview before this release and now produces a dark-mode preview, and confirm the change is intended.
Verify opening the dialog on a desktop showed a 1200-pixel-wide dialog before this release and now shows a wider dialog, and confirm the new size is intended.
Verify opening Text to Diagram with preview mode off showed a preview panel before this release and now hides it, and confirm that result is intended.
Verify choosing AI repair for an invalid diagram with an error had no repair action before this release and now sends a repair request, and confirm that result is intended.
Verify deleting the first assistant reply in a two-turn chat was not available before this release and now removes that turn and everything after it, and confirm that amount of deletion is intended.

report.summary: The release makes drawing edits and canvas previews more consistent and reliable.
keyChanges: Overlapping-element hit testing and arrow binding now continue past opaque objects whose type does not support a fill, which can change which object is selected or connected.

Frame highlighting now supports rectangles, diamonds, ellipses, arrows, lines, freehand drawings, text, images, frames, and embeddable content, and clears when selection is dismissed or drawing is finished.
Older browsers missing newer array operations now receive fallback behavior so the editor can continue to operate.
A single frame-linked element is now inserted at the end of the drawing rather than immediately before its frame, which may change its visual stacking among overlapping elements.

When adding a mixed selection to a frame, elements already in that frame are now included in the reorder with newly added elements; dragging toward a frame also previews the selection in frame order before release.

Bulk additions use the frame’s last child as the insertion point when available, while an explicit null insertion position means the end of the drawing. Frame resizing and replacing frame contents use the updated membership and ordering behavior.
When a frame-containing library item is inserted or dropped, its original element order is preserved, so verify that its frame contents remain associated and appear in the intended order.

Frame hit-testing now considers the object above the insertion point and, during dragging, excludes selected objects; text creation also gives a text container priority over a different overlapping frame.
Creating objects inside a frame now updates its highlight, and switching tools clears any existing frame highlight.

New elements assigned to a frame are inserted with that frame’s children instead of simply being appended after all scene elements, affecting pasted text, images, embeddable items, and other insertions.
Pasting or dropping frame-containing drawings now requests preservation of their frame-child order, so copied or Library content should retain its intended stacking order.
Pointer movement now updates frame highlighting when an eligible drawing tool is active, and rendering uses element, selection, drag, and highlight state to decide how in-progress elements appear.

The drawing canvases now use a canvas-specific change marker, rather than the scene marker, to decide when to refresh; the visible result should stay current as the drawing or interactive feedback changes.
Single- and multi-element size edits still update resized elements and refresh frame membership at the end of a resize; the supplied changes do not establish a user-visible difference from before.

When selected elements from outside a frame are dragged over it, their rendered order is previewed among that frame’s contents before the drop; dragging elements already in the target frame does not trigger this reorder.
Rendering now uses a frame-aware draft element and refreshes its cached result when that in-frame draft’s version changes, so verify its preview updates as it changes.
Newly drawn objects, embedded frames, generated frames, and completed flowchart nodes now use shared insertion handling; objects associated with a frame also trigger frame-highlight handling.

When a selection is dropped to update frame contents, the candidate frame is chosen using the selection’s common current frame and excludes selected objects; objects already assigned to the target frame are no longer filtered out beforehand.
Adding a Library item now preserves the order of objects inside its frames.

report.summary: The release updates server startup and data handling, with related validation and command-line changes.
keyChanges: When the configured database path ends in .json and the file is missing, startup now creates it with default data before loading it; verify this using a missing JSON database path.

Editing the configured routes file now restarts the server, whereas previously it only logged the change; router setup errors are now printed before the process exits instead of propagating directly. Other changes preserve existing behavior.
File watching now uses the platform’s native watcher, so filename reporting and notifications may differ from the previous watcher.
Collection filters now skip records when the filtered field is falsy, so records with values such as false or 0 may no longer match queries that previously found them.

Filter operators are recognized only when their suffix is at the end of a query key; ordinary field names containing strings such as “_ne” now use exact matching instead of the previous not-equal interpretation.

Create and update now pass request-body values through unchanged, while item lookup, update, and deletion no longer convert ID strings before matching; embedded and expanded resource handling otherwise has no behavior change evident in the supplied diff.

The default middleware stack no longer includes request-body parsing or method overriding, while the database router now installs both; requests through the router retain these capabilities, but requests through the default stack alone do not.

When adding a record to a nonempty collection whose highest ID is nonnumeric, the server now generates the string ID with a different generator; empty collections still start at 1 and numeric IDs still increment.
Database data is now validated when the router starts; the exact invalid-data cases are not specified. Other edits to database searching and relationship checks do not change their runtime logic.
Nested GET and POST requests now keep the parent ID as text instead of converting values such as "1" to a number or "true" to a boolean, which may affect how linked records are matched.
Database data validation now rejects top-level values that are not plain objects and properties whose names contain a slash.
The previous JSON-filename recognition helper was removed; no affected application surface or caller is identified.

A new command-line entry point invokes the existing CLI setup, so QA should confirm it reaches argument handling when launched with a source; changing variable declarations and property shorthand does not alter behavior.
